articleTitle: Invited talk 3: Design of chassis MIMO antenna using characteristic mode theory
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Provides an abstract of the invited presentation and may include a brief professional biography of the presenter. The complete presentation was not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: MM-wave phased array antenna for whole-metal-covered 5G mobile phone applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel mm-wave phased array antenna for whole metal covered 5G mobile handset is proposed. The proposed array antenna consists of eight rotated slot antenna elements that are arranged on the upper frame of the metal-body. The proposed array demonstrates good S-parameter characteristics in frequency band ranging from 27.1 to 28.6 GHz and mutual-coupling between antenna elements is less than -19 dB. The proposed array antenna has the hemi-spherical beam coverage suitable for 5G mobile communication.

articleTitle: Dipole antenna with sheath-cover for seawater use
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To design antennas for underwater communication systems using LF band, the transmission factor of dipole antennas with the sheath immersed in seawater are investigated by numerical study. Comparison of antenna characteristics between dipole antennas with different sheath structure is presented.

articleTitle: Series feeding rectangular microstrip patch array antenna for 77 GHz automotive radar
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a 1×10 series feeding rectangular microstrip patch array antenna for 77 GHz automotive radar. The proposed antenna is designed based on the transmission line model analysis method. To satisfy the sidelobe level of −20 dB in E-plane, 20 dB Taylor distribution is applied to the proposed antenna. Considering the measurement environment, waveguide to microstrip transition is designed and combined with the antenna. To evaluate the antenna performance, a prototype of the proposed antenna is fabricated and tested. The measured −10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth is 3.8% (75.04–77.95 GHz). The measured broadside gain and sidelobe level in E-plane at 76.5 GHz are 16.56 dBi and −17.2 dB. The simulated and measured results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: LP and CP polarization reconfigurable antennas for modern wireless applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper will present a series of novel polarization reconfigurable antennas for modern wireless applications. First, three multi-linear polarization reconfigurable antennas with the switchable 0°, +45°, 90° and -45° polarizations are investigated for mitigating the polarization mismatching problem in wireless biomedical applications. Three distinctive techniques were adopted to realize the same reconfigurability but with different radiation performance. In the beginning, a multi-dipole structure was designed. Four switchable half-wavelength dipoles were arranged in a compact structure and fed by a same source. Later, we used the slot antenna as the basic radiating element to realize the same polarization reconfigurability but with the improved directivity. Furthermore, to reduce the profile of the previously proposed two designs, a multiple L-probes fed circular patch antenna was designed. The profile was significantly decreased but the gain was improved. Second, three circular polarization reconfigurable antennas are introduced for increasing the channel capacity in satellite applications. Initially, a wideband CP reconfigurable antenna with conical-beam pattern was realized at the first time. Later on, two wideband broadside CP reconfigurable antennas were designed. The achieved bandwidth of our proposed antennas are widest among all the previously reported works.

articleTitle: Gain enhancement of millimeter wave antenna with metamaterial loading
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper a dipole antenna is loaded with C-shaped metamaterial unit cell array. This array of metamaterial unit cells acts as a dielectric lens to focus the E-filed radiated from the dipole antenna in a particular direction. The effect of loading metamaterial layer on the dipole is studied, a gain enhancement of 5dB is observed. The predicted results were verified through measurements and it is observed the antenna has a return loss of -10dB in the 26-30 GHz frequency band. The radiation properties in the E-plane is also measured, the antenna has a measured peak gain of 11dBi when loaded with the metamaterial. This compact antenna is a suitable candidate for compact planar handheld devices.

articleTitle: Configuration of an X-band FMCW radar targeted for drone detection
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses the detection of drone with Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave (FMCW) Radar system. The system employs 11GHz to 11.15GHz frequency bandwidth to generate sawtooth linear wave through bistatic antennas with the gain of 33.7dBi, and the output transmitter power is 35dBm. Metal baffles were placed between and each side of the antennas to minimize the direct path interference. The system also includes digital down converter to obtain IQ signal with minimum mismatch. In the actual performance measurement, the drone signal was detected up to more than 500m distance in real-time with the error of less than 0.1%. The data has been saved as bin file and then later processed with MATLAB.

articleTitle: 28/38GHz dual band slotted patch antenna with proximity-coupled feed for 5G communication
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a slotted-rectangular patch antenna with proximity-coupled feed operated at dual band of millimeter-wave (mmV) frequencies, 28GHz and 38GHz. The antenna was built in multilayer substrate construct by 10-layers Low temperature Co-fiber Ceramic (LTCC) with 5 mils thickness each. The slotted-patch and thick substrate are configured to enhance the bandwidth and obtain a good result in gain as well. The bandwidth using are 21.3% at 28GHz and 13.0% at 38GHz with the direction gains are 8.63dBi and 8.62dBi at 28GHz and 38GHz respectively.

articleTitle: A polarization reconfigurable textile patch antenna for wearable IoT applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A polarization reconfigurable textile patch antenna for wearable internet of things (IoT) applications is suggested. PIN diodes were applied on the truncations of the suggested patch antenna in order to provide three reconfigurable polarizations. The antenna covers 2.4-GHz industrial, scientific and medical (ISM) band and has an average gain of 5.96 dBi among three polarizations. For practical integration with wearable garments, all elements of the antenna are constructed with fabric materials. Furthermore, overall performance of the antenna is analyzed on body-mimicking phantom for realizing a wearable environment.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband millimeter-wave bowtie antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We present an ultra-wideband antenna for mm-wave applications. The antenna consists of a bowtie patch integrated with the feeding network. The feeding network is implemented as a multilayer substrate structure. The differential excitation of the bowtie is performed in a similar way to Magneto-Electric Dipoles and Marchand baluns. The simulated antenna shows a relative bandwidth of 2.6 : 1 with a reflection coefficient better than -8 dB. The radiation pattern remains fairly stable over 20-50 GHz with a boresight directivity of 5.8-8.3 dBi.

articleTitle: A negative index metamaterial lens for antenna gain enhancement
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a transmission type negative refractive index metamaterial surface acting as a planer surface lens is presented. A measured 3 dB transmission band of 2 GHz from 8.55 GHz to 10.55 GHz is obtained. Material property of the proposed meta-surface is extracted by using free space technique. The designed meta-surface is radiation beam conversing in nature. Aperture efficiency of the designed meta-surface is 84.30 %. A high gain antenna is designed by placing the proposed double stacked meta-surface lens over a micostrip patch antenna operating at 10.06 GHz. A gain enhancement of 8.55 dB in H-Plane and 6.20 dB in E-Plane at resonating frequency 10 GHz is obtained. The cross polarization level is improved by 8 dB.

articleTitle: Investigation of a Ka-band Luneburg lens made of a glide-symmetric holey structure
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A Ka-band 2D flat-profiled Luneburg lens antenna implemented with a glide-symmetric holey structure is presented. The required refractive index for the lens design has been investigated via an analysis of the hole depth and the gap between the two metallic layers constituting the lens. The final unit cell is described and applied to create the complete metasurface Luneburg lens showing that a plane wave is obtained when feeding at an opposite arbitrary point with a discrete source.

articleTitle: An analysis of signal environment on 1030/1090MHz aeronautical L-band systems
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The operational performance of 1030/1090MHz aeronautical radio system is required to be estimated whether or not they will interfere harmfully with each other by sharing the frequency band. The performance of these systems will be estimated with some interference measures such as the received pulse densities. This paper provides the results of an analysis of 1090MHz signal environment which recorded by the flight experiments.

articleTitle: Metasurface-backed monopole printed antenna with enhanced bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the bandwidth enhancement of monopole printed antenna backed with metasurface is presented. The proposed antenna which is intended to work at frequency of 2.3MHz consists of a rectangular patch on the top side and a metasurface on the other side. It is designed on an FR4 Epoxy dielectric substrate with the thickness of 0.8mm. To demonstrate the feature of bandwidth enhancement, a conventional patch antenna works at the same resonant frequency is implemented on the same dielectric substrate as comparison. From the characterization, it shows that the −10dB working bandwidth of proposed antenna achieves 630MHz where this is 6 times larger than the conventional patch antenna which has the −10dB working bandwidth of 100MHz.

articleTitle: Microstrip antenna with CSRR ground structure
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel multi-band single feed microstrip antenna with metamaterial structure that satisfies WiMAX and WLAN applications is proposed in this paper. The conventional antenna consists of a rectangular microstrip patch at a frequency band of (4.9752 ∼ 5.1777) 5.08 GHz. By loading a complementary Split Ring Resonator (CSRR) at the ground plane, three frequency bands: 2.5113 ∼ 2.609, 2.9026 ∼ 3.2056, and 5.5406 ∼ 5.8773 are achieved. The operational bands covered by the antenna are WiMAX 2.5 GHz and WLAN 5.2/5.8 GHz. The application of CSRR to patch antenna has made it possible to design simple, compact, and miniaturized metamaterial antenna for wireless communication systems.

Author Keywords: triple band and multi band frequency

articleTitle: An E-band antenna-diplexer compact integrated solution based on gap waveguide technology
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel compact integrated antenna-diplexer for Frequency-division duplex low latency wireless backhaul links at E-band is presented. The proposed solution is designed in a multilayer architecture with each layer having different functional blocks. The layers have been stacked on top of each other without any electrical contact requirement between them. This is achieved by using packaging property of gap waveguide technology. A corporate-fed 16 × 16 slot array antenna is integrated with a 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order diplexer. The simulated reflection coefficients are better than −13 dB for both input ports in the designed passbands. The simulated realized gains at the middle of channel 1 (73.5 GHz) and channel 2 (83.5 GHz) are respectively 31.8 dBi and 32.9 dBi, obtaining a high isolation of 50 dB between the two input ports.

articleTitle: Wideband RCS reduction of vivaldi antenna using electromagnetic band gap absorbing structure
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this letter, a Vivaldi antenna with wideband RCS reduction using Electromagnetic Band Gap Absorbing Structure (EBGAS) is designed. The EBGAS coveres on the antenna ground. The EBGAS constructed by split rectangular ring loaded with resistors and dielectric spacer. Compared with the metal ground Vivaldi antenna, RCS has reduced about 15 dB in the frequency band of 4–18 GHz and almost without gain loss. This antenna has wideband scanning ability, can be used for phased array antenna stealth design.

articleTitle: Gain enhancement of microstrip patch antenna using I-shaped Mushroom-like EBG structure for WLAN application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper present the microstrip patch antenna with I-shaped mushroom like EBG structure for gain enhancement. By properly placing the electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structure around radiating patch, the gain of a conventional microstrip patch antenna is improved. In order to achieve the EBG operation for wireless local area network of U-NII 1 and 2 bands, the EBG structure is formed by using the I-shaped resonator. The radiation pattern results indicate that the gain of the proposed antenna is improved of around 2 dBi at the operating frequency of 5.2 GHz. Moreover, the suppression of side- and back-lobe radiation is achieved by the presence of EBG structure.

articleTitle: Electro-textile glove-tags for wearable RFID applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We present passive UHF RFID electro-textile tags integrated into two types of gloves for wearable RFID applications. The performance of the electro-textile glove-tags is evaluated on a male test subject and the results are compared to glove-tags with copper tape antennas. Based on the achieved results, the read ranges of the electro-textile tags are very close to those of the copper tape tags and tags on both types of gloves show attainable read ranges of 2.5-3 meters, when measured near the human body.

articleTitle: A compound reconfigurable microstrip antenna with agile polarizations and steerable beams
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Achieving both polarization switching and beam steering independently, in a compact antenna structure, is a major challenge for compound reconfigurable antennas. In this paper, a new cavity-backed proximity-coupled reconfigurable microstrip antenna provides an efficient solution. Three different linear polarizations (0°, 45°, 90°) can be obtained by switching PIN diodes on a proximity-coupled feed network. For each polarization state, the main beam can be steered in three directions by using a reconfigurable parasitic-element network. The antenna has nine different working states in total. For all states, the measured input reflection coefficients are below -10 dB, with the measured realized gains ranging from 7.2-8 dBi.

articleTitle: 3D-printed graphene and stretchable antennas for wearable RFID applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study presents the potentials of 3D printing in the utilization of passive RFID components on a cotton substrate. New types of 3D-printable conductive materials, graphene ink and stretchable silver conductor, are used in antenna fabrication. Our measurement results confirm that both types of wireless components reach high performance: the achievable read ranges of the graphene and stretchable tags are close to 5 and 11 meters, respectively. These results are well comparable to those of previously reported silver and copper textile RFID tags.

articleTitle: A frequency-tunable varactor-loaded single-layer ring microstrip antennas fed by an L-probe with a reduced bias circuit
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents design of a varactor-loaded frequency-tunable ring microstrip antenna with reduced bias circuits. Two varactor diodes are mounted on square ring patch element fed by an L-probe to realize a frequency-tunable microstrip antenna. An L-shaped feeding probe is used to realize impedance matching of the ring microstrip antenna. Resonant frequency of the proposed antenna can be tuned electronically by a DC bias voltage applied to the varactor diodes. In order to develop a frequency-tunable multiband microstrip antenna with multiple ring patch elements, reduction of the bias circuits is an important issue. In this paper, one of the bias circuits for negative bias port of the frequency-tunable ring microstrip antenna is removed by using a via hole connecting the ring patch and the ground plane at the zero-voltage plane. Fractional bandwidth of the frequency-tunable range of the proposed antenna with the reduced bias circuit is measured to be around 10% under the condition of over 3 dBi gain and the reflection characteristics less than -10 dB.

articleTitle: An experimental study on OAM mode-multiplexing with dielectric lens fed by uniform circular array
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The feasibility of a high capacity radio link employing Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) mode-multiplexing is discussed in this paper. Experiments are conducted with the supports of Software Defined Radio (SDR) based system for signal processing, A/D and D/A conversions, modulation and demodulation (MODEM), and dielectric lens fed by Uniform Circular Array (UCA) for OAM signals transmission and reception. We confirm the successful transmission of 14 different 16-QAM data streams corresponding to 7 OAM modes (0, ±1, ±2, ±3) in combination with 2 polarizations (±45deg) over a 0.5m link at 5.1GHz, which results in a high spectral efficiency of 56bps/Hz.

articleTitle: An automotive stacked ceramic patch antenna with an integrated GNSS and SDARS antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper propose a stacked ceramic patch antenna that is composed with two ceramic patch antenna for Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) and Satellite Digital Audio Radio Service (SDARS). The proposed antenna stacks up GNSS antenna on SDARS antenna to reduce the antenna volume without degradation of antenna performances. The proposed antenna covers all of the required gain at the entire azimuth range. The overall volume of proposed antenna is 36×36×9 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The antenna with high performance and minimized structure is a highly marketable product.

articleTitle: 3D inkjet printed flexible and wearable antenna systems
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: With the advent of wearable sensors and internet of things (IoT), there is a new focus on electronics which can be bent so that they can be worn or mounted on non-planar objects. Moreover, there is a requirement that these electronics become extremely low cost, to the extent that they become disposable. The flexible and low cost aspects can be addressed by adapting additive manufacturing technologies such as inkjet printing and 3D printing. This paper presents inkjet printing as an emerging new technique to realize low cost, flexible and wearable antenna systems. The ability of inkjet printing to realize electronics on unconventional mediums such as plastics, papers, and textiles has opened up a plethora of new applications. A variety of antennas such as wide-band, multiband, and wearable, etc, which have been realized through additive manufacturing techniques are shown. Many system level examples are also shown, primarily for wireless sensing applications. The promising results of these designs indicate that the day when electronics can be printed like newspapers and magazines through roll-to-roll and reel-to-reel printing is not far away.

articleTitle: A down-conversion method for attenuation of leakage signal in FMCW radar
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a new down-conversion method to attenuate leakage signal in frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar. The proposed method reduces the effect of phase noise in the leakage signal. It can be simply realized through digital signal processing without additional hardware. Specifications of practical FMCW radar and the phase noise which is bad enough were assumed and simulations in these conditions were performed. Power spectral density (PSD) results show that while a target signal is buried by the phase noise tail of the leakage signal, the proposed method detects the target signal by attenuating the tail.

articleTitle: A miniaturized wideband dual-polarized antenna for base-station applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized wideband dual-polarized antenna loaded with parasitic loops and straight dipoles has been proposed for 2G/3G/4G base-station applications. Firstly, by loading four parasitic loops to the corners of regular crossed loop dipoles, a miniaturized structure and enhanced impedance bandwidth can be obtained. Then, based on the miniaturized structure, two straight dipoles are inserted into the gap of crossed loop dipoles, and a further widened impedance bandwidth is realized. Measurement shows that the antenna achieves an wide impedance bandwidth of 49.6% with SWR<;1.5 (1.7 to 2.83 GHz) and a high isolation of greater than 28 dB within the bandwidth. Also, a stable radiation pattern with half-power beamwidth of 66.1±3.4° at horizontal plane and a stable gain of 8.5±0.5 dBi are obtained simultaneously over the working frequency band.

articleTitle: A hand gesture recognition system based on 24GHz radars
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presented a gesture recognition system for human-computer interaction based on 24GHz radars. We describe this system designed for frequently used gesture detection like hand pushing, hand pulling, hand lifting and hand shaking. Decision tree was established to classify these original signals into the four sets of gestures. Through a set of tests on this gesture-recognition system, we proposed that this system could achieve an overall accuracy rate higher than 92%.

articleTitle: Compact circularly polarized S-band antenna for pico-satellites
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact square-shaped circularly polarized antenna is presented for pico-satellite application. Four dipole antennas are integrated with a phase delay line on a Rogers RO4003C to operate at 2.4 GHz with a dimension of 0.724λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> (55mm) × 0.724λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> (55mm) × 0.0112λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> (0.85mm) based on the lowest guided wavelength. Reflection and radiation performance exhibited are acceptable, with an impedance bandwidth and axial ratio bandwidth of 34 % and 11 % respectively. The proposed antenna operates in circular polarization with a maximum gain of 3.49 dB towards the forward direction.

articleTitle: An ultra-thin wide-angle cross polarization conversion metasurface with enhanced bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this article, a bandwidth-enhanced metasurface has been designed using single circular split ring as unit cell on the top surface of a metal backed FR4 substrate. The structure behaves as cross polarization conversion (CPC) metasurface over full width at half maxima (FWHM) bandwidth of 12.94 GHz ranging from 9.44 GHz to 22.38 GHz. The proposed CPC metasurface maintains bandwidth enhancement upto 45° incident angles under both TE and TM polarizations. The structure is ultra-thin (~ λ/11.4 with respect to the centre frequency) in nature.

articleTitle: Integration of very-low-profile slot antenna into notebook metal cover with narrow bezel
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An integrated slot antenna with a very low profile of 4 mm to the top edge of the notebook metal cover for WLAN operation is proposed. The antenna was integrated in the top cover and fed by soldering the cable across the slot. The antenna design consisted of two parallel-connected slot portions with the dimensions 80 mm and 2 mm. The larger slot portion contributed to both half- and the one-wavelength modes for operation in the 2.4 and 5.2 GHz bands with one matching inductor incorporated to attain good input impedance. The frequency ratio of these two modes can be controlled by adjusting the tuning portion in the larger slot. In addition, the 5.8-GHz resonance was generated by the smaller slot portion, making it possible for the very-low-profile slot antenna to obtain tri-WLAN-band operation.

articleTitle: Power control unit for E-class power oscillator of 6.78 MHz wireless power transfer
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a power control unit for e-class power oscillator of 6.78 MHz wireless power transfer (WPT). Generally, the E-class switching mode power amplifier is a very efficient amplifier. It is suitable for high frequency amplifier. The output power is related to a DC power supply voltage and load resistance. Thus, it is shown that the output power can be controlled by changing DC power supply voltage value. In this case, the output power is controlled by using a microcontroller together with a variable voltage regulator circuit. The proposed power control unit for E-class power oscillator of 6.78 MHz wireless power transfer is worked very well. The controlled power levels are 5, 10, 15, 20 and 45W at 50 Ohms load.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of MU-MIMO THP with user scheduling in terms of system capacity and fairness
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the performance evaluation of multi-user MIMO (MU-MIMO) employing Tomlinson Harashima precoding (THP) in consideration of user scheduling techniques from the viewpoint of system capacity and fairness. In this paper, the ordering process is adopted for THP, and both semiorthogonal user selection (SUS) and proportional fairness (PF) are considered as user scheduling techniques. Their opposite characteristics make it possible to establish the degree of matching between precoding and user scheduling techniques. The system-level performance with unequal CNR users is evaluated through computer simulations, and it is compared with the performance of linear precoding (LP).

articleTitle: A miniaturized antipodal vivaldi antenna for microwave imaging
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A miniaturized antipodal Vivaldi antenna (AVA) with bandwidth of 1-5GHz is proposed in this letter. The miniaturization of this end-fire directional antenna was realized by employing elliptically shaped conductors with two pairs of elliptically opened slots on them and one pair of symmetrically loaded structures. Additional reflection structures was designed to ensure the antenna's directivity at low frequency part within the bandwidth. The antenna was fabricated and measured through experiment, agreeing well with that of computer CST® simulations. The designed antenna can be applied to medical microwave imaging system.

articleTitle: Toward wide-band low-loss gap-waveguide-integrated grid amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A passive W-band 19-channel spatial power splitter/combiner is presented, for the applications in grid amplifiers design. The design employs a linear array of chip-to-air-filled waveguide contactless connections, and are directly integrated within a single-layer. The meta-material-based gap waveguide is used; it enables a low-loss low-profile solution. The quasi-optical beamformer gives rise to a parallel-plate planar waveguide field which excites an array of contactless chip-to-waveguide transitions via step-tapered ridge gap waveguides. The other beamformer restores the field distribution (after amplification) and excites a wave going towards the waveguide output. Furthermore, the gap waveguide technology isolates the amplifiers from one another and provides a packaging solution in a single unit. The simulated return loss of the back-to-back structure is larger than 12 dB, while the insertion loss is smaller than 1.2 dB over the entire W-band (75-110 GHz).

articleTitle: Hyperthermia performance of conformal applicator for limb tumor in presence of water bolus
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper examines the influence of water bolus coupling layer on the specific absorption rate and temperature distributions respectively in the tissue during hyperthermia treatment of human limb tumor using a previously reported microstrip slot antenna integrated with a compact artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) reflector at 2.45 GHz. The simulation study reveals the effectiveness of the antenna-AMC combination for hyperthermia treatment of arm and thigh tumors. Further, the results indicate that during treatment, hotspot in the skin can be reduced by optimizing water bolus temperature.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized single-fed wide-slot antenna for UHF RFID reader
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a design of the universal reader antenna applied for the radio frequency identification (RFID) system with the operating frequency from 840 MHz to 960 MHz. The antenna structure consists of a rectangular loop and a rectangular feeding patch which are the important elements to produce the circular polarization. The total size of the reader antenna is 120 mm ×120 mm fabricated on the FR4 substrate with thickness of 3.18 mm and with the dielectric constant of 4.3. From the measured results, it is obvious that the proposed reader antenna radiates a bidirectional pattern with the circular polarization, covering the operating frequency from 750 MHz to 1150 MHz with axial ratio bandwidth of 42%. The axial ratio and gain at the boresight direction are 1.03 dB and 3.62 dBic, considering at 900 MHz which the center frequency band of universal RFID standard.

articleTitle: A frequency reconfigurable slot dipole antenna using surface PIN diodes
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose a frequency reconfigurable slot dipole antenna mounted with surface PIN (S-PIN) diodes. Instead of using conventional chip-packaged PIN diodes, a plasma channels induced on the S-PIN diodes with high carrier concentrations are used to electrically change effective lengths of the slots. Thus, by turning on and off the S-PIN diodes, we can make our antenna operate in three different frequency bands. Reasonably high realized gain near at each resonant frequency confirms that the plasma channel well mimics a desired metallic property rather than absorbing RF signals. In addition, we can also estimate appropriate conductivity of the proposed S-PIN diodes by parametric study of simulations, which was not clear in conventional researches.

articleTitle: Diffuse scattering prediction for 26GHz band in indoor office environments
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the accuracy of a diffuse scattering prediction method with an effective roughness model by using detailed structural data in the form of a point cloud for high frequency band in indoor office environments. It also presents the effect of diffuse scattering on propagation characteristics. We compared measurement and prediction results in the 26 GHz band. In so doing we clarified that almost the same accuracy prediction results were obtained as those for measured delay spread with the RMSE value 0.4 ns. We also confirmed that multiple bounce specular reflection waves obtained on the basis of rough surface are dominant because their total received power is larger by about 10 dB than those of diffuse scattering waves in the 26 GHz band in indoor office environments.

articleTitle: A high isolation dual-band MIMO antenna for WLAN application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-band planar slot antenna is proposed for multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) array conformation, which achieves the 2.4GHz and 5.8GHz bands for wireless local area network (WLAN) application. The isolation between two antenna elements in the operating frequency bands is greater than 20dB by employing the decoupling slots structure. The envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) in the operation bands is less than 0.01, which shows that it has excellent performance in MIMO system.

articleTitle: A multilayer-stacked UWB Yagi antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: By taking advantage of a wideband bow-tie antenna in the Yagi configuration, a novel multilayer-stacked ultra-wideband (UWB) Yagi antenna is proposed. First, the fundamental 3-layered UWB Yagi model is studied with respect to a few critical dimensions. Then, several directors are added to form a multilayer-stacked Yagi antenna, where the width of the directors is optimized in a monotonic decreasing manner. A six-layered UWB Yagi antenna is studied by simulations. It covers 3.4–10.6 GHz with its return loss better than 10 dB, and it achieves a high directivity up to 13 dBi and a relative cross-polar level better than −10 dB in the whole band.

articleTitle: A flower-shaped stub slot antenna with dual band-notched characteristics for UWB applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A flower-shaped stub slot antenna with dual band-notched for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna can cover UWB spectrum with dual band-notched characteristics. The two notched bands are designed by using the parasitic square C-shaped Strip and the ellipse C-shaped slot, which can reject the frequency band of 3.2 to 3.7 GHz and 5.13 to 5.9 GHz. Furthermore, the proposed antenna has small size with dimensions of 16 × 24 × 0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Therefore, this antenna is another candidate that is suitable for applying to UWB technology.

articleTitle: Path-loss prediction considering human-body shadowing of multi-path components in crowded area at 4.7 and 26.4 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the measurement and simulation results in a crowded area from our previously proposed path-loss prediction method. The root-mean-square (RMS) error between the simulation and measurement results was less than 4 dB, confirming that our method can accurately predict path loss in crowded areas.

articleTitle: Antenna gain and phase center estimation for broadband antenna using metal ground plane
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We have already proposed a single antenna method for estimating an antenna factor of log-periodic dipole array antenna at 10 m antenna distance up to 1 GHz. In this paper, we apply our proposed single antenna method for double ridged guide horn antenna. For estimating the far field antenna gain, we apply the antenna phase center modified Friis transmission formula. We show the estimation results of far field antenna gain of double ridged guide horn antenna. Difference between the estimated gain using our proposed method and using 3-antenna extrapolation method is less than 0.83 dB in the frequency range from 1 GHz to 6 GHz.

articleTitle: Wide-band spatially distributed TE10 substrate integrated waveguide transition for high-power generation at mm-wave frequencies
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An array of microstrip lines is used for the direct excitation of the spatially distributed TE10 substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) mode. The proposed configuration can generate 4x more power with a 4x smaller form factor relative to a single microstrip-to-SIW transition, while offering a larger bandwidth. This is an important step toward the generation of high power in densely integrated mm-wave antenna systems.

articleTitle: Portable wide-band channel sounder based software defined radio for studying the radio propagation in an outdoor environment
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, applying the multimedia wireless sensor networks and computer vision techniques in the outdoor agriculture field can be observed. Since the performance of such techniques is limited by the low data rate of the wireless sensor network, the transmission using the wider bandwidth is one of the possible solutions. This paper proposes the technique to develop the wide-band channel sounder for investigating the wideband propagation characteristic in such outdoor environment by utilizing only the low cost and simple narrow-band software defined radio system. It can be realized by synchronizing the timing between the transmitter and the receiver over the air using the power detection approach as well as implementing the multitone-overlapping frequency stepping technique for the wideband coverage. The validation test in the laboratory was performed to verify the proposed channel sounder.

articleTitle: A novel design method for miniaturizing FSS based on theory of meta-materials
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel method has been developed that uses an equivalent circuit model with lumped elements to design a miniaturized Frequency Selective Surface (FSS), which is based on the theory of meta-materials. Specifically, the equivalent circuit model is introduced to simplify the design of the miniaturized FSS without using numerical analyses such as the method of moments (MoM), finite-difference time-domain (FDTD), or finite element method (FEM) in order to avoid many calculations and trials and errors. In this paper, to verify the proposed method, simplified band-pass and band-stop FSS models that have unit cells composed of an inductor and a capacitor are evaluated by comparing frequency characteristics of one S-parameter calculated by theoretical and numerical analyses. Additionally, to clarify the applicability of the equivalent circuit model with lumped elements to the design of miniaturized FSS, relationships between the ratio of the analytical resonant frequency to the theoretical resonant frequency and the ratio of the period of unit cells to the theoretical wavelength are evaluated by changing the parameters of the unit cells in the two cases. The evaluations results reveal that the proposed method can be used to design a miniaturized FSS under specific conditions.

articleTitle: A study into the PIN diode-based active metasurface for beam steering applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the PIN-diode modelling of an active-metasurfaced patch antenna at 2.45 GHz. The metasurface composed of closed-rings that coupled to a probe-fed patch antenna. Both the ideal and actual equivalent circuits with parasitic elements and two gap-lengths of closed rings are considered. Results indicate that the gap-lengths and parasitic elements affect the directivity and the beam directions.

articleTitle: Outage analysis of energy-harvesting based multihop cognitive relay networks with multiple primary receivers and multiple power beacons
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an energy-harvesting based decode-and-forward multi-hop cognitive relay protocol, where secondary users harvest energy from the radio frequency signals transmitted by multiple dedicated power beacons (PBs) to support the information transmission. The secondary transmitters including source and relays must adjust their transmit power to satisfy interference power constraints required by multiple primary receivers (PRs). For performance evaluation, we derive exact closed-form expressions of outage probability (OP) for the proposed method over Rayleigh fading channel. Moreover, the asymptotic expressions for the outage performance at high and low signal-to-noise (SNR) are given to provide insights into the system performance. Then, Monte Carlo simulations are performed to verify the analysis results. The obtained results presented that the outage performance of the proposed system significantly depends on the number of PBs, the interference constraint as well as the position of PBs and PRs. Finally, the analytical asymptotic results show that the optimal time splitting ratio only depends on the number of hops and the number of PBs at low transmit signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: Smallest form factor, high performance 2–18 GHz cavity-backed archimedean spiral antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present for the first time, the smallest form factor (50mm diameter) two-arm Archimedean spiral on TMM4 substrate, meeting all the performance metrics, which are necessary for commercial-grade product development, for UWB applications. The results show that the proposed antenna has gain above -5dBi, axial ratio less than 3dB and measured return loss less than -10dB throughout the whole 2-18 GHz band demonstrating the best performance with the smallest size.

articleTitle: A switch-beam circular array antenna using pattern reconfigurable Yagi-Uda antenna for space communications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a switch-beam circular array antenna using pattern reconfigurable Yagi-Uda antenna. A two-beam switching Yagi-Uda antenna is applied as an array element. The 3-element circular array is introduced to be able to switch the main beam in azimuth direction by switching the beam and shifting the excitation phase of array elements. The array antenna is designed at 2.4 GHz for drone or UAV radio controlling. The two-beam elements and 90°-shifted phase of excitation are applied to realize the proposed switched-beam array antenna. The simulated results show that the array antenna can provide 7 main beam directions covering a half azimuth plane (0° ≤ φ ≤ 180°) and gain of the array antenna is higher than 7 dBi.

articleTitle: Beam reconfigurable antenna using switchable parasitic elements for V2V applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A pattern reconfigurable antenna is proposed for vehicle to vehicle (V2V) communication applications. The proposed antenna consists of a monopole antenna at the center of the equilateral triangle structure with three reconfigurable parasitic elements with a PIN diode at each sidewall of the structure. When the diode is on, the parasitic element becomes a reflective surface. When the diode is off, the parasitic element becomes transparent surface to a vertically polarized incident wave. Therefore the beam steering property of the proposed antenna can be implemented by controlling the on/off state of a PIN diode of each parasitic element. The -10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth is 480 MHz from 5.66 GHz to 6.14 GHz. The gain at 5.9 GHz is 6.15 dBi with beam steering along the azimuth plane (θ = 90° plane).

articleTitle: Non-linear inter-user interference reduction for multi-user full-duplex MIMO system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper propose a method of suppressing inter-user interference in the in-band full duplex communication. In this method, an interference compress technique is used for eliminating the interference at the receiving terminal. Also, we evaluated the achievable transmission rate of the proposed method by using channel state information (CSI) measured by the outdoor field experiment.

articleTitle: LHCP X-band printed antenna with ellipse-shaped truncation for microsatellite data communication
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The development of left-handed circularly polarized (LHCP) X-band printed antenna for microsatellite data communication is presented. The antenna which takes a circular shape with ellipse-shaped truncation is designed to resonate at the frequency of 8.2GHz with the minimum axial ratio bandwidth of 400MHz. The proposed antenna is deployed on a 1.6mm thick NPC-H220A dielectric substrate. The realized antenna can achieve the 3dB axial ratio bandwidth of 6.3% or 520MHz ranges from the frequency of 7.98GHz to 8.5GHz.

articleTitle: Effects of the common mode on radiation patterns of the tapered slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We herein investigate the design of a tapered slot antenna (TSA) that is divided into a radiator and a feeding circuit (balun). We measured the differential component and common component of the surface current on the TSA in a previous study. Moreover, we measured the radiation patterns of the radiator and the balun in order to discuss the radiation of the TSA. In particular, the differential component and the common component of the radiator are measured. The radiation pattern of the TSA is calculated by synthesizing the three components of radiation from the radiator and the balun. The common component of the radiator is shown to be only slightly affected by the radiation of the TSA.

articleTitle: Beam-tilted lens-corrected horn antennas for wide-angle radiation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For covering a specified wide circular area with a tilted sectoral beam, this paper proposes compact beam-tilted multimode horns based on coaxial dual-path guides and shaped dielectric-lens onto the horn aperture. We present two design examples with a beam tilted up to 20 degrees for 24 GHz radio-sensor systems. One is constructed with an axially symmetrical structure and also is fed by a bend waveguide, and the other is loaded with an eccentric circular waveguide and an asymmetrical dielectric-lens for tilting the beam. We verify effectiveness of the proposed antennas from evaluating the radiation patterns and VSWR numerically and experimentally.

articleTitle: Planar antenna array on LTCC and rogers substrates for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The next generation of wireless communications is the horizon, and the telecoms world is waiting to see exactly at which frequencies 5G will be implemented. Despite some unknowns and technological challenges, it is increasingly becoming clear that the millimeter-wave will be a key enabler for 5G by allocating more bandwidth to deliver faster, higher-quality video, and multimedia content and services. The principal advantage of use of millimeter wave bands is a large amounts of contiguous spectrum can be used, which allows the delivery of high data rates, but the technology is not so mature as in microwave frequencies. This paper presents array antennas using different materials: low-temperature cofired ceramics (LTCC) and Rogers substrates of a single radiating element, 1×1 and 2×2 array. The 2×2 element array antenna achieves a −10 dB bandwidth from 58 to 62 GHz with a peak gain of 12.2 dBi at 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Square loop frequency selective surface with wide-passband properties using multi-period structures
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The frequency selective surface (FSS) with ultra-wide passband performance and a sharp rejection near the side of the passband is investigated in this paper. The proposed cascaded FSS consists of a 2-D periodic array of square loop aperture (SLA) and an array of bandstop square loop (SL) with different period. Under different incident waves, the proposed second-order FSS and third-order FSS provide 3 dB relative bandwidth 114% and 125%, which achieve wider bandwidth in comparison with the previously proposed structures.

articleTitle: Frequency reconfigurable compact MIMO antenna for WLAN application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A frequency reconfigurable Multiple-input Multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for Wireless Local Area Network(WLAN) application is proposed. Multiple-Input Multiple-output (MIMO) technology has been incorporated into wireless local area networks (WLANs) through the IEEE802.11n and 802.11ac standards. These MIMO WLAN systems can support up to four antenna elements and four data streams for each user or mobile station. These systems operate in the frequency bands of 2.4-2.5 GHz (802.11n) and 4.9-5.725 GHz. (802.11n and ac).

articleTitle: Compact segmented loop antenna for UAV applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle) applications, a proposed miniaturized segmented loop antenna is comprised of a segmented loop, stubs, and a shorting strip. By reducing the number of segments and adding stubs, the compact segmented loop antenna is realized. Addition of the shorting strip improve the impedance matching. The antenna has omnidirectional radiation at 956 MHz.

articleTitle: High-gain and broadband antenna using microstrip combined with the waveguide antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of high gain and broadband waveguide antenna which is fed by using a microstrip antenna is at 2.33 to 5.24 GHz. A feeding network is broadband microstrip antenna with the flower-shaped combined with the rectangular waveguide antenna to improve the directive gain. The proposed antenna can be fabricated on conventional low-cost materials by using FR4 and aluminum plate and the high gain and wideband performance are achieved with gain up to 8.79 dB. The simulated and measured impedance bandwidths of the broadband waveguide antenna are 76.88 % for |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| < 10 dB. The discrepancy between simulation and measurement is analyzed.

articleTitle: Ground clutter suppression in GPR using framing based mean removal and subspace decomposition
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) is one of the effective tools for detecting subsurface objects. However, the existence of ground clutter negatively affects target signal extraction particularly for shallowly buried objects and/or weak target responses. Thus, the reliable clutter suppression method is needed for enhancing the target responses. This paper proposes a novel approach for ground clutter reduction by using framing based mean removal and a subspace decomposition method. In the first step, the GPR signal is processed by cross-correlation with a reflection from a flat-surface as the reference for determining the timing range of surface reflection. Then, the mean of the two neighboring traces in the predicted range is removed. The singular value decomposition and K-means algorithm are used to remove the residual noise according to the singular values. The simulation results indicate that the proposed method can effectively suppress the ground clutter without contamination of the target signal.

articleTitle: A low-profile wideband gradient refractive index lens antenna based on metasurface
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a new low-profile high-gain wideband gradient refractive index (GRIN) lens fed by a magnetic-electric (ME) dipole antenna. As a constituent part of this lens, a novel sub-wavelength nonresonant metamaterial unit cell composed of 3-layer substrates is also proposed. By applying Rogers 5880 and air as the top and bottom layers, high and low refractive indexes can be achieved for realizing the core layer and impedance matching layer (IML), respectively. Therefore, the proposed lens antenna can exhibit high gain of 19 dBi and -10 dB bandwidth of 58% (6.8-12.4 GHz). Moreover, due to the high refractive index which is realized by the bilayer cross-shaped rings meta unit cell, the total thickness of the lens is 0.32 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the wavelength at 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Compact printed UWB MIMO antenna with pattern diversity characteristic for portable devices
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper a novel compact printed ultra wide band (UWB) multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna is presented with pattern diversity characteristic for portable devices. The MIMO configuration consists of two identical compact UWB antennas with a very simple decoupling circuit. To analyze the performance of antenna in UWB range the impedance bandwidth, isolation, radiation pattern, gain and efficiency are investigated. However, the MIMO performance is analyzed by envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) of the UWB MIMO antenna.

articleTitle: MIMO monopole microstrip antenna for LTE
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discuss about a MIMO monopole microstrip antenna for LTE application. The MIMO antennas that are currently commercially available for LTE applications generally only cover a narrowband of LTE frequency. Meanwhile, the antenna to cover wider bandwidth will cost a high price. A MIMO microstrip antenna is proposed to overcome that issue due to its small size compared to other antenna for wider bandwidth so that it could save the cost. Based on the measurement in anechoic chamber, the proposed antenna gives a good performance for frequency of 800–2600 MHz. The MIMO monopole microstrip antenna elements have antenna gain of 2–5 dB and mutual coupling below −20 dB.

articleTitle: A reconfigurable Yagi-Uda antenna using EGaIn liquid metal
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A reconfigurable Yagi-Uda with the liquid metal is proposed in this article. By a new electrochemical method for reversible, we control the length of liquid eutectic gallium indium (EGaIn) in the capillary. Electrochemical deposition (or explode) of a surface-oxide on the EGaIn significantly lowers (or increases) its tension to induce the liquid metal up (or down) of the capillary. The three-element array consists of the elements whose lengths can be changed with the liquid metal, resulting in the array directors can be transformed into reflectors, and elements can be changed to the different frequencies. Simulation in CST shows that good impedance matching is realized from 0.85 to 0.95 GHz with the gain over 5dBi and the VSWR lower than 2 across the entire band. The utilization coefficient of aperture field reached 70%. This antenna can be widely used in millimeter radar or communication system.

articleTitle: A high impedance folded dipole antenna with three conductors for energy harvesting applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We have studied a high impedance antenna in order to improve the rectifier efficiency for energy harvesting applications. Folded dipole antenna (FDA) with high impedance of over 10 kΩ is proposed. To obtain higher impedance stepup ratio compared with the conventional FDA, an FDA consisting with three strip conductors is investigated. Impedance stepup ratio is calculated and the results in theory, simulation and measurement are compared.

articleTitle: Design of balanced CPW-Fed L-shaped CP antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a balanced CPW-fed circularly polarized (CP) antenna is proposed. The antenna consists of two L-shaped monopole radiating elements which are deployed perpendicular to each other to excite orthogonal radiation fields. A 90° delay line section is embedded in one of the differential feedlines to provide 90° phase difference between signals fed to the two input ports. The combination of the above designs were verified to give good CP radiation field patterns. In addition, to suppress the common-mode signals, a half-wavelength CPW line section is connected between the two feedlines for producing a transmission zero in the DM passband under CM operation. For the designed balanced CP antenna, Measurement shows that the |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dd</sup>| ≤ -10dB DM operating band covers a frequency range of 2.04-2.87 GHz. Very good CM suppression was observed with the measured CM reflection coefficient greater than -3 dB for 2.1-2.86 GHz. The simulated 3-dB axial ratio band is 2.38-2.54 GHz.

articleTitle: A study on channel characteristics of massive MIMO in urban street environments
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper shows 20 GHz band channel characteristics of Massive MIMO in urban street cell environments with vehicle traffic. 10×10-Uniform Planar Array (UPA) formed with unidirectional antenna elements, facing to opposite sidewalk is used as a base station antenna, and is located on the sidewalk. The MIMO channel characteristics are then evaluated by calculating each propagation path when the receiver with two dipole antennas moved on the sidewalk along the roadway. As the results, it is expected that vehicle shadowing produces significant influence to MIMO channel characteristics.

articleTitle: Focusing characteristics of near-field radiations from multi-panels of phased array of antennas in circularly cylindrical arrangement
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the focusing characteristics of near fields radiated from multi-panel phased array antennas, where each panel of the antenna array is designed to focus its radiation in the antenna near-field region, for UHF-RFID applications. The cylindrical arrangement of panels creates a relatively symmetrical focusing region beneficial to the tag detection within a confined region of bio-medical applications for non-contact medical information extraction.

articleTitle: Wireless sensor node with UHF RFID for monitoring system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes the development of indoor monitoring system based on UHF RFID system and raspberry Pi 3. An algorithm is developed to link the UHF RFID reader module to the Raspberry Pi 3, send the data received to a database via wireless network, and display the data on a user interface module. To determine the best RFID tag for the system, the performance of two UHF RFID tags, UPM DogBone and AZ-9640 is held. The result is collected and tabulated, and it can be concluded that UPM DogBone shows better performance BECAUSE the size of the antenna is bigger than that of AZ-9640.

articleTitle: Beam-steering antennas using metalines
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Four linearly-polarized (LP) metalines are adopted for realizing an LP beam-steering antenna, where one of the four feed points is activated (connected to a source) and the remaining three feed points are non-activated (open-circuited). Similarly, an antenna system composed of four circularly-polarized (CP) metalines is investigated to realize a CP beam-steering antenna. The LP and CP waves radiate in the backward direction relative to the activated feed point.

articleTitle: 5.8 GHz rectifier circuit for electromagnetic energy harvesting system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an RF rectifier circuit for electromagnetic energy harvesting system. The double voltage rectifier together with the super capacitor are employed to harvest the electromagnetic energy. The proposed circuit is designed to operate at 5.8 GHz Wi-Fi frequency band. The Schottky diode SMS7630-061 is used to implement the proposed rectifier circuit. The super capacitor 5 V with capacity of 1 F is employed to collect the electromagnetic energy. It is found that the output voltage is greater than 2.8V at 5.5-5.8 GHz.

Author Keywords: 1. Double Voltage RF Rectifier Electromagnetic energy harvesting

articleTitle: Design of a wideband circularly polarized 2 × 2 array with shorted annular patches at X-band on a CubeSat
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The design of a single layer wideband circularly polarized 2 × 2 microstrip array at X-band frequencies is described. The antenna elements are shorted annular patches and the array is driven with a sequential-phase feeding network. The array is modelled on a 1U CubeSat. The performance of the array is compared to a single element microstrip antenna.

articleTitle: Scattering performance of a reflectarray using log-periodic dipole array element
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Scattering performance of a reflectarray using a log-periodic dipole array (LPDA) element is demonstrated numerically and experimentally. The LPDA element and the reflectarray are designed using method of moments (MoM). The designed 10 × 1 reflectarray was fabricated using a 3D printing technology. A bistatic radar cross section (BRCS) of the designed reflectarray was measured in a radio anechoic chamber. The measured BRCS is in good agreement with that obtained using the MoM except for ripples and the effect of near-field. According to so-called self-complementary structure of the LPDA element, 1-dB bandwidth over 40 % is achieved for the designed reflectarray.

articleTitle: Comparison of meander line and NFRP miniaturization techniques for RFID on-chip antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Antenna miniaturization techniques using meander line and Near-field Resonant Parasitic (NFRP) are presented in this paper. Also, antenna performance including reflection loss and gain have been optimized during the scale-down process. The proposed antennas are compared with the theoretical limits of small antennas to confirm the optimized performance in a limited space. The smallest possible size of the proposed antenna is 0.0232λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> in length or ka = 0.103. The proposed scaling strategy will be applied to the design of RFID on-chip antennas in the future.

articleTitle: A study on channel capacity of MIMO systems with a receiver with antenna pattern modulation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We evaluate the channel capacity of MIMO systems whose receiver uses Antenna Pattern Modulation (APM) to develop multiple received signal components by a single receive antenna unit. We assume the antenna pattern which varies with sum of sinusoidal waveforms with different frequencies. The APM generates diversity branches in the frequency domain. We evaluate the channel capacity of the proposed MIMO systems for the case of two transmit antennas. The capacity of the proposed system increases in increasing the number of arrived paths because of the path diversity gain.

articleTitle: E-band double layer cavity backed slot array antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper a double layer cavity backed slot array antenna at E band is presented for point-to-point wireless communication. The antenna is built using an equal-split rectangular waveguide feed network and 2×2 elements sub array. The feed network is composed four E-plane T-junctions to lower the leakage between the metal plate. The 8×8 slot array antenna has been fabricated using PEI resin. The measured reflection coefficient remains below −10dB with reasonably good radiation patterns and gain over 24.8dB of the band from 71 GHz to 86 GHz.

articleTitle: Multi-polarization reconfigurable omnidirectional antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A new multi-polarization reconfigurable omnidirectional antenna is proposed. The antenna consists of a top-loaded monopole for vertically polarized working state (VP), a circular loop for horizontally polarized working state (HP). The circularly polarized working state (CP) is achieved by exciting the monopole and the loop simultaneously with different phases. It is shown that the bandwidth overlapped for VP, HP, and CP is about 25% (1.7-2.2 GHz) with good omnidirectional patterns.

articleTitle: Flexible printed antenna for digital TV reception
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A flexible printed antenna has been developed for digital television (DTV) reception. The antenna is a meander line printed on a polyimide film. It is extremely thin, flexible, compact, and very light weighted. The antenna is designed to operate in the UHF band with a relatively broad bandwidth covering the DTV broadcast frequency in Thailand. Due to its thinness and flexibility, the antenna is suitable for being integrated in a television set, conformally mounted on a wall or window, laminated within a glass window, etc. A prototype antenna has been built and tested. Measurement results are shown in this paper.

articleTitle: A circularly polarized bi-directional surface wave antenna with low-profile
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A surface wave antenna (SWA) with low profile and circular polarization is proposed. The proposed structure consisting two substrates: microstrip element on upper and feeding patch with ground plane on the lower. A microstrip line is radiating element with a length of approximately 2λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> which can radiate circular polarization resulting in bi-directional beams along the longest part of the elements. The hook-shaped elements are added by connected to the ground plane to generate horizontal component of electrical field with 90-degree phase difference with the vertical components radiated by the microstrip element.

articleTitle: A dual-band LHCP stacked patch antenna array
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study developed a 2×4 dual-band left-handed circular polarization (LHCP) patch antenna array for receiving Global Positioning System (GPS) reflections at 1227 MHz and 1575 MHz. The antenna element is achieved by probe feed stacked patch and the signal is combined by an 8-way power divider. According to the measured results, the axial ratio at the center frequencies is below 3 dB and the peak gain of the antenna array is about 12.2 dBic and 14.5 dBic at 1227 MHz and 1575 MHz respectively.

articleTitle: Simulating the MIMO efficiency of antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Presented is a mathematical model to compute the multiple-input multiple-output efficiency of a multiport antenna in the single-user case. The evaluation comprises the performance of a zero-forcing receiver in two limiting propagation scenarios, i.e., the random line-of-sight and the rich isotropic multipath channels.

articleTitle: Low profile wideband planar AMC surface for X-band applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel design of low profile wideband artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) surface structure. The ±90° reflection phase bandwidth of the AMC surface is 7.93-12.23 GHz (S11≤ -10 dB), while the 0° reflection phase center frequency is 10 GHz. With the utilizing of the 6 × 6 AMC surface, a patch antenna can achieve a bandwidth enhancement of 233% and increased gain of more than 2 dB in the operating frequency band of the AMC surface.

articleTitle: Mechanical satellite tracking free distributed array antenna system for satellite base stations
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel satellite base station configuration based on the Distributed Array Antenna (DAA) technique is studied to eliminate mechanical satellite tracking equipment. A DAA controller integrates all antennas so each antenna's aperture can be downsized and its transmitting power reduced while realizing the required characteristics. This paper revealed the maximum gain achievable with the DAA base station.

articleTitle: Hexagonal monopole antenna with reconfigutablity between UWB and band notched UWB
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A hexagonal monopole ultra wideband (UWB) antenna with reconfigurable band suspension functionality is experimentally studied in this paper. The proposed antenna is capable to switch its resonance from entire ultra wideband to single band notched ultra wideband applications using single p-i-n diode switch. The impedance bandwidth enhancement of the antenna is achieved by optimization of the hexagonal radiating patch and the ground plane. Single slot is inserted in hexagonal patch to embed the p-i-n diode. Simulated and measured results of return loss, E/H-field patterns and gain are obtained and good agreement is achieved.

articleTitle: Meander line tag antenna with inductively coupled parasitic element and T-loop feed
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a meander line dipole antenna for Ultra High Frequency Radio Frequency Identification (UHF RFID) tag applications is presented. The proposed antenna consists meandered dipole with end spiral conductor, an inductively coupled parasitic element for size miniaturization and T-loop for feed structure. The antenna is designed for North America UHF RFID frequency band (902-928 MHz) with Alien Higgs IC chip. The size of proposed tag antenna is 50mm × 12mm and exhibits good characteristics like reflection coefficient, impedance characteristics and radiation pattern with smaller size.

articleTitle: Absorber integrated planar slot array antenna for a 120-GHz-band close-proximity wireless system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We investigated the millimeter-wave absorber integrated planar slot array antenna for a 120-GHz-band close proximity wireless system. Precise alignment and multiple reflection between Tx-Rx antennas become the problem for the application of >100-GHz-close-proximity wireless system. The millimeter-wave absorber integrated planar slot array antenna solves these problems. We adopted the split-ring resonators (SRRs) patterned on the dielectric layer for the absorber, and the simulated S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> of the absorber at 125 GHz is below -40 dB. We simulated the transmission characteristics of the close proximity wireless system using these absorber integrated planar slot antennas. The simulated fluctuation of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> in the 120-130 GHz band is below 4 dB, and the delayed waves that comes from the multiple reflection between Tx and Rx antenna was suppressed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of analog OAM transmission using dual-circular polarized antenna array
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate feasibility of orbital angular momentum (OAM) based analog transmission method. The method uses analog discrete Fourier transform (DFT) feed networks for mode generation as well as circular array antenna with right-hand and left-hand circular polarizations. The simulation revealed the designed array antennas enhance the capacity up to double of the single polarization scenario.

articleTitle: A compact two-port tunable dual-band spiral antenna for MIMO terminals
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a frequency tunable Dual Band Inverted L Spiral Antenna (DBILSA) for Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) mobile terminals is presented. Two different shapes of L-shape and spiral shape were combined to produce a dual band response. Varactor diodes were used to simultaneously tune the resonant frequency from 1900 MHz to 3100 MHz (in the lower band) and from 3300 MHz to 3700 MHz (for the upper band), with a minimum reflection coefficient of -10 dB. Maximum realized gains of 2.83 dB (in the lower band) and 3.28 dB (in the upper band) are achieved. Besides that, a high isolation between the two DBILSA elements reduced the mutual coupling to result in an Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) of less than 0.2. Along with its frequency tuning ability and the low ECC, the proposed MIMO antenna is deemed suitable for mobile terminal applications.

articleTitle: Bistatic RCS reduction characteristics of flat and curved metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Thin metasurface absorbers with stable absorbing frequency in the oblique incident angles have been required. This paper presents the bistatic RCS reduction characteristics of the flat and curved metasurfaces in TE incidence wave. In both flat and curved metasurfaces, when the incident angle increases, the absorbing frequency shifts to higher. However, the RCS reduction decreases as the incident angle increases. In addition, the curved metasurface shows similar RCS reduction characteristics to those of the flat metasurface.

articleTitle: A simple circularly polarlized antenna array for millimeter-wave applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A simple circularly polarized (CP) antenna array is proposed for millimeter-wave applications. The proposed CP antenna array has a two-layer structure, which is easy for fabrication. A circular loop with a parasitic element is used as the radiation element for wideband operation. It is shown that the proposed 4×4 CP antenna array can achieve a gain of 13-16 dBi from 28.5 to 31.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Element pattern prediction in mutually-coupled arrays through isolated antenna characterization
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A simple method is proposed that is capable of predicting antenna array embedded element patterns based on the radiation and scattering characteristics of a single isolated antenna element. The effect of mutual coupling, which causes embedded element patterns to differ, is accounted for through the multi-scattering of electromagnetic fields between array elements. This is a post-processing step and therefore obviates the need to run time-consuming full-wave electromagnetic field simulations, which is particularly important when numerous antenna array configurations need to be analyzed rapidly. The accuracy of three single-scattering versions of the pattern prediction method are evaluated on a range of two-element dipole arrays.

articleTitle: Fundamental study on angular resolution improvement of SAR tomography by using Khatri-Rao Product virtual array processing
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: SAR Tomography (TomoSAR) regards multi-baseline observation data as array observation data and realizes three-dimensional imaging by applying direction of arrival (DOA) estimation processing. To improve angular resolution of the TomoSAR with suppressing ambiguity, many repeat-pass data are required. However, it is often difficult to increase the number of data because of the cost. In this paper, we propose to apply the Khatri-Rao (KR) product virtual array processing to the multi-baseline observation data. We show that the KR processing improves angular resolution of the TomoSAR and suppression of ambiguity by using the experimental data obtained by the Pi-SAR2-X.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave frequency scanning antenna for body centric communication
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
