abstract: Millimeter wave spectrum is the main candidate for body centric wireless applications such as health monitoring, live streaming, and gaming. In this paper, a frequency scanning microstrip antenna array is designed as it provides reconfigurability in the direction of main beam pattern. The designed antenna is an array of 16 elements with the measured impedance bandwidth from 33GHz to 40GHz. The S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> is better than -10 dB and S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> of less than -10 dB is achieved. The beam shift is obtained for frequencies from 33GHz to 36GHz with shifts from -45° to -31.2° and +31.2° to +45°.

articleTitle: Dual-band bandpass filter with double-step impedance dumbbells for the second band improving
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This microstrip dual-band bandpass filter consists of double open-ended resonators and dumbbells designed by using the concept of symmetry. Two transmissions zero appear by zero-degree feed position. The proposed bandpass filter is created to support WLAN applications at 2.45 GHz and 5.20 GHz, respectively. Both insertion losses are greater than -0.9 dB and the return losses are below -18 dB. The proposed bandpass filter has compact size by 26.135 × 14.44 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> dimension.

articleTitle: Element-staggered, circularly polarized reflectarray with linearly polarized feed for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a circularly polarized reflectarray with linearly polarized feed operating at 28GHz for 5G applications. The proposed reflectarray is composed of a flat reflecting surface populated with numerous two-layer ground-backed non-resonant subwavelength rectangular patch elements which are in staggered arrangement and a Vivaldi antenna as the linearly feeder. Simulated results demonstrated that the reflectarray provides a gain around 27dB and a axial ratio better than 3dB within the 24-32 GHz operating frequency range (equivalently 29% bandwidth).

articleTitle: Antenna placement on complex platforms by using characteristic mode analysis and characteristic basis function technique
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The paper investigates the problems of placement of antennas on complex platform to realize the desired impedance and radiation patterns using the Characteristic mode analysis (CMA) as well as the Characteristic Basis Function technique. A comparison of the two techniques is presented when they are applied to two real-world examples, namely a mobile phone and the topside of a ship.

Author Keywords: Characteristic Basis Functions: antennas on complex platforms

articleTitle: Evaluation of vital sign distribution using array antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The authors investigated the spatial distribution of the vital sign on the human body using array antenna. We deployed the array antenna in front and back of the body, and used direction of arrival (DOA) estimation method. As a result, it was found a vital sign distribute intensely at left of the chest, which corresponds to the source location of cardiac impulse.

articleTitle: Design of antenna reflector using two layer frequency selective surfaces for directivity enhancement in UWB application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of UWB reflector for antenna application by using two layers of a band stop frequency selective surface (FSS). The structures of both FSS are based on the modified square ring resonator. By combination of two FSS structures, they achieve the wide frequency range of 2.9-11.2 GHz. The demonstration of the FSS reflector with UWB slot antenna shows that the radiation efficiency of antenna is improved over the entire UWB spectrum.

articleTitle: Use of coordinate rotation angle for improving man-made target detection performance
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose an improved coordinate rotation method for four component decomposition. The experimental results show that the proposed method has higher performance for detecting man-made targets.

articleTitle: Study of dielectric properties in sphere for fruit quality classification
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a material properties analysis of sphere with microwave free space measurement for monitoring fruit classification. The monostatic radar cross section (RCS) at various complex relative permittivity (ϵ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = ϵ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>' - jϵ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>") was analyzed and used for determining different material. Variation of the dielectric constant (ϵ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>') provides higher the monostatic RCS than the loss factor (ϵ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>"). The measured results in 0.8 to 3 GHz frequency range show an obvious difference in backscattered that is possible to separate fruit in spherical shape.

articleTitle: Multi-beam massive MIMO using beam selection with only amplitude control
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Massive MIMO transmission has been attracted much attention as one of key technologies in next-generation mobile communication system, because it enables improvement in service area and interference mitigation by simple signal processing. Multi-beam massive MIMO configuration has proposed that utilizes the beam selection in analog part and blind algorithm such as constant modulus algorithm (CMA) which does not need channel sate information (CSI) is applied in digital part. In this paper, to achieve the further higher transmission rate, we propose beam selection method with only amplitude information regarding the multi-beams.

articleTitle: Improvement of radio propagation estimation accuracy by completing plane-based 3D models obtained with depth sensors
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to improve the estimation accuracy of radio propagation simulation using a 3D model reconstructed by depth sensors, recovering missing regions of the 3D model is important. In this paper, we report an evaluation result of indoor radio estimation accuracy by using such a completed 3D model. We first describe the evaluation scene and the measurement method of radio powers we used for experiments. We then give an overview of the method for reconstructing and completing a 3D model of the evaluation scene. Finally, we compare simulation results obtained with the original model and the completed model against the real measurements. The errors obtained with the original and completed model were 2.40 dB and 2.16 dB respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of the 3D model completion for the indoor radio estimation.

articleTitle: High-frequency asymptotic solution of scattering field by three-layered dielectric slab for accurate propagation analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper derives high-frequency asymptotic approximate solution of scattered field by three-layered dielectric slab. Here H-polarized case is considered. In order to bundle or collect the multiple reflected rays inside the slab into the primary reflected and transmitted rays, high frequency asymptotic approximation technique is applied. We call the derived primary rays `collective rays'. By using the present ray solutions instead of the conventional ones, the internal multiple reflections effect can be easily included in ray tracing analysis without increase of the computational cost, and one can execute accurate propagation analysis through indoor-to-outdoor (or outdoor-to-indoor) environments efficiently.

articleTitle: A printed inverted-F antenna for circular polarization — Part 2
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Authors have proposed a printed inverted-F antenna (PIFA) for circular polarization. In this paper, an approach to improve the bandwidth is investigated. It is shown that the bandwidth can be widened by designing the rectangular element loaded at the feeding line as short as possible. The redesigned PIFA in this paper has approximately twice (210MHz) the bandwidth of the 3dB-axial ratio with a 10dB-return loss than that of the circularly polarized PIFA previously. The antenna area is 0.068λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>: the wavelength at the center frequency). The antenna is small in size.

articleTitle: Impact of yaw angle of wind turbines on diffraction loss of radar signals
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The impact of rotor yaw angle on the diffraction loss of a radar beam due to scattering at a 3-blade rotor of a wind turbine (WT) is investigated. Simulation results for a C-band weather radar are based on 2D Fresnel-Kirchhoff diffraction approach considering negligible impact of the ground plane.

articleTitle: A fast 3-D ray tracing method for wave propagation prediction using a reflection tube tree
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A fast 3-D ray tracing method based on image theory is presented. The proposed method defines reflection tubes and organizes them in a tree structure to treat images efficiently in a complex 3-D environment. The method can account for all possible rays undergoing multiple reflections and transmissions, and its predictions agree well with the measurements.

articleTitle: High efficiency with low X-pol compact antenna test range
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper. High performance quiet zone of CATR is designed and implemented. The size of quiet zone is 1.2m × 1.2m × 1.2m with prime feed offset 3 meters reflector. The cross-pol plane wave is −60 dB at boresight beam direction. The operating frequency of this CATR is from 10 GHz to 40 GHz. The power budget of CATR is analyzed for low cross-pol antenna measurement. Both results of simulation and measurement of CATR are also compared.

articleTitle: Invited talk 5: 3D inkjet printed flexible and wearable antenna systems
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: With the advent of wearable sensors and internet of things (IoT), there is a new focus on electronics which can be bent so that they can be worn or mounted on non-planar objects. Moreover, there is a requirement that these electronics become extremely low cost, to the extent that they become disposable. The flexible and low cost aspects can be addressed by adapting additive manufacturing technologies such as inkjet printing and 3D printing. This paper presents inkjet printing as an emerging new technique to realize low cost, flexible and wearable antenna systems. The ability of inkjet printing to realize electronics on unconventional mediums such as plastics, papers, and textiles has opened up a plethora of new applications. A variety of antennas such as wide-band, multiband, and wearable, etc, which have been realized through additive manufacturing techniques are shown. Many system level examples are also shown, primarily for wireless sensing applications. The promising results of these designs indicate that the day when electronics can be printed like newspapers and magazines through roll-to-roll and reel-to-reel printing is not far away.

articleTitle: Study on propagation loss through human body for wireless capsule application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The transmission factor of a dipole to dipole and a loop to loop through homogenous human muscle equivalent material is investigated using the FDTD analysis. The transmission factors of the dipole system and the loop system are compared and the optimization of antenna type and the optimal frequency is also discussed. In the case of dipole system, a local maximum of transmission factor is observed at frequency domain. In the case of loop system, the transmission factor decreases as frequency increases monotonously. The transmission factor of loop system is larger than that of the dipole system in the low frequency region, while the performances of both two systems are almost the same in the high frequency region.

articleTitle: H-plane SIW horn antenna made of textile for millimeter-wave WBAN application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: H-Plane substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) antenna made of textile for millimeter wireless body area network (WBAN) application is proposed. Three-stepped tapered matching structure was added to a coaxial feed for improving the impedance matching. The ground was extended to the antenna aperture to prevent the degeneration of radiation pattern by phantom. The extended arc shaped substrate improves the front-to-back ratio. In order to integrate with a wearable device, textile materials are used for making the antenna. The simulated 10-dB reflection coefficients bandwidth is 7380 MHz (26.03 GHz-33.41 GHz) which covers potential candidate frequency bands (28 GHz, 32 GHz) of 5G communication. The peak gains are 11.25 dBi at 28 GHz and 12.39 dBi at 32 GHz on the skin equivalent phantom.

articleTitle: Selective wireless power transfer for multiple receivers by using magnetic resonance coupling
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) is expected to spread around the world. WPT has two types, one is magnetic induction and another is magnetic resonant coupling (MRC). In magnetic induction, the amount of received power is determined by the transfer distance and the amount of magnetic flux through receiving coil. Therefore in transferring power to multiple receivers at each fixed transfer distance, power is transferred to all of the receiving coils through which magnetic flux passes. It is the problem that power may be distributed to the other receivers. This paper proposes transferring power to only one of various receivers by using MRC, selective WPT. In MRC, since a receiver is coupled to a transmitter by the resonant frequency, one receiver is distinguished from the others by the frequency. Experimental results represented the success of selective WPT. This proposal is useful for transferring power to one appropriate receiver independently of other receivers.

articleTitle: Plane wave excitation of wide optical leaky waveguide antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the plane wave excitation of the optical leaky waveguide antenna (OLWA) by the taper array and offset parabolic reflector to obtain high antenna gain. The taper array is composed of 12 slow tapers, and obtain high aperture efficiency. The parabolic reflector enables small size as compared with the taper array. We compare the performance of these excitation methods for the wide grating waveguide (GWG) in the simulation.

articleTitle: TE-wave scattering and transmission from misaligned dual-metallic grating screens
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a rigorous analysis of electromagnetic scattering and transmission of dual-metallic grating screens. The Fourier transform is used to represent the electric and magnetic fields in the spectral domain and the boundary conditions are enforced to obtain simultaneous equations using the mode-matching technique. Numerical results show that the dual-metallic grating screens exhibit asymmetric electromagnetic scattering and transmission properties with respect to the screen axis due to the change of the lateral displacement between dual-metallic gratings.

articleTitle: Complex relative permittivity analysis for monitoring watermelon
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a study of complex relative permittivity (ϵ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=ϵ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>'-jϵ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>") for monitoring watermelon. The complex relative permittivity of peel and pulp are analyzed as variation of maturity stages and used for determining mature fruit of watermelon from the measured reflection coefficient. The results depict the operating frequency is in the range 0.8 to 3 GHz. The distinct difference of reflection coefficient for immature and mature watermelon presented the feasibility to design a watermelon classification system.

articleTitle: Single/dual band selectable metamaterial absorber
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A single or dual band selectable metamaterial absorber constituted by a toppled “H” like shaped structure with four diamond shaped patch is presented in this paper. Attached to the diamond shaped patches are copper switches (S1, S2, S3, & S4) which are used in switching operational frequency/operational modes The proposed structured demonstrated single or dual band operation mode reconfiguration. It resonated at 7.20 GHz for single band where as it resonated at 7.20 GHz and 11.20 GHz for dual band operation mode. An FR4 substrate was used and the incidence wave angles were varied from 0° to 60°. Simulations results showed peak absorption of 100% was achieved at both resonance frequencies where as a minimum of 94.20% at 11.20 GHz was achieved.

articleTitle: Design of ellipsoidal reflector antennas for near-field RFID applications at UHF band
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of an ellipsoidal reflector antenna for the RFID applications at UHF band, which can be potentially integrated with a dome-shape building structure. Due to the dual-focus radiation characteristics in the ellipsoid near-field region, the feed located at one of the two foci can create a focused field distribution around the other focus, which is located in the ground area covered by the dome. In this case, the radiated energy will be confined so minimizing the interference effects outside of the targeted area.

articleTitle: A flexible transmission line using coplannar waveguide for on-body links
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A single layer non-contact coupling transmission line for on-body applications at 2.45 GHz is presented in this paper. The transmission line consists of units in series, and each unit functions as a band-pass filter or a two-side coupled half-wavelength resonator. The segmented coplanar waveguide is applied to make the transmission line have only a conductive layer. An advantage of the transmission line is that there is no need for ground plane in the case of a few millimeter spacing to body. The flexibility of the transmission line is provided by using 0.18 mm paper substrate and 9 μm silver ink conductor which can be easily embedded into fabric. The coupling power between the transmission line with an external antenna is evaluated and is good for short range communications.

articleTitle: Hierarchical MCU architecture for dynamic phase shifter controls in radiation beamforming by phased array of antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a hierarchical MCU (micro-control unit) architecture to reduce the number of wires required to control the RF devices of large phased array of antennas. In addition to cost reduction, the decrease of control wires may also reduce the electromagnetic interferences to the antenna radiation that are caused by the presence of wires. In particular, Genetic algorithm (GA) was also implemented to find the parameters in binary codes to reduce the phase discrepancy. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the feasibility.

articleTitle: A 433 MHz compact complex impedance-transforming balun
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A 433 MHz compact size balun that can transform a complex source impedance value to a complex load impedance value is demonstrated. The balun design is based on a coupled-line coupler balun. The simulation shows a good performance at 433 MHz operating frequency.

articleTitle: A flat, broadband and high gain beam-steering antenna for 5G communication
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A flat and low profile, wideband and high gain Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) Transmission Line (TL) Butler Matrix (BM) beamforming network (BFN) for beamforming and beam-steering applications at 28 GHz (5G) is presented in this paper. Four distinct beams steering between -35° to 35° with sidelobe and return-loss level below -10 dB are generated by connecting the proposed BFN to microstrip antennas forming a phased array antenna. The simulated and measured results are shown and discussed.

articleTitle: Comparison of spatial correlation between Japan and Thailand
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Site diversity is the one technique that has been used to reduce the rain attenuation effect for long time ago. Since the past, we just located the site diversity far away from the main site and thought that can be completely reduced the rainfall effect, but it does not. To improve this idea, in this paper, we propose another factor as call spatial correlation in order to design the location of site diversity more accuracy. We evaluate the spatial correlation for Japan and Thailand to confirm that the spatial correlation is totally different in each area and we should include this factor into the site diversity gain formula.

articleTitle: Moving target echo simulation of Video Synthetic Aperture Radar (ViSAR)
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Video Synthetic Aperture Radar (ViSAR) is a novel technique to continuously monitor moving targets in the interested area. From the video echo provided by the ViSAR system, the motion trail of the moving target can be easily obtained. Therefore, the echo of the moving target should be carefully studied, which is important in practical application for moving targets tracking in ViSAR system.

articleTitle: Broadband carpet cloak consisting of reflectarray with the Ω-shaped elements
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, a cloaking technology using reflecting elements has been marked. Cloaking devices using reflectarray have simple and very thin structure, so they are especially suitable for cloaking. This paper proposes a carpet cloaking using wideband reflectarray.

articleTitle: A planar reversed log-periodic UHF near-field antenna for RFID application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A planar reversed log-periodic near-field antenna is proposed for ultra-high frequency (UHF) radio frequency identification (RFID) application in this letter. The proposed antenna is composed of two planar reversed log-periodic dipole antenna (LPDA) units. The concept of two closely spaced, oppositely directed currents (ODCs) and the design guideline of LPDA are adopted to achieve strong and uniform magnetic field in the near-field zone of the antenna with a broad bandwidth. The proposed antenna is printed on a 170×170×1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> FR4 substrate. Except strong and uniform z-orientation magnetic field (Hz), the simulated results also show the antenna can achieve a broad bandwidth of 133MHz (833-966MHz) as well.

articleTitle: A 3-D printed lightweight cavity-backed monocone antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A lightweight exponentially tapered cavity-backed mono-cone antenna made by 3-D printing and conductive paint coating is proposed. To make the 3-D printed structure be metalized, three layers of conductive paint are used. To verify the proposed fabrication method, the 3-D printed antenna was fabricated and its return loss and far-field radiation characteristics were analyzed.

articleTitle: Rectangular dielectric resonator antennas with a thin graphene film
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the study of rectangular dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs) with a thin graphene film placed on the top surface of the resonator. The effect of the graphene film with different conductivities on the |S11| response and antenna gain of the rectangular DRAs is investigated. Both 50% and 100% graphene film coverage cases on the top surface of the DRA are considered. In the latter case, the dielectric resonator antenna is transformed into a microstrip antenna. For both cases, simulation and experimental results are presented. The results show that the graphene film conductivity has a significant effect on the performance of the DRA.

articleTitle: 3D printed System-on-Package (SoP) for environmental sensing and localization applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents for the first time an innovative 3D printed SoP sensor node with temperature, pressure and humidity sensing capabilities. It has an integrated wireless readout through a near isotropic (900MHz) GSM antenna-on-package. This sensor node is connected to the internet for remote monitoring and has the capability of localization. The paper presents the design of antenna-on-package as well as details of the communication and localization system. Fabrication challenges unique to 3D printing and integration of electronics on 3D printed circuit board are also discussed. Finally, the paper presents measurement results of antenna radiation pattern, return loss, localization accuracy and accuracy of sensing parameters.

Author Keywords: auxiliary vector potential isotropic antenna design

articleTitle: Compensation of antenna effects for stepped-frequency radar identification systems
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a compensation of variation effect of antennas for stepped-frequency radar identification systems. The antenna effects due to the variation in the antenna response and the mutual coupling degrade the target response in the identification systems. The equation used to reduce the antenna effect is derived. The simulations are demonstrated to validate the benefit of the compensation technique. The simulations are divided into several cases including different antennas and different shapes of objects. The simulation results confirm that the use of the compensation can improve the target response compared with the ideal case of without the antenna.

articleTitle: Accurate breast surface imaging method with FDTD-based waveform correction for microwave mammography
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Microwave mammography is promising alternative from X-ray based imaging modality, in terms of compactness, low cost and cell-friendly exposure. The most important part of this modality is a suppression of surface reflection clutters, which can be enhanced by combining accurate surface shape estimation. The coupling effect between antenna and breast surface degrades accuracy in the shape estimation, which is caused by a mismatch between reference and observed waveform. To solve this problem, this paper incorporates the Envelope-based shape estimation and FDTD-based waveform correction with a fractional derivative adjustment. Numerical simulation based on realistic breast phantom derived from MRI show that our proposed method significantly enhance the accuracy for breast surface imaging and the SCR (signal to clutter ratio) by suppressing a skin reflection.

articleTitle: Design of the modified WDRA for SAR indication of the breast tumor location
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the recent times the antenna is being used in the medical development for the efficient microwave imaging to detect the breast cancer. The role of design in this research is wideband dielectric resonator antenna (WDRA) by using an inverted L-shape with respect to the curved top face of DRA and inverted trapezoidal patch feed. The antenna design is modeled by using CST microwave studio software to demonstrate S11 and gain. WDRA that make this replication can also be used in the function of a medical technique that refer to specific absorption rate (SAR) of energy by tissue, the energy absorption properties of tumor over than normal breast tissue are shown in frequencies band between 4 GHz to 9 GHz, which it can be detected the phantom with precision in the size at the least 4 mm.

articleTitle: Design of chassis MIMO antenna using characteristic mode theory (invited paper)
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a design method for a chassis MIMO antenna based on characteristic mode theory. Specifically, we provide a way to use a chassis with one axis of symmetry as a multiport MIMO antenna. The method utilizes a combination of characteristic mode and a mode-decoupling network, and suggests a way to design an inductive coupling element to excite specific characteristic modes while simplifying the mode-decoupling network.

articleTitle: Dual-band conformal antenna with omnidirectional radiation pattern on cylindrical surface
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-band conformal antenna which resonates at lower WLAN (2.4 GHz) and high WLAN (5.8 GHz) frequency bands. And for both the bands, the conformal antenna has perfect omnidirectional radiation pattern. The proposed antenna is conformed onto a cylindrical structure of radius 200 mm. And the electromagnetic model and parametric analysis of the proposed antenna is developed in HFSS for optimization and analysis. The performance simulation results of the antenna are presented.

articleTitle: The effect of flange connectors on the radiation performance of narrow wall slotted waveguide antenna at X-band frequency
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper demonstrated the radiation performance of the effect of connecting two narrow wall slotted waveguide antennas using flange connectors at X-Band Frequency. The antenna designs consist of 64 slot at WR90 waveguide, with UBR100 flange connector. The simulation results show that side lobe level is the most influenced performance by connection. The antenna without flange connector has a better side lobe level of 5.06 dB compared to the antenna using a flange connector. The antenna without flange connector has a better side lobe level of 2.15 dB compared with the connecting trimmed flanges.

articleTitle: A high gain dielectric rod antenna with small aperture and wide band
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to reduce the minimum antenna measurement distance, the aperture reduction is needed. While the aperture reduction will cause the gain of the antenna reduced. The method of loading the elongated dielectric rod on the rectangular waveguide can remarkably improve the gain of the antenna without increasing the antenna aperture. A simulation study was carried out on the antenna with a dielectric rod loading covering 18–36 GHz. The dielectric rod is loaded on waveguide WR42 fed by the parallel coaxial. The CST simulation results show that the reflection coefficient of the antenna is lower than −10 dB in the frequency range of 18–36 GHz, the gain is stability in 10–16 dBi, and high efficiency is reached at high frequency, which is 95%.

articleTitle: Fixed-frequency beam-steerable leaky-wave antenna operating over a wide band
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a Half-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide (HMSIW) with interdigital slots mounted on its surface is used to explore fixed-frequency beam-steerable characteristic of Composite Right/Left Handed (CRLH) antenna based on HMSIW structure. By combining varactors and the PIN diodes with the antenna structure, fixed-frequency beam-steering radiation pattern can be realized. Main goal of our work is to realize a wide range of beam-steering angle at fixed frequency. In addition, because of the backward-to-forward frequency scanning ability of CRLH structure, we also focused on realizing fixed-frequency beam-steerable ability over a wide band. Moreover, the antenna is designed to be +45° polarized, so there is a potential that the antenna can be circular polarized if combined with the symmetric -45° antenna.

articleTitle: A hybrid diagnosis method for defective array elements based on compressive sensing and Iterative shrinkage thresholding algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The aim of this conference paper is to introduce a novel and effective diagnosis method for defective array elements by hybrid Compressive Sensing (CS) and Iterative Shrinkage Thresholding Algorithm (ISTA). The proposed method utilizes the framework of Compressive Sensing and the sparse signal is constructed via difference incentives of reference array without failures and array under test with failure elements. Fourier transform submatrix is used to constitute measurement matrix and a random undersampling strategy is implemented on the far field radiation patterns of reference array and array under test to acquire measurement data. Three ISTA, including Parallel Coordinate Decent (PCD) Algorithm, Separable Surrogate Functional (SSF) Algorithm, Iterative Reweighted Least Square (IRLS) Algorithm are then applied to reconstruct the sparse signal. Several simulation experiments are carried out and the results indicate that proposed method not only locates the positions of failure elements precisely, but also identifies their failure types using far less measurement points compared with traditional methods.

articleTitle: Experimental results of displacement measurement on a slope using 920-MHz-band radio waves
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In our previous study, we proposed a landslide monitoring system using a phase difference in the 920-MHz-band radio waves and experimentally confirmed that the positioning accuracy is of the order of millimeters. However, the experiments were not carried out on a real slope. In this paper, we report the experimental results of landside monitoring on a slope with tall vegetation.

articleTitle: A low-profile ultra-wideband directional antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to reduce the profile of the ultrawideband directional antenna, a disc-shaped combined dipole used as a feed is proposed, and a rectangular metal plate with right angle bend is used as a reflector. The disc-shaped dipole is used as a director. Through CST Microwave Studio modeling and simulation, ultimately achieved operating in 0.7-2.4 GHz, with a gain of more than 4 dBi ultra-wideband directional antenna. The ratio of the profile dimension to the wavelength of the minimum operating frequency is 0.15, and the front-to-back ratio is more than 6.5 dB. The simulation results show that the antenna can be regarded as a combined antenna of electric dipole and magnetic dipole.

articleTitle: Waveguide-type transmitarray antennas with a concave surface profile analogous to rotman lens for spatial feeding to radiate collinear multi-beams
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an architecture of transmitarray antenna consisting of waveguide-type elements. The array has a planar surface profile facing the beam directions of radiation, and has a convex surface profile facing to the feeds of illumination. The concave surface is analogous to the curve of Rotman lens for the applications of multi-beam radiation. The additional phases required in the concept of Rotman lens are created by controlling the domensions of waveguides. The transmitarray becomes very compact and functions in a standing alone fashion when it is illuminated by multiple feeds. The algorithm and examples will be demonstrated by numerical examples.

articleTitle: Triple band textile antenna using split annular ring
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a triple band textile antenna using split annular ring is presented for wearable applications of WLAN and WiMAX systems. The proposed antenna is designed to cover the frequency of 2.40 GHz (2.40 GHz to 2.484 GHz), 3.50 GHz (3.40 GHz to 3.69 GHz) and 5.20 GHz (5.15 GHz to 5.35 GHz). The antenna is made of felt fabric with dielectric constant of 1.90 as a substrate to obtain flexibility and lightweight structure. The characteristics of antenna such as |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|, radiation pattern and gain were investigated theoretically and experimentally. The simulation and measurement results are in reasonable agreement. Results show that the proposed antenna has good performance, can be applied for wearable applications.

articleTitle: Detection of an impure palmyra juice using short-time matrix pencil method
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the technique to detect the impure palmyra juice using short-time matrix pencil method (STMPM). The STMPM utilizes a sliding window and a matrix pencil method for extracting complex natural resonances of an object. Since the pure and impure palmyra juice have different complex permittivity, the complex natural resonances should also be different. The variation of complex natural resonances can later be used for designing a chipless RFID for impure palmyra juice detection.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized pyramid dielectric resonator antenna with single aperture fed
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A polarized pyramid dielectric resonator antenna fed by rectangular slot aperture is presented. The proposed dielectric resonator with given width to length ratio is easy to generate left-handed circular polarization by clockwise rotation angle of 45°. By optimizing the design parameters, 3dB axial ratio bandwidth of 8.9% (8.86-9.68GHz, 820MHz) and impedance bandwidth of 45.8% (7.78-12.4GHz, 4620MHz) are obtained. Moreover, the average antenna gain within the AR bandwidth achieves 6.8dB with less than 0.5dB variation. To verify the effectiveness of the design, the proposed antenna is simulated, fabricated and measured, achieving a good consistency between experimental and simulation results.

articleTitle: A reflectarray antenna design for installation on a 3U-CubeSat
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We present a realistic design of a reflectarray antenna for installation on a 3U-CubeSat, taking into account the dimensions of the CubeSat and space constraints afforded by the dispenser.

articleTitle: Processing of ultra-high resolution spaceborne spotlight SAR data based on one-step motion compensation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: With the development of spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR), the high resolution has become a hot topic again in recent years. However, the higher the resolution is, the worse the accuracy of the traditional hyperbolic range model (HRM) gets. In the case of ultra-high resolution spaceborne SAR, the curved orbit should be taken into account. To overcome this problem, we present a modified data-focusing scheme integrated with state-of-the-art airborne SAR motion compensation methods for spaceborne spotlight SAR. Firstly, one-step motion compensation is selected to correct the orbit curvature effectively, which has been applied in ultra-high resolution airborne SAR systems. Meanwhile, the two-step approach (TSA) is introduced to solve the azimuth spectral folding phenomenon. The simulation results validate the effectiveness of the scheme.

articleTitle: Specific absorption rate investigation on multiple antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Dealing with multiple antennas in various wireless devices has raised a distress of health effect. Thus, the investigation towards the relations between the electromagnetic field (EMF) radiation and human health is significant to be discovered. Hence, this paper presents the specific absorption rate (SAR) investigation on a single and 1 × 2 array of microstrip patch antenna operated at 0.8, 0.85, 0.9, 1.9, 2.1 and 2.6 GHz. The antenna is implemented close to specific anthropomorphic mannequin (SAM) human head model that fixed at 10 mm distance and 0.19 W for both single and 1 × 2 array tools in CST Microwave Studio 2016. The SAR performance for both; single and multiple antennas satisfied the standard limit established for all designated frequencies at averaged 1g and 10g mass of tissues.

articleTitle: Maltese-cross slot-array type frequency selective surface for a submillimeter-wave band
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-polarization Maltese-cross slot array (MCSA) type frequency selective surface (FSS) is designed for separating the submillimeter-wave band around 600 GHz in view of future application to spaceborne submillimeter-wave spectrometric radiometer. Based on this design, the FSS is fabricated by applying a photolithographic process on a thin dielectric (SiN) substrate. The transmission and reflection characteristics measured for the fabricated MCSA agree well with those simulated by the method-of-moment calculation. The possibility of the broadening of the transmission bandwidth by stacking the MCSA in two layers is also discussed.

articleTitle: Mode matching/FEM hybrid analysis for a short-slot 2-plane coupler considering the structural symmetry
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The hybrid analysis of mode matching/FEM (MM/FEM) is applied to a waveguide short-slot 2-plane coupler. The analysis model is reduced to the one-eighth model by considering the three-dimensional structural symmetry. The analysis results agree well with those by HFSS.

articleTitle: A power divider with tunable power
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a power divider is proposed. The presented divider consists four varactors and two microstrip lines. The divider has four ports, port 1, port 2, port 3 and port 4. Port 1 is the input port, and port 3, 4 are output ports. Besides, port 2 is the isolated port. When the capacitance of the four varactors is 0, the power is outputted in port 4. When the capacitance of the four varactors is 1 pF, the power is outputted in port 3. Therefore, a tunable power divider is achieved by adjusting the capacitance of the four varactors.

articleTitle: A high-gain high-efficiency corporate-fed slot array antenna directly fed by ridge gap waveguide at 60-GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An 8×8 slot array with high-efficiency and corporate-fed single layer by ridge gap waveguide at 60-GHz is introduced in this paper. The manufactured antenna depicts more than 19.6% bandwidth with input reflection coefficient better than -10 dB and the aperture efficiency higher than 70% with around 26 dBi realized gain between 58 and 66 GHz.

Author Keywords: millimeter wave and slot array antenna

articleTitle: Design of waveguide to microstrip line transition at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Now a day's increasing demand for higher bandwidth and other benefits of millimeter waves like line of sight communication and non bending property, molecular absorption, higher antenna gain at high frequencies make millimeter wave component design a favorite area of working. This transition structure of waveguide to microstrip line is useful for integration of high frequency circuits to the waveguide port without the use of connectors which are lossy at high frequency. Transition structure here is designed and simulated using HFSS software.

articleTitle: Invited Talk 6: Bio-effects of EM environment on human beings
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: New types of devices from electromagnetic (EM) technology and scientific area have emerged from its core in our society for a variety of purposes. EM radiation from these devices has caused growing concern about possible bio-effects and interference produced in the other devices. Our aim is to show the danger so that public can decide the risk they want to take. Quite similar to many phenomenon, it had its own obstacles and antagonisms (the entities and bodies that avoid, absorb, block, and/or reduce EM radiation) while it was intended to utilize its existence and specifications for the benefit of mankind. There are studies, researches and applications on the field heretofore. Focusing to a significant point, this talk also aims to establish an informational, intellectual ground to predict and measure the effects and interaction of electromagnetic radiation in the environment on living beings present as shoal. It is now the question that asks how much the human can tolerate the bio-effects, by produces the EM radiation in the environment. Even though there are numbered factors affecting electromagnetic pollution. In this talk, we will discuss the EM pollution in the environment and how much significance it is, thence to make a conclusive judgment about the issue. This talk, in addition, will focus on the sources of EM radiation, bio hazards cause by EM pollution, protection measures and standards relating the topic.

articleTitle: Computation of the far field from a nonuniformly spaced antenna elements using a least square method
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to describe a least square method to compute the far field from a nonuniformly spaced antenna array. This is because the far field pattern of an antenna array is the Fourier transform of the current distribution developed on the antenna structure, This is equivalent to computing the spectrum from a nonuniformly spaced data set using a least squares method. The merit of analyzing a nonuniformly spaced data set is that one need not satisfy the Nyquist sampling theorem in the strict sense. This is acceptable as long as the average sampling rate for the nonuniformly spaced data satisfies the Nyquist sampling theorem. A Fourier based least squares method can easily be extended to deal with nonuniformly spaced data, however the disadvantage of this procedure is that it is highly computational time intensive. Hence in this approach a Hilbert transform based methodology is described to significantly reduce the computation time without sacrificing accuracy. Hence, in methodology, this method is an extension to the Lomb periodogram technique which deals with the computation of the spectrum from a nonuniformly based data set. The problem with the Lomb periodogram method is that it cannot differentiate between the positive and the negative frequencies of the spectrum even though it has various other advantages. For example the effect of bias in the processed data can be reduced significantly in addition for a nonuniformly spaced data. Also because of a nonuniformly sampled data it is difficult to correctly estimate the amplitude of the far field or equivalently the spectrum hence a two-step methodology will be presented where at the first stage one solves for the spectral components and then applies a least squares solution procedure to get the best amplitude of the spectrum or equivalently the complex amplitudes for the far field. The Hilbert transform methodology is applied to reduce the computation time by a factor of one half in the computation of the complex spectrum as the real and imaginary parts of a causal function are indeed related by the Hilbert transform.

articleTitle: Characteristic mode analysis for small handset antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The recent cellular phones including smart phone have various functions. And the built-in antennas with broadband and multi-band characteristics inside the limited space have been required. For designing the small handset antenna, the full-wave analysis method, e.g. the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method, is employed. The design goal is to meet various required performance while keeping its small size. This paper presents the characteristic mode analysis (CMA) for small handset antenna design with the excitation of the antenna.

articleTitle: Noise figure evaluation of metamaterial structure including active components
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: One of the ways to obtain non-reciprocal response is a utilization of active components. Active components inherit non-linear responses and noise production. These “unwanted” accompanying response should be comprehended in advance, for metasurface application of this metamaterial structure in addition to planar microwave component, which are no needs to be considered in pure passive metamaerial structure. In this paper, noise figure as a response of frequency through the metamaterial operation frequency range is evaluated. The results indicate the clear necessity of noise figure consideration for the case of metamaterial structure including feedback loop and active component.

articleTitle: Specific area communication system using binomial coefficients array
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Restriction of communication area is preferable in view point of security. In this paper, a communication area restriction method is proposed. In the proposed method, binomial coefficient array for transmitting and for jamming is used. In the conventional method, the beam for jamming was formed using 2 elements; while in this paper, the beam is formed using 8 elements binomial array. As a result of analysis, it is shown that the undesired radiation is drastically reduced by the proposed method.

articleTitle: Invited talk 4: Compact multiband antennas using coplanar structures for several wireless applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Several compact multiband antennas used for wireless communications will be presented in this lecture. Most of antennas are based on the slot and coplanar structures. The first antenna is a compact broadband printed slot antenna integrating with filters for band notching. The filters including I-shaped and inverse L-shaped narrow slits and L-shaped conductor strip are integrated in the proposed antenna structure. The EMI mitigation at the frequency ranges of 2.7 to 3.2 GHz, 4.1 to 4.7 GHz, and over 6.1 GHz is obtained. The antenna can operates at frequency ranges of 2.26 to 2.68 GHz, 3.28 to 4.09 GHz, and 4.75 to 6.04 GHz. The nearly omni-directional and likely bi-directional radiation patterns are obtained in xz and yz planes, respectively. The average gains of all bands are given to be 1.67 dB, 2.75 dB, and 5.5 dB, respectively. The second one is a compact quad-band antenna using step-impedance slot with spiral stub technique. The interdigital capacitive coplanar waveguide feed is also employed, resulting in size reduction because of its slow-wave effect. Moreover, with this technique, the second harmonic frequency can be controlled as desired, while the third and fourth harmonics are caused by the step-impedance slot and spiral stub. The antenna has a compact size and can response for the frequency of 1.8 GHz, 2.45 GHz, 3.7 GHz and 5.2 GHz. The antenna has omni-directional patterns at all frequencies and the gains are 2.01 dB, 2.12 dB, 2.03 dB and 2.06 dB, respectively. Also, some other compact multiband antennas will be presented. All of these antennas are suitable to apply for various wireless applications including LTE, WIFI and WiMAX.

articleTitle: Invited talk 8: Measurement of the 664 GHz feed horn for the ICI instrument of the MetOp SG satellite
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the results of the antenna pattern measurements conducted on the Ice Cloud Imager 664 GHz feed horn at the ESTEC Sub-mmwave Scanner (SmS) in support to the ICI instrument of the MetOp-SG program. Very good agreement between simulations and measurements was obtained, both in the co- and cross-polar component. The measured peak directivity was 26.28 dBi ± 0.13 dB while the simulated one was 26.35 dB.

articleTitle: Experimental study of antenna selection methods in distributed uplink MU-MIMO
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Uplink MU-MIMO techniques achieve the high frequency efficiency. However, it is known that the frequency efficiency depends on the arrangement of antennas of the access point. Moreover, we have proposed the distributed antenna system (DAS) which selects the high density arranged antennas according to user distribution and shown its effectiveness using narrow band signals in an actual indoor environment. For the actual implementation, this paper proposes an antenna selection methods that selects the antenna in a limited area and selects the antenna in a non-limited area. We compare the basic characteristics of the DAS when applied the uplink MU-MIMO by broadband OFDM signals in an indoor environment for each selection method, and demonstrate the effectiveness of DAS with the proposed antenna selection methods.

articleTitle: Short dipole antenna array for on-ship NVIS application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work aims at reporting certain short dipole antenna array configurations which are developed and optimized for better utilization of Near Vertical Incidence Skywave (NVIS) application on ships.

articleTitle: Plenary talk 1: Ultra-wideband arrays with low cost beamforming back-ends
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Future communication links will require higher data rates, multiple beams, and higher transmit/receive gains, in addition to smaller weight, cost, and power. With the growing interest for reduced size platforms and the requirement for ultra-wideband (UWB) performance to address multifunctionality, there is a strong need for UWB apertures to enable increased spectral efficiency, multifunctionality and security, there is a strong need for small UWB apertures, particularly at millimeter wave frequencies. Such apertures enable increased spectral efficiency, spatial multiplexing, concurrent beams at different frequencies. Furthermore, UWB arrays offer high data rates and allow for secure communication using long codes that spread across the bandwidth. An added feature will be the capability for simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) applications.

articleTitle: Small-sized metamaterial feeding system combined polarization-reconfigurable antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a palm-sized metamaterial antenna system having reconfigurable polarization as well as dual-band characteristics. Basically, three antennas are laid by 45 degrees in order and excited by a compact metamaterial equal-ratio and equal-phase power-splitter, and the radiated fields of the antennas are mixed to turn the vector of the polarization to another. The legitimacy of the proposed method is examined by observing the in-phase outputs from the odd-numbered power-dividing device for both 900 MHz and 2.4 GHz, and checking the changeable polarization with the antenna gain over 2 dBi for all the polarizations.

articleTitle: Experimental validation for millimeter-wave channel measurement in reverberation chamber
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An experimental validation for millimeter-wave (mm-wave) channel measurement is presented in a reverberation chamber (RC) at 28 GHz band. A 28 GHz channel sounder and a vector network analyzer were used to measure complex channel transfer functions at the specific position of the rotating mode-stirrer in the RC. To demonstrate the experimental validation according to different antenna directions and polarizations, we have compared cumulative distribution functions for each case with Rayleigh distribution.

articleTitle: The A-DGTD method for a defect dielectric slab
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To deal with randomness and uncertainty problems, an adaptive discontinuous Galerkin time domain (A-DGTD) method is proposed to quantify the influence of defect factors. In order to prove the efficiency of the method, the standard statistical analysis is performed to calculate the mean of reflection coefficients caused by random/uncertain physical parameters on a dielectric slab.

articleTitle: A rectangular patch rectifying antenna array for wireless power transmission applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a suspended-rectangular patch rectifying antenna (rectenna) array for 2.45 GHz wireless power transmission is presented. The proposed rectenna, which consists of an antenna array and a rectifying circuit, is designed to convert the RF signal into DC power. The antenna structure is designed by using a rectangular patch which radiates unidirectional pattern. The air substrate of the antenna is used to achieve high gain. The rectifying circuit is designed based on voltage diode with stub matching circuit. The dimension of the proposed antenna is square of 190 mm. The measured gain of this antenna is 14 dBi. At the distance of 1 m, the proposed rectifying circuit achieves the output voltage of 1.5 V and output current of 0.15 mA with a 1 MΩ resistor load and a transmitter power of 34.6 dBm EIRP.

articleTitle: Exponential horn antenna excited by circular ring for bridging outdoor wireless LAN applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a circular ring is used to excite exponential horn antenna presented for bridging outdoor wireless LAN applications. The advantage of this structure does not require a waveguide feeding system. The purpose of this antenna design is to achieve unidirectional antenna which is operated at the center frequency of 2.45 GHz (2.40 GHz to 2.484 GHz). The characteristics of the proposed antenna such as |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|, radiation pattern and gain are also demonstrated. The results show that the antenna have given a high gain of 14.6 dBi and |S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup>| less than -30 dB at the center frequency. The proposed antenna is very useful for bridging outdoor WLAN systems.

articleTitle: A reconfigurable notch band UWB monopole antenna based on the split-ring resonators
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel ultrawideband (UWB) antenna fed by coplanar waveguide (CPW) with reconfigurable band notch frequency is described in this letter. The proposed antenna consists of a semi-circular single monopole providing broad bandwidth and two pairs of spilt-ring resonators (SRRs), where switches are placed in order to realize a tunable rejection frequency band. Also, contributed by these switches, a single/dual notch band conversion is realized. The notch band of proposed antenna covers WLAN, C-band and X-band satellite communication system frequency.

articleTitle: Plenary talk 3: Guidance and radiation of metasurface waves
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Metasurfaces constitute a class of thin metamaterials, which can be used from microwave to optical frequencies to create new electromagnetic engineering devices. They are obtained by a dense periodic texture of small elements printed on a grounded slab. Changing the dimension of the elements, being the sub-wavelength 2D-periodicity equal, gives the visual effect of a pixelated image and the electromagnetic effect of a modulation of the equivalent local reactance. The modulated metasurface reactance (MMR) so obtained is able to transform surface or guided waves into different wavefield configurations with required properties. The MMR allows a local modification of the dispersion equation and, at constant operating frequency, of the local wavevector. Therefore, a metasurface modulation permits addressing the propagation path of a surface wave, according with a generalized Fermat principle, as happen in ray-field propagation in inhomogeneous solid medium. This may serve for designing lenses or point-source driven beam-forming networks. When the MMR exhibits a periodic modulation along the SW wavevector, the wave propagation is accompanied by leakage; i.e., a surface wave is transformed into a leaky-wave, and the structure itself becomes an extremely flat antenna. In every case, introducing asymmetry in the pixel allows for a polarization control.

articleTitle: Effect of configuration of MIMO base station antenna on cannel capacity in street cell environment
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper clarifies the effects of configuration of a MIMO base station antenna on the channel capacity in line-of-sight street cell environment. It is shown that the optimum beam width in the horizontal plane depends on the road width and the distance from the base station. Moreover, it is also shown that the channel capacity decrease as the service area becomes wider.

articleTitle: Design of ultra-broadband bidirectional ring antenna with superellipse slot using MoM-RWG
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a very simple bidirectional ultra-broadband antenna, which comprises a cylindrical ring, a disc surface probe, and a superellipse slot. The proposed antenna covers many world-famous frequency bands: GSM, UMTS, LTE, WLAN, WiMAX and UWB. In the design, numerical simulations are performed using the method of moments (MoM) with RWG basis function. The ultra-broad bandwidth is approximately 9.2 GHz (1.71-10.91 GHz). The radiation patterns are bidirectional with feasible peak gains for the entire band. The antenna has the advantages of very simple structure for manufacture and ultra-broadband for bidirectional applications, which is a suitable candidate for long and narrow communication sites.

articleTitle: Simple impedance tuning technique for resistive antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A simple tuning technique is proposed to regulate the input impedance of resistive antennas over ultra-wide bandwidth. The proposed tuning technique involves adding extra copper pattern near the antenna drive point. It was shown to affect the input impedances of a resistive dipole and a 12-arm resistive cross dipole over ultra-wide bandwidth. The technique was applied to the 12-arm resistive cross dipole to improve the voltage standing wave ratio performance and shown that the proposed technique may be useful in tuning the resistive antennas.

articleTitle: Characteristics of a dual-broadband antenna with crossed elliptical probes and L-shaped slits
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Characteristics of a dual broadband antenna are investigated. The antenna consists of crossed elliptical probes, L-shaped slits, and split circular ground-planes. The proposed antenna covers various widely-employed frequency standards: IEEE 802.11b/g/n, IEEE 802.16, GSM, UMTS and LTE. The design and investigation are based on numerical simulations. The dual broad-bandwidths are 1.46 GHz (1.69-3.15 GHz) and 1.69 GHz (4.93-6.62 GHz), which simultaneously cover the above-mentioned frequency standards. The radiation patterns are of conical-beam type with peak gains of 3.1 and 5.1 dBi at 2.45 and 5.5 GHz, respectively. It has the advantage of main-beam directions pointing to nearly the same tilt angle for both main operating bands, which can be very useful for ceiling-mounted installations and simultaneous dual-band operations.

articleTitle: Design of frequency selective surface reflector using interdigital slot and application for LTE
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a new frequency selective surface (FSS) using interdigital slot structure. By using the interdigital slot unit cell, the size can be reduced from A/2 of conventional one to A/8. Moreover, the proposed interdigital slot FSS can be applied with a dipole antenna to resonate at 1.8 GHz, resulting in a high gain of 8.43 dB. The radiation pattern is directional and bandwidth is about 180 MHz. The proposed FSS structure can be applied with any radiator used for LTE system.

articleTitle: A blind signal separation using eigenvector synthesis
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a blind signal separation method for two incoming waves using eigenvector synthesis is proposed. The array weights to separate each waves are made from two eigenvectors. Numerical results show that the proposed method could improve the signal separation characteristics.

articleTitle: Spatial electric field distribution near the base station antenna using ray tracing
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We evaluate electric field distribution radiated from a base station antenna operating at 2.65 GHz, installed on a building. The surrounding environment is numerically modeled. The modeling changes a problem of realistic multipath human exposure assessment into a quantification analysis of electric field intensity. Multipath propagation of the field reflected by the urban environment is considered with the help of the ray tracing. The result of the ray tracing is compared to that of the other algorithm to show that the ray tracing has an advantage in urban exposure scenario.

Index Terms: Spatial Distribution Of The Electric Field

articleTitle: 3.5 THz dual feedhorn quantum cascade laser a step towards achievng a frequency stable supra-THz heterodyne local oscillator
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We present the first antenna power measurements from a double metal terahertz-frequency quantum cascade laser (THz QCL) mounted within a waveguide cavity and incorporating dual diagonal feedhorns that enable directional output coupling of THz radiation from both laser facets. The feedhorn antenna patterns have been measured simultaneously at a frequency of 3.5 THz and with the QCL operating at an ambient temperature of 60 K in continuous wave mode. Comparison with a feedhorn theoretical model shows good pattern correlation and implies that the QCL signal is likely propagating within the waveguide in a fundamental mode.

articleTitle: Design of small CRPA arrays with circular loop antennas for frequency-insensitive properties
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a small CRPA array with frequency-insensitive properties. The array consists of seven elements, and each element is composed of upper and lower circular loops that are designed to resonate at 1.575 GHz and 1.227 GHz, respectively. The lower loop is fed by the hybrid chip coupler, and the upper loop is electromagnetically coupled for a frequency-insensitive feeding mechanism. Due to the frequency-insensitive behavior, the bore-sight gain of each array element is maintained to be greater than -5 dBic from 1.21 GHz to 1.74 GHz, and this bandwidth can be further extended by adjusting the width of the upper circular loop, which varies the ratio of electric and magnetic coupling strengths in the proposed feeding mechanism.

articleTitle: Characteristic discussion of discrete-time uniform geometrical theory of diffraction for PEC wedge diffraction problems
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the establishment of time domain (TD) uniform geometrical theory of diffraction (UTD) based on the discrete-time electromagnetics (DT-EM) to treat the diffraction problem of PEC curved wedges. The focus is placed on the comparison of parametrical characteristics of DT-UTD when different types of TD basis functions are employed to build up the matrix equations in DT-EM. In this examination, the characteristics of both local and global TD basis functions will be discussed to show their truncation errors and convergence along wave propagation. Numerical tips will be also discussed to provide a promising computation.

Author Keywords: Time domain uniform geometrical theory of diffraction
Wedge diffraction and Basis function expansion

articleTitle: A W-band directional radiation antenna loading dielectric sheet based on SIW technology
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to improve the gain of the array antenna element in the W-band and reduce its horizontal dimension, The directional radiation antenna loading dielectric sheet based on SIW technology is proposed. The antenna uses a conventional micro strip line to feed the gradient open micro strip line. Then the gradient open micros trip line feeds the SIW. Finally, the dielectric sheet loaded in SIW will radiate the W-band electromagnetic wave. After modeling and simulating in CST Microwave Studio<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>, the antenna model has a reflection coefficient which is less than -10 dB over range of entire 86.04-110 GHz frequency. And the gain at the typical frequency of 94 GHz reaches 16.1 dB, the side lobe level is below -13.7 dB. The horizontal dimension of the antenna is calculated to be 0.658 time of wavelength according to the electrical size corresponding to 94 GHz. The designed antenna has the characteristics of small horizontal dimension, high gain and lower side lobe, and can be applied to the antenna array of passive millimeter wave imaging system.

articleTitle: Removing phase outliers in POA based landslide monitoring using cumulative residues
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of removing outliers from phase measurements in phase of arrival (POA) based localization, applied for the landslide monitoring. Our approach adopts so called cumulative residues and recursively removing outliers. The simulation results show that the proposed method has successfully removed outliers.

articleTitle: Workshop 2: Characteristic mode and characteristic basis analyses of real world antenna design problems
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The Characteristic Mode theory of antenna analysis and design has received the attention of many researchers in recent years, because it provides a brand new way of looking at the problem of placing antennas on a given platform to achieve a desired radiation pattern; to reduce coupling between antennas in a MIMO design; to achieve a wideband performance compared to that of the original antenna, etc. In this presentation, we will begin by reviewing the fundamentals of the Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA) to bring the audience up-to-date with the fundamentals of CMA as well as with its latest developments. Next, we will discuss a number of real-world problems arising in practical antenna applications, and identify some challenging issues that have been encountered by the antenna designers in the process of applying the CMA to these problems. These include, among others, excitation of the Characteristic modes on complex platforms; antenna placement on these platforms to achieve a desired radiation pattern, specified over a limited angular range; determining excitation coefficients of antennas to achieve interference suppression of unwanted signals.

articleTitle: Performance improvement of waveguide to coaxial adapter by using split ring resonator and wire medium structure
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the performance improvement of rectangular waveguide to coaxial adapter of horn antenna for radar system at L-band frequency by using metamaterial structure based on a wire medium. The main point is to utilize a split ring resonator (SRR) as bandpass filter and the wire medium metamaterial placed on the waveguide's aperture for gain increment. This idea has been insisted by CST simulation software. We found that this proposed SRR can improve the desired resonant frequency at 1.3 GHz and provided the narrower bandwidth, whereas, the wire medium structure can increase the gain around 3dB, approximately.

articleTitle: 2D antenna array design with WINNER-based antenna simulator
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For the future fifth generation (5G) communication systems, one of the promising techniques is the massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO), which applies hundreds of antenna elements for antenna design. However, how to evaluate a good structure of two-dimensional (2D) antenna array for a specific channel environment in designing massive MIMO systems is still under research. In this paper, we first propose a WINNER-based antenna simulator, which can provide the system performance, such as system capacity, under different channel environments and antenna configurations. With the proposed simulator, the connection between the system performance and antenna design can be built. Furthermore, the simulation results for different 2D antenna array analysis in designing Massive MIMO systems are also shown and then we will finally conclude our observations for massive MIMO antenna design.

articleTitle: A substrate integrated magneto-electric dipole antenna and its 3D MIMO system with metasurface for 5G/WiMAX/WLAN/X-band applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A substrate integrated magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna with metasurface is proposed for the 5G/WiMAX/WLAN/X-Band MIMO applications. In order to provide the low profile characteristic, the radiated electric dipoles and the shorted wall are integrated in the multi-layer substrates at different altitudes. Unlike the conventional metasurface antenna, by introducing the ME dipole structure with modified zigzagged radiated dipole, the wideband and unidirectional features can be achieved. As a result of the 3D hexagonal structure, the good ECC performance can be obtained by the MIMO antenna system. Also, a 360° full unidirectional coverage in the operating frequency bands can be acquired.

articleTitle: Array antenna composed of microstrip line fed inverted L antenna printed on dielectric substrate
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The two elements array antenna composed of inverted L antennas printed on the two-layer dielectric substrate and excited by the microstrip line through the slot is proposed and numerically analyzed. The size of the antenna is 0.24 λ by 1.25 λ by 0.0352 λ. The S 11 less than -10 dB is satisfied from 23.96 GHz to 24.06 GHz, and gain is 3.63 dB at frequency of 24 GHz. In the numerical analysis, the electromagnetic simulator WIPL-D based on the Method of Moments is used.

articleTitle: A compact UHF cross dipole antenna with reconfigurable radiation patterns using passive parasitic elements
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact UHF cross dipole antenna with reconfigurable radiation pattern is presented. The proposed antenna achieves beam-forming using a modified Yagi antenna concept and the passive parasitic elements. The measured impedance bandwidth of the cross dipole antenna is 884-915 MHz. It is possible to use reflector and director depending on the ON, OFF state of the pin diode. The measured antenna peak gain is 3.3 dBi at 898 MHz.

articleTitle: Effect of antenna frequency bands on the resolution of GPR images
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
