abstract: This paper presents an investigation of the effect of the antenna frequency band on the ground penetrating radar (GPR) image resolution. The investigation is achieved through simulations. In the simulations, two Scutcheon antennas are modeled as the receiving and transmitting antennas. A cross-shaped object is buried under the ground constructed with the dielectric material. The Gaussian pulses with different frequency bands is transmitted and propagated to the buried object. The EM wave scattered from the object is collected to form the GPR image. The simulation results obtained from different frequency band show that the resolution of the GPR image obtained from the wider frequency band is better than that of the GPR image obtained from narrower one.

articleTitle: A miniaturized independently tuning dual-band multi-mode antenna using the postwall slotline
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A miniaturized independently tuning dual-band multi-mode antenna using postwall slotline (PWS) is proposed and simulated in this work. The antenna consists a stepped impedance slot and a patch on the other side of the substrate, and the patch is attached at the edge of the slot by shorting pins. The stepped impedance slot based on the postwall slotline is actually a dual-mode slotline antenna working at 2.81 GHz-3.19 GHz, as a low frequency operating band, and the patch works at a higher frequency band of 4.43 GHz-4.56 GHz. The use of stepped impedance slot miniaturizes the size and widens bandwidth of the antenna. Both the slot and the patch are fed by a microstrip line, and their operating band can be controlled independently, which is a good merit for applications of wireless communication.

articleTitle: Numerical studies of mixed compact stencils for two-dimensional Helmholtz equation with circular interfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We present method of connected local fields to solve Helmholtz equation for high index-contrast dielectric structures with circular interfaces. Numerical examples of computing two-dimensional Green's functions for silica rods in free space are discussed. Our method is based on the piece-wise linear approximation of the dielectric curved interface combined with a wide-angle transparent boundary condition that also uses compact stencils. We report here that compared with exact Green's functions our numerical errors are well under one percent for both TE and TM polarization at a low sampling density of ten points per wavelength.

articleTitle: Compact asymmetrical patch dipole antenna for indoor digital terrestrial television reception
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the compact asymmetrical patch dipole antenna for digital terrestrial television reception in indoor environment. It can be operated in the frequency of 430-980 MHz. The antenna structure is a patch designed on a rectangular printed circuit board (PCB). The patch is cut as asymmetrical planar dipole as the radiating element on the FR4 substrate that is appropriated for indoor application. The proposed antenna is designed based on the 75 Ohm standard, and it is simulated using CST microwave studio. From the simulated and measured results, it is found that the proposed antenna has |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| less than -10 dB over the frequency of 430-980 MHz and omni-directional radiation pattern with a gain of 2 dBi. It can be efficiently used in digital terrestrial television.

articleTitle: Design method of meta-surface for broadband reflected wave reduction
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes a design method of a metasurface that consists of two types FSS (Frequency Selective Surface) and the ground plane to realize broadband reflected wave reduction. The ideal filtering characteristics of one FSS is clarified when the other FSS is a patch type FSS. A loop and patch type FSS is proposed to realize the ideal filtering characteristics. Then, a meta-surface with reflected wave reduction function is constructed with the patch type FSS and the proposed FSS. As a result, 48.9 % of a relative bandwidth within a reflection amplitude -10 dB or less is obtained by the proposed meta-surface.

articleTitle: A wearable EEG-based control network and emergency medical assistance system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presented the design of a wearable EEG-based control network and emergency medical assistance system which works and is now under test by volunteers. The system can detect the user's blink control signal, heart rates and brain signal, etc. A new scheme to control the device for disabilities was proposed in the paper. A DSP was used to calculate and process these data which can also send messages of the patients to the control center and make emergency calls to the nearest hospital for the patients, especially for patients which suffered from epilepsy and disabilities. The proposed system was proved to be practical and helpful in assisting the injured, elderly and disabled groups.

articleTitle: A stable gain printed log-periodic dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, A novel stable gain printed log-periodic dipole antenna (PLPDA) with two slotted dielectric substrates, based on the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technologies is proposed. This antenna consists of a traditional PLPDA fed by SIW, which reduces dielectric loss and conductor loss and two pieces of Rodgers5880 substrates with periodic slots, two pieces of Rodgers5880 substrates are symmetrically loaded on PLPDA above and under respectively. The effects of slotted dielectric substrates were simulated. Simulated results show that antenna achieves a more stable gain than the traditional antenna over the frequency of 24.2-34.1GHz with reflection coefficient less than -10dB.

articleTitle: Radio over fiber network technologies for linear cell systems in millimeter-wave bands
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Millimeter-wave signal feeding technique to remote radio transceivers via an optical fiber network is discussed particularly in linear cell configurations using radio over fiber technologies. Double-sideband and single-sideband modulation schemes with suitable modulation frequency are demonstrated under 10-km-class optical fiber network configuration.

articleTitle: Concept for low cost CNC machined gain reference antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Gain standards for accurate antenna measurements are expensive due to their extensive calibration procedure. This paper presents a concept for low cost antennas that comprise of sheets of FR-4 which are accurately manufactured using modern CNC technology. This accuracy in turn will render the calibration procedures unnecessary. The impact of tolerances is studied to determine whether the concept is eligible for further investigation.

articleTitle: Study of integrated THz antenna geometries using metasurface for imaging applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Terahertz technology has grown much interest especially in the imaging field. This development, compliant with the low-cost sub-micron CMOS process for focal plan array configuration, addresses some issues about the performances of antennas on a silicon substrate and on a reduced metal stack. Here, two antenna geometries are studied on different electromagnetic (EM) environments and coupling characteristics with the rectifying MOSFET detector. By using electromagnetic band gap (EBG) surface with co-design between the MOSFET and the antennas, S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> of -18.2 dB with 5.8-dBi gain and a radiated front-to-back ratio of 10.1 dB are achieved around 290 GHz.

articleTitle: On-body transmission for dual-band antenna incorporated with dual-band AMC waveguide jacket
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the different antenna orientation is investigated for on-body transmission by introducing the Dual-band Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) waveguide jacket. The transmission for on-body is measured using two flexible dual-band antennas attach to the Dual-band AMC waveguide jacket. The real measurement has been conducted with a man with the height of 180cm and 75kg weight. The measurement is conducted in small space area by using portable network analyzer. It is found that the transmission of the antenna is depends on the antenna orientation and the waveguide jacket acts like a path for the antenna to propagate between each node. The result shows that the 10 dB improvement when the antenna is in the same plane.

articleTitle: Bandwidth enlargement of λ/4 monopole above ground plane with metallic holes structure
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the bandwidth enlargement method of the conventional λ/4 monopole antenna on finite ground plane is investigated for utilization in IFF (Identification friend or foe) of the secondary radar the operating frequency 1.03-1.09 GHz. For the initial study, we have proposed the structure of the resonant holes on the surface of a sector of metallic cylinders covering such the monopole that placed on the circular ground plane with λ/2 of radius. The simulation results such as reflection coefficients (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>), gains, and radiation patterns of four different structures are analyzed by using CST microwave studio software. We found that its bandwidth could be enlarged to the maximum value around 86.81% at S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>= -10 dB when the opposite side of the proposed structure is free-space. However, the gain at the desired bandwidth is not much increased while the higher frequencies can provide the higher gain. Furthermore, it is found that the radiation patterns of four cases still be similar even though the monopole is covered with the different structure.

articleTitle: An ultra-wideband omnidirectional radiation dipole antenna with Klopfenstein curve boundary
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of the stability of the UWB omnidirectional radiation antenna, a three-dimensional bipolar antenna is proposed, which is composed of metal frame with Klopfenstein curve boundary. The antenna is fed with a 50 Ω coaxial line and the reflection coefficient |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <;-10 dB is achieved in the frequency range of 0.45-23.8 GHz. In addition, the H-plane pattern at 22 GHz in the high frequency band remains omnidirectional. The simulation data of the antenna is obtained by CST Microwave Studio<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> software simulation. The polarization direction of the proposed antenna is only 0.67 times the minimum operating frequency and it has the characteristics of miniaturization and stability of the pattern.

articleTitle: The ring antenna with circular probe feeding for MIMO systems
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the ring antenna with circular probe feeding for MIMO systems. The ring antenna structure was adjusted by using the circular probe feedings on the ground plane to increase bandwidth and arrangement the elements of array antenna in four cases. The structural tuning technique was used Computer Simulation Technology (CST) program to analyze the antenna characteristics such as S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, the envelope correlation coefficient and radiation patterns. The measurement applying at result reveals that the orthogonal position is the best case for applying at the frequency ranges of 1–4 GHz. The mutual coupling is less than −20dB and the average gain is 4.19 dBi.

articleTitle: A compact folded crossed omnidirectional ultra wideband antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: With compact folded method, a kind of folded crossed dipole ultra wideband antenna is proposed with omnidirectional radiation characteristics on the horizontal direction in this paper. The antenna is comprised of orthogonal crossed semicircular metal discs with twice 90° folded on both ends. Horizontal size is reduced obviously compared with original crossed semicircular disc antenna. This antenna operates from 3.1GHz to 17.2GHz with S11<;-10 dB, and the maximum gain is 3.7dB. The out of roundness for radiation patterns is less than 0.2 dB. The group delay is around ± 0.5ns in whole operating frequency ranges.

articleTitle: Printed ku-band phased array designs for CubeSats
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The element design of two very low profile dual-polarized Ku-band phased arrays for use on nanosatellites are presented in this paper. Both exhibit conical scan greater than 65 degrees over a bandwidth exceeding 17 per cent with worst-case active VSWR better than 3:1 and axial ratio less than 4 dB. These properties make such arrays eminently suited on nanosatellites designed for commercial services requiring global coverage.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized circular ring antenna with short pin
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of dual-polarized circular ring antenna with short pin to ground plane. The antenna is proposed to use in the Multiple-Input Multiple-Output communication systems. The parameters of the antenna that are ring radius (a), ring width (d), probe length (l), short pin length (p), and ground plane size (G) were analyzed at the operating frequency of 2.2 GHz. The results showed the |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| was lower than -11 dB with the |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| of -17 dB. The effective of the short pin that used for reducing the mutual coupling between two probes can be investigated.

articleTitle: User effect on the efficiency of 4-port mobile terminal antenna at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a planar 4-port antenna is designed to investigate the effect of user finger for mobile terminal application. The proposed array antenna covers a bandwidth of 2.5 GHz centered at 28 GHz. The effects of user's finger on the antenna are studied in four different positions on top of antenna elements, with six distances between antenna and user's finger. The losses due to the increased shadowing are studied in terms of radiation efficiency (RE) and matching efficiency (ME). Results indicated that there is no significant losses in terms of ME regardless of the antenna and finger variations, while a maximum loss of up to 75 % is observed for RE.

articleTitle: Radio astronomy network and geodesy for development project: The 40-m Thai national radio telescope
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Radio Astronomy Network and Geodesy for Development (RANGD) Project by National Astronomical Research Institute of Thailand (NARIT) has been approved for year 2017–2021 with human capacity building as the main objective. Among several skills-developing activities, 40-m and 13-m radio telescopes are to be constructed as future national facilities. Missions of RANGD project include research development in radio astronomy, Earth sciences and advanced engineering. Current status and project timeline will be reported.

articleTitle: Enhancement of bandwidth for a TL resonator based CRLH leaky wave antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a transmission line (TL) resonator based composite right/left-handed (CRLH) leaky-wave antenna (LWA) is investigated. In order to enhance input impedance bandwidth, bandpass filter synthesis technique is utilized to design matching sections. An example LWA with a fractional bandwidth of 0.4 is designed and fabricated, and the measured results agree well with numerical results.

articleTitle: A collective UTD ray solution for the radiation from conformal linear antenna arrays on a large cylinder
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A uniform geometrical theory of diffraction (UTD) ray solution has been developed for describing the radiation fields produced by a linear antenna array which is conformal to a cylindrical conducting structure. The fields are described collectively in terms of just a few rays which are launched from a specific critical point in the interior and from the two end points of the linear array. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the validity and efficiency of the present collective UTD ray solution.

articleTitle: DOA estimation of desired signals using radio holography and signal cyclostationarity
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The radio holography method performs the direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation of radio waves with a relatively simple array system because it uses a reference antenna. This paper proposes a new radio holography method in which cyclic correlations of digital-modulation signals are introduced for the DOA estimation of desired signals only. The DOA estimation accuracy of the method is evaluated by computer simulation and the effectiveness of the method is shown.

articleTitle: Antenna on silicon with bandwidth improvement
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper antenna on silicon is presented. This paper proposes design of micro strip antenna on silicon with improved bandwidth. Proposed antenna is for X-band frequency. To improve bandwidth, ground defect being created on silicon substrate. With this we are improve bandwidth by 4–8 times. Designed verified both in HFSS simulation tool and on VNA after fabricating device.

articleTitle: A low-profile metamaterial magneto-electric dipole antenna with band-notch characteristics for 5-G MIMO base-stations
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low profile magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna with wide H-plane and band-notch features is proposed for the fifth generation of mobile communication (5G) Multiple Input Multiple Output(MIMO) applications. The radiated electric dipoles are designed with two kinds of separated arc-shaped planes at different altitudes to provide the dual-band and wide H-plane characteristics. By employing the E-shaped metamaterials to set in the center of the magnetic dipole, the volume of the antenna can be reduced to approximately 46%. In addition, two U-shaped notches together with a rectangular notch are introduced to provide the band-notch feature to 2.4 GHz Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN). Further more, its MIMO system which consists of three elements can provide a 360<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> unidirectional coverage in the frequency bands from 2.4 GHz to 3.75 GHz.

articleTitle: Cuboid dielectric resonator antenna array placed on # slots for LTE femtocell base stations
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A Cuboid Dielectric Resonator Antenna fed by microstrip feed line is studied. The dielectric resonator of the antenna is made by a material with high dielectric constant ϵ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=30. The impedance matching of dielectric resonator can be improved by using a # slot in the ground. In additional, a two elements array is used to enhance the performance of the antenna. This proposed antenna is suitable for long-term evolution (LTE) band 7 and LTE band 38 femtocell base stations with impedance bandwidth more than 200 MHz.

articleTitle: A study of dual-fed dual-polarized crossed bowtie antennas for radio astronomy application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we study the dual-fed dual-polarized crossed bowtie antennas with different structure proposed for the radio telescope system in 300 MHz band. The performance of crossed bowtie antennas designed on the same surface (co-planar) and on different surface (stack-patch) are compared. The simulation of these antenna structures were carried out using CST Microwave Studio to determine the impedance bandwidth (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| and |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sub>| less than -10 dB), the antenna gain, the radiation pattern, and the antenna polarization in the frequency range 305-355 MHz. The simulation results confirmed that the proposed antennas are suitable for the radio telescopes system.

articleTitle: Multi layer planar Ka-band satellite receive antenna with integrated LNA
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The scientific payload GeReLEO-SMART will be launched on the German geostationary satellite “Heinrich-Hertz”. It should prove the technology readiness of a data receive antenna for low earth orbit (LEO) satellites and work as a data relay. The receiving antenna works in the Ka-Band and is composed of a four layer soft substrate PCB with integrated preselector band pass filter and low noise amplifier (LNA). The LNA is mounted in a cavity of the PCB stack and connected by bond wires. This paper gives an overview of the components, their design and expected performance.

articleTitle: Evaluation of field strength distribution by Modified Edge Representation (MER) in compact range communication with shadowing objects
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The features of compact-range communication system is introduced briefly. The system in presence of a shadowing object is simply modelled. Modified Edge Representation is applied to evaluate field strength of the system. In the end, bit error rate (BER) is roughly estimated under the multipath-free condition.

articleTitle: Invited talk 1: Computation of the far field from a nonuniformly spaced antenna elements using a least square method
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to describe a least square method to compute the far field from a nonuniformly spaced antenna array. This is because the far field pattern of an antenna array is the Fourier transform of the current distribution developed on the antenna structure, This is equivalent to computing the spectrum from a nonuniformly spaced data set using a least squares method. The merit of analyzing a nonuniformly spaced data set is that one need not satisfy the Nyquist sampling theorem in the strict sense. This is acceptable as long as the average sampling rate for the nonuniformly spaced data satisfies the Nyquist sampling theorem. A Fourier based least squares method can easily be extended to deal with nonuniformly spaced data, however the disadvantage of this procedure is that it is highly computational time intensive. Hence in this approach a Hilbert transform based methodology is described to significantly reduce the computation time without sacrificing accuracy. Hence, in methodology, this method is an extension to the Lomb periodogram technique which deals with the computation of the spectrum from a nonuniformly based data set. The problem with the Lomb periodogram method is that it cannot differentiate between the positive and the negative frequencies of the spectrum even though it has various other advantages. For example the effect of bias in the processed data can be reduced significantly in addition for a nonuniformly spaced data. Also because of a nonuniformly sampled data it is difficult to correctly estimate the amplitude of the far field or equivalently the spectrum hence a two-step methodology will be presented where at the first stage one solves for the spectral components and then applies a least squares solution procedure to get the best amplitude of the spectrum or equivalently the complex amplitudes for the far field. The Hilbert transform methodology is applied to reduce the computation time by a factor of one half in the computation of the complex spectrum as the real and imaginary parts of a causal function are indeed related by the Hilbert transform.

articleTitle: Second iteration of slotted fractal log periodic dipole antenna (LPDA)
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact log periodic antenna (LPDA) is presented in this paper. In this paper, a slotted second iteration of LPDA is demonstrated for size reduction that used for UHF digital TV band application. The proposed antenna operates from 0.5GHz to 1.5GHz for the reflection coefficient ≤ −10dB and maintain the gain of more than 5dBi. The antenna is designed on FR4 Epoxy dielectric substrate with the thickness of 1.6mm and relative permittivity of 4.6. The size of LPDA fractal Koch with slotted second iteration is successfully reduced by 26% as opposed to the size of the antenna in 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> iteration.

articleTitle: Dual band MIMO antenna composed of inverted L elements printed on dielectric substrate
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The dual band MIMO antenna composed of inverted L antenna is proposed and numerically analyzed. The design frequency is 2.4 GHz to 2.5 GHz, 5.15 GHz to 5.35 GHz. Inverted L antenna is formed by the coplanar waveguide. The parasitic planar rectangular loop is placed above the of inverted L antenna. When the size of conducting plane is 51 mm by 48 mm, the S11 less than -10 dB is satisfied from 2.4 GHz to 2.5 GHz, and 5.15 GHz to 5.35 GHz. The distance between two antennas is 35 mm. The S21 less than -20 dB and the correlation coefficient less than 0.002 are satisfied at these two frequency bands. In the numerical analysis, the electromagnetic simulator WIPL-D based on the Method of Moments is used.

articleTitle: Design of geometrical asymmetry in phase-shifting nonreciprocal CRLH metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we review how to design geometrical asymmetry for enhancement of phase-shifting nonreciprocity and for optimizing its dispersion in composite right/left handed transmission lines for antenna applications.

articleTitle: A study on the use of metasurfaces for magnetic resonance imaging of human body models
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A numerical study of a radio frequency transceiver coil incorporating a capacitive metasurface is investigated for 1.5T magnetic resonance imaging of the cervical spinal cord. Full field simulations are carried out using the head of a human body model where the magnetic flux density (B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup>) is compared to a standard transceiver coil. It is shown that an average improvement in B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> of 70% can be observed inside the cervical spinal cord.

articleTitle: A study on antenna arrangement optimization of massive MIMO
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to efficiently arrange a large number of antenna elements in limited space of base station by using mathematical optimization with channel response correlation between two antenna elements as an objective function. We place antenna elements in various sized areas by the method. The arrangement results are compared with planar equidistant arrangements. We found that the average 11.3% performance improves at 50% value of cumulative distribution function of channel capacity in a street cell environment with two users.

articleTitle: Influence of channel prediction using theoretical autocorrelation on MIMO capacity in line-of-sight environment
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this report, we investigate prediction accuracy of fading channels in line-of-sight (LOS) environment when using autoregressive (AR) model. We especially evaluate the accuracy of the predicted channel in LOS environment when applying the theoretical autocorrelation formula of the LOS environment to the AR model. The influence of the prediction methods on MIMO capacities is also investigated. The simulation results clarify that the channel prediction using the LOS formula is superior to that using the NLOS formula especially when predicting the future channel at the large time interval.

articleTitle: Study of dual-frequency absorbing materials based on frequency selective surfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to achieve a ultra-wideband operating characteristics. A low profile dual-band absorbing structure is proposed, the two-dimensional periodic array double ring printed on a dielectric substrate, and insert the chip resistors in four symmetrical positions on the circumference of the ring. The RCS of the two-dimensional array of finite element simulation, the influence of the various parameters of the structure of the electromagnetic wave absorption characteristics of the final results show that the new dual-band absorbing structure can be a metal reflector of RCS reduced. A 4×4 array is simulated, and the result indicates a excellent absorber characteristic to vertical incident electromagnetic wave. The relative bandwidth with return loss below -10dB at 2.4GHz and 5GHz are 10% and 12% respectively. The frequency selective surfaces can be used in aircraft stealth.

articleTitle: Invited talk 7: A reverse operation self-consistent evaluation approach for evaluating singular integrals in method of moments
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Discussed herein is a novel approach entitled reverse operation self-consistent evaluation (ROSE). Specifically, we applied ROSE for the treatment of weak-singular and hypersingular kernels in surface integral equations (SIEs) for the computation of electromagnetic (EM) scattering from perfect electrical conductors (PEC). In this paper, we restrict our discussion to the weak-singular and hypersingular kernels employing respectively div-conformal RWG basis functions and non-conformal piece-wise constant vector basis functions.

articleTitle: Miniaturization and broadbanding of an open terminated folded inverted-L antenna with slits
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We have proposed an open terminated folded inverted-L antenna (FILA) with slits. In order to miniaturize the FILA, several slits are employed on the substrate surface. Folded structure is used for broadbanding. Design of the FILA to achieve broadband characteristics is shown. Simulation and measurement are implemented, and comparison of the results are evaluated. Finally, we calculate the product of bandwidth and radiation efficiency (Bη product) and evaluate it of the FILA compared with the theoretical limitation.

articleTitle: Aperiodic isophoric slotted waveguide antenna for point-to-point communications at Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We report the intermediate results on a novel slotted waveguide antenna for point-to-point communications at Ka band. The antenna adopts an aperiodic layout with uniformly-excited elements capable of meeting the ETSI class II radiation pattern envelop in all planes with high aperture efficiency. A total of 16 regular waveguide subarrays with an aperiodic inter-column spacing along the E-plane are fed by a corporate feed network located underneath. The prototype was milled in three layers of aluminum and bonded by vacuum brazing. Measurements confirm a 15% impedance bandwidth. The simulated patterns satisfy the radiation pattern envelop and have a gain above 28.5 dBi over 29-31 GHz, corresponding to an efficiency better than 80%.

articleTitle: A study for radar absorbent material composed of dielectric materials considering frequency dependency
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Reducing the radar cross section (RCS) is important to suppress radio wave interference. Many radar absorbent material (RAM) have been investigated according to performance requirements. This paper presents the RCS reduction characteristics of RAM composed of dielectric materials for 3 GHz. The optimum values of dielectric substance condition to design flat layer RAM are investigated. Moreover, RCS reduction results obtained by considering frequency dependency also show that RCS reduction increases and the absorption range is wider by adding the RAM layer. This indicates that the proposed two flat layers RAM can be used at a broadband frequencies around 3 GHz.

articleTitle: Improvement of object position estimation accuracy using hyperbola and ellipse
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A position estimation technique using electromagnetic wave has been proposed for object detection in wireless power transmission. However, conventional position estimation method has a problem that position estimation accuracy varies with object position. This paper proposes a position estimation method using hyperbola obtained from time difference and ellipse obtained from path length. Due to the orthogonality between the hyperbola and the ellipse, it is enabled to accurate position estimation regardless of the object position. Moreover, effect of thermal noise at the receiver antennas and antenna spacing of the receiver on position estimation accuracy is shown.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation on NOMA and transmit BF with user selection by the number of beams
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: As a technique for improving the transmission rate within a limited frequency band, Multiuser MIMO (MU-MIMO), which realizes MIMO transmission with multiple user terminals, has been attracted much attention. However, it is not possible to communicate with the users that exceed the number of base station (BS) antennas in the MU-MIMO transmission. We have proposed a method by using non orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) and Zero Forcing (ZF) at the BS and Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) at user terminals (UTs). In this paper, we evaluate the performance when the number of beams with NOMA applied is increased up to four by computer simulation using actual propagation channel. Furthermore, we propose a scheduling algorithm for 6-user and 3-beam at the BS that reduce the performance degradation by interference among users and verify that the improvement on the bit error rate by the propose method.

articleTitle: Circuit-electromagnetic co-simulation in designing a negative impedance circuit at VHF band
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper compares simulation results of a negative impedance converter (NIC) obtained from a circuit-only and circuit-electromagnetic (EM) co-simulation to demonstrate the impact of parasitic effects. The NIC is designed to produce a negative capacitance by cross-coupling two field-effect-transistors. In the circuit-EM co-simulation, the bulk of the transistors and other components are exactly modelled to consider the parasitic effects. The simulations are performed with a 50 ohm termination and a VHF monopole antenna connected at the output port. The results show that the parasitic effects play a significant role in determining the operation frequency of NIC.

articleTitle: Size reduction of log-periodic dipole array antenna using folded planar helix elements
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the size of a log-periodic dipole array antenna is reduced using partially applied folded planar helix dipole elements. The proposed antenna shows almost no gain deterioration in the entire operating bandwidth even though its size is reduced by 39 %. Due to its reduced size and lightweight characteristics, it is expected that the proposed antenna could be effectively utilized in the mobile radio wave direction finding systems.

articleTitle: Emulating SCME power delay profile in reverberation chamber
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An experimental set-up and procedure for emulating realistic fading channels in a reverberation chamber is described in this contribution. Of particular interest is the generation of power delay profiles of urban-macro and -micro channels defined in the 3GPP Spatial-Channel-Model-Extended (SCME). The input signal to the chamber is generated by convolving a rectangular pulse with delay taps using a Matlab driven signal generator. Afterwards, a clustered power delay profile is produced by stirring effects in the reverberation chamber and verified using a high speed oscilloscope. The results show the proposed test set-up can be used to generate realistic fading channels for antenna or mobile device testing in a simple and inexpensive manner.

articleTitle: Uplink BER measurement of MIMO full-duplex system using end-fire arranged arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The eigen-beamforming with the end-fire arrangement has been proposed as an interference suppression method suitable for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) full-duplex. We clarify the effectiveness of this scheme by experimentally evaluating the bit-error-rate (BER) performance of the uplink desired signal from the mobile terminal while the self-interference in the base station is suppressed. The results showed that the proposed method suppressed interference power by 23.8 dB and achieved BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> even though the desired signal power was 15 dB lower than that of the scenario without the self-interference suppression.

articleTitle: A Ka-band phased array of antennas with parallel-plate parabolic reflector feeding network for high energy-efficient radiation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The paper presents a Ka-band phased array of antennas with a beamforming network (BFN) realized by using parallel-plate parabolic reflector cavity. The BFN is realized in the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) formed cavity with a point-excitation to form a space-fed configuration. In addition, the corrugation structure on sidewalls of the two input reflecting surfaces is constructed to disturb the cavity resonance and mitigate multi-path interferences as the waveguide propagation to create the required phases for antenna excitations. The proposed BFN is used to excite an 8 × 10 antenna array at top layer of the standard PCB to demonstrate the characteristics of low loss and high directivity. The measured results show the 20.8 dB of gain and 23.45 dB of directivity at 38 GHz.

articleTitle: Half space radiation antenna for UWB ranging and localization application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Integrating the concept of Antipodal Vivaldi antenna (AVA) and planar disc-shaped dipole, a half space radiation UWB antenna is proposed in this letter. The antenna adopted approximately 1/4 of the disc-shaped dipole as its radiator, fed by the AVA's exponential slot structure. The proposed antenna has an ultra-wide bandwidth and nearly half space radiation pattern. This character makes it applicable to UWB ranging and localization field. The antenna analysis and design was carried out by CST software. The prototype was fabricated and experimentally measured. The simulation and measurement result confirms the feasibility of the design.

articleTitle: Plenary talk 2: Real challenge of mobile networks toward 5G: An expectation for antenna & propagation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Mobile communication service is widely penetrating to all the society as the key infrastructure. It is spreading beyond the conventional telephone service. Wide variety of social services including e-commerce, e-bank, navigation, location, healthcare, and education are offered on the network. It's not too much to say that people can never part with a smartphone as the most frequently use interface between a human and society.

articleTitle: Step shape antenna for MIMO applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper a novel planar antenna is proposed for 5.2GHz band application. The area of designed antenna has been reduced by 52% in comparison to a conventional rectangular microstrip patch antenna. The antenna has three vertical stripes and one horizontal stripe. The length and width of these stripes are varied to tune the antenna for a certain operating frequency. The antenna is fed by using a 50 ohm microstrip line connected at the center of horizontal stripe. The fabricated antenna has return loss of 22dB at 5.27GHz and impedance bandwidth of 120MHz. A parametric study has been carried out to analyze and to find the design sensitive parameters.

articleTitle: Design of a partial-corporate-feed circuit of a waveguide reflection-canceling slot low-sidelobe array antenna in the 60GHz band
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A partial-corporate-feed waveguide reflection-canceling 16×28-slot array antenna is designed for 60 GHz band in order to suppress the sidelobe level by excitation of Taylor distribution. The simulation by HFSS gives low sidelobes by redesign of the feed waveguide. The measurement result is improved by eliminating isolated etching pattern of the feeding layer.

articleTitle: Modeling small antennas on large convex metallic surfaces with a very thin uniform material coating
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A Uniform Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (UTD) is developed for modeling realistic small antennas placed on large, smooth, convex metallic surfaces with a uniform material coating which is extremely thin (with respect to the convex surface radii of curvatures). The very thin uniform material coating on a convex metallic surface is approximated here by a linear surface impedance boundary condition for simplifying the analysis. An asymptotic matching procedure is performed in the deep lit region of the antenna in order to model an actual small antenna by a simple equivalent UTD based source, which can then be combined with an appropriate UTD dyadic Green's function for the convex impedance surface for predicting its radiation pattern. Numerical results will be presented to illustrate the utility of the present approach.

articleTitle: Time saving EM-simulation method by using passive frame of DCO
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a simulation method for the DCO. EM simulations are essential and inevitable for modern LC oscillator design. Although EM-simulators provide high accuracy, the EM-simulation time is very long when metal-oxide-metal (MoM) capacitors are present. The proposed frame-based EM-simulation can significantly reduce the EM-simulation time even in the presence of MoM capacitors without influencing the accuracy. To verify the proposed method, a DCO was fabricated using a 55-nm CMOS process. Measurements of the DCO are in good agreement with the frame-based post-layout simulation results.

articleTitle: Characteristic examination of near-field EM backscattering from ground vehicles by phased array antennas at mmW frequencies
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates the electromagnetic backscattering characteristics of moving vehicles when they are illuminated by the radiation of radar antennas. In particular, the vehicles are located close to the antennas as appeared in the anti-collision warning system at millimeter wave (mmW) frequencies. The backscattering fields are processed through the procedure of a realistic radar system to exhibit the signal characteristics of realistic radar system. Numerical examples are presented to discuss the methodology and characteristics in detection justification.

articleTitle: Evaluation of human body shadowimg loss in an indoor environment
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the human body shadowing loss characteristics by finding the received signal using the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method and the actual measurement in three-dimensional indoor environments. We show the human body shadowing loss when a single human body moves between transmitting and receiving antennas. Furthermore, we show the human body shadowing loss characteristics when multiple human walk and consider the relationship between the first Fresnel zone and the human body shadowing loss.

articleTitle: Fast idenfitication of small inhomogeneities without diagonal elements of MSR matrix
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, we investigate the mathematical structures of imaging function used in subspace migration for obtaining images of small dielectric inhomogeneities when the diagonal elements of multi static response (MSR) matrix cannot be obtained. Based on the asymptotic formula in the presence of inhomogeneities and the structure of the singular vectors linked to the nonzero singular values of the MSR matrix, we establish a relation between the imaging function and Bessel function of order zero of the first kind for full-view inverse scattering problem. Experimental results of numerical simulations with noisy data are presented to validate our findings.

articleTitle: Workshop 1: Multi-Gbps massive MIMO for 5G mobile devices and MIMO system performance verification
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Massive or Full-Dimension MIMO antennas are promising for application in the next-generation mobile devices such as the smartphone for the fifth-generation (5G) communications to achieve multi-Gbps throughput. It has been recently demonstrated that with 12 antennas embedded in the limited space in the smartphone, 3.8-Gbps throughput can be obtained for 12 × 8 MIMO operation with 100-MHz bandwidth and 256-QAM modulation. A new MIMO OTA testbed has been developed for the MIMO system performance verification. Details of the MIMO theory and the promising MIMO antennas for the smartphone will be addressed. Results of the multi-Gbps Massive MIMO in typical indoor and outdoor propagation scenarios will also be presented and its potential applications for 5G communications will be discussed.

articleTitle: Various kinds of antenna and their applications (invited talk)
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Antennas are important for digital data communication and radar applications. For various applications, special performances of antennas are required. In this paper various kinds of antenna, reflector antenna, phased array antenna, low profile antennas, and reconfigurable antennas, will be discussed for various applications.

articleTitle: Reading distance extension of original RFID reader with technique of metamaterial structure
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the application of metamaterial structure for improving the gain of antenna to extend the reading distance of UHF RFID reader without any modifying of the original reader. The proposed structure of metamaterial is designed on the theory of Spilt Ring Resonator (SRR), which located in front of such the RFID reader, while the back side of reader is blocked with a metallic sheet as reflector. At last, we found that the proposed structure of metamaterial can provide the gain around 9.16 dB when compared to the original one (around 1.84 dB).

articleTitle: Comparison of three compact-SAR mode through rice phenology monitoring
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is known to all weather usable radar system. It can divide linear polarimetric SAR (LP-SAR) and circular polarimetric SAR (CP-SAR). However, CP-SAR has been proven to less effect of the Faraday rotation in the ionosphere. On the other hand, in spite of polarization, full polarimetric SAR (FP-SAR) has some drawbacks of limited swash width, an increase of system complexity, data rate and power consumption. Hence, dual polarimetric SAR (DP-SAR) becomes attractive configuration, and thus some researchers employ DP-SAR for their research. Accordingly, we need to know the feature of each DP-SAR. We investigate to confirm the difference of each DP-SAR adopting same H/α decomposition for rice phenology monitoring.

articleTitle: Calculation of residue error in FDTD method for numerical dosimetry
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a residual error indicating an accuracy of numerical solutions obtained by finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is calculated at a single frequency. The method extends a methodology of finding the convergence of the FDTD solutions previously proposed by the authors. By using our approach, the accuracy of the FDTD solutions is preserved by values of the calculated residue error. It is also shown that the residual error converges to a constant value at a steady-state condition.

articleTitle: Artificial magnetic conductor for low-profile and human-friendly IoT antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) structure employed for low-profile antenna operates in Wi-Fi 5 GHz band for wearable internet of things (IoT) devices. A proposed AMC structure comprises of a combination of ring slots. This structure can improve the impedance bandwidth of a planar dipole antenna when the size of AMC surface is approximately half wavelength. The simulation results demonstrate that a dipole antenna on the proposed AMC surface is low profile and has less effect when operating on human body.

articleTitle: Novel integration-time conversion of rain-rate statistics for rain attenuation prediction models
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Rain rate statistics is an essential part of rain attenuation prediction models. Mostly, the 1-min integration time is required for the rain rate statistics and, if it is not available, the methods in the Rec. ITU-R P.837 are commonly used to convert the available statistics to the statistics with 1-minute integration time. In this work, a novel integration-time conversion method is proposed based on the multi-rate signal processing and the correction scale. The performance results show that the proposed method is promising and outperforms the existing ITU-R models.

articleTitle: Dual-band FPC dipole with pattern reconfiguration for wifi application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band dipole with pattern configuration, FPC structure antenna is proposed. By controlling the pin diodes on the reflectors, three modes of radiation pattern are generated for 2G and 5G, respectively, and Reconfiguration antenna can be achieved. DC trace and RF trace are highly integrated and easy to combine with electronic products. Results of measurement for return loss, radiation pattern and antenna efficiency of proposed design are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Workshop 3: Use of EM beams for the efficient simulation of antenna and scattering problems
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: It is well known from the independent works of Keller, Deschamps, and Felsen, respectively, that an electromagnetic (EM) point current source positioned in complex space produces a beam wave field which is highly localized about its forward propagation axis. It is noted that the EM field of a complex source beam (CSB) constitutes an exact solution of Maxwell's equations, and it is simply obtained by an analytic continuation of the exact closed form expression of the EM field for a point current in real space, where the real source coordinates are replaced by complex values. In its paraxial region, a CSB automatically reduces to a Gaussian Beam (GB). By controlling the values of the complex source coordinates, one can produce either a CSB with a very broad (not well focused) beam or a very narrow (highly focused) beam; consequently, such a CSB field can be made to pass smoothly from the field of a real point source to a plane wave field. It is clear that CSBs can serve as highly useful basis functions to represent EM fields, and indeed they have been used in this fashion by some researchers in this area. Here, additional useful methods for developing convergent CSB expansions to represent the fields of EM sources, via appropriate EM equivalence theorems, will be illustrated. Applications of such CSB expansions to analyze a class of electrically large practical antenna and scattering problems will be presented to demonstrate their utility.

articleTitle: Magnetic resonance compatible head implantable sensing antenna with three-dimensional structure
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A three-dimensional (3D) loop-based antenna with compact structure for intracranial sensing applications is presented. The overall dimensions of the antenna is 1×1×0.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The antenna operates over the medical implant communication service (MICS) band and is capable to communicate effectively with the external interrogators. The antenna is found to be compatible with magnetic resonance based triaging systems.

articleTitle: Design of small CRPA arrays with high-dielectric ceramic superstrates for gain enhancement
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes small CRPA arrays with high-dielectric ceramic superstrates for dual-band operation. Each array element consists of inner and outer microstrip rings printed on a high-dielectric substrate, and a hybrid chip coupler is used for quadrature excitation to achieve circular polarization. The superstrates with high relative permittivity are designed to have a cylindrical shape and are placed above the inner ring area to enhance the bore-sight gain. The results show that the bore-sight gain of the active element pattern is -1.54 dBic at 1.5754 GHz and -3.35 dBic at 1.2276 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a wideband 6-port MIMO antenna using leaf-shaped monopole and notch antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a design of a wideband 6-port antenna array which can be used for MIMO communication systems. In the designed antenna that operates over the frequency band of 7-10GHz, four leaf-shaped notch antennas and two leaf-shaped monopole antennas are employed as radiating elements. Performance of the antenna is evaluated by the finite difference time domain (FDTD) analysis and measurement. Over the design frequency range from 7GHz to 10GHz, the designed antenna has the reflection coefficient of less than -10dB, and the mutual coupling between ports are observed to be below -12dB.

articleTitle: Impedance effect of elliptical curved surface on RFID tag performances
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the effect of the impedance curved surface to the characteristics of the RFID tag. The proposed passive RFID tag is placed on the elliptical curved surface. From the simulation result, it this found that the proposed RFID tag has a flat gain in the UHF RFID frequency band in Thailand. Moreover, the variation of the length and width of the elliptical surface is important effect on the input reactance of the RFID tag.

articleTitle: Adiabatic Floquet wave modes for metasurface antenna design
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces an adiabatic Floquet modes expansion to design modulated metasurface (MTS) antennas. In these antennas, a MTS implements periodically modulated impedance boundary conditions to transform a bounded surface wave into a radiative leaky wave. A Floquet Wave expansion locally matched to the impedance boundary conditions well describes fields and currents on the MTS. This expansion constitutes a valid tool to model and design MTS antennas.

articleTitle: Local plane wave extrapolation based compact transparent boundary conditions for the Helmholtz equation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We present a high-order accuracy compact transparent boundary condition (TBC) for the Helmholtz equation. These TBC coefficients are derived from the principle of local plane wave extrapolation (LPWE). LPWE is when an EM field at a given point on the computational border is computed from the combined extrapolated field of a carefully chosen set of outgoing plane waves that pass through all neighboring points inside the computational domain. Hence, by design, LPWE-TBC can absorb both propagating and evanescent waves for both edge and the corner points. Numerical examples of computing two-dimensional free-space Green's functions are discussed. LPWE-TBC errors are well under one percent at a low sampling density of ten points per wavelength.

articleTitle: SAR moving target imaging using semi-blind two-dimensional autofocus algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Due to uncertainty on target's motion, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) processing can't compensate for the two-dimensional (2-D) phase error of moving targets completely. Therefore, moving targets SAR images often appear 2-D defocused. In this paper, we propose a 2-D autofocus method for refocusing the defocused moving targets SAR images. The new method only requires a direct APE estimation, while the residual 2-D phase error is computed directly from the estimated APE by exploiting the analytical relationship between the 2-D phase error and APE. The simulation experiment proves the proposed approach offers obvious advantages in both computational efficiency and estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: High efficiency and broadband design of reflectarray and measured results
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: On the reflectarray using ring-type resonator elements, a high efficiency design method was adopted and its results were confirmed at the design frequency. In this paper, in addition to the conventional high efficiency design method, a reflectarray was designed and measured by considering the broadband conditions. As a result, the aperture efficiency of the fabricated reflectarray was more than 65% in the relative bandwidth of 9.7%. Thus, the proposed design method was confirmed to have high efficiency wide band characteristics.

articleTitle: A-low-profile unidirectional beam antenna using dogbone structure
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A surface wave antenna with an antenna gain of 6.29dBi and an FB ratio of 16.7dB at 8.3GHz is presented. This antenna is vertically polarized and designed for unidirectional beam having a low-profile structure with a height of 0.098λ_0. This antenna is composed of a loop element and arrayed dogbone-shaped elements. The phase distribution of electric field radiated from both elements are analyzed the antenna mechanism.

articleTitle: Temperature and SAR distribution in human head from mobile phone of 2G, 3G, 4G using FEM modeling
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, to examine the impact of distance, and angle on the human head during the regular functioning of a mobile phone, a head model is constructed via COMSOL software dataset. The handset antenna has been configured with a patch antenna being a radiation source at 900 MHz, 1800 MHz and 2100MHz, respectively. Temperature increase and specific absorption rate distribution on the user's head with various angles and distances are simulated by using finite element method. It is observed that the values that are obtained in the simulations are in good agreement with the basic limitations set up ICNIRP, designating that the safety restrictions will not be dared by the usage of user.

articleTitle: Multiple-access coding technique for focal plane array LIDAR
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The manufacture of focal plane APD array becomes the fundamental limitation of array LIDAR. To overcome the bottleneck, a novel focal plane array LIDAR mechanism by applying multiple-access coding technique is proposed. Encoding, multiplexing and digital decoding are the essential modules added to this LIDAR system. The structure and principle of this LIDAR system is presented. The experiment indicates the sytem can achieve high-resoultion and high-precision imaging with small-scale APD detectors.

articleTitle: Study of multiple repeater antennas for high frequency (HF) RFID reader
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a study of multiple repeater antenna design for high frequency (HF) RFID reader. This work aims to show the possibility of increasing the reading area of the conventional HF RFID reader antenna by using the proposed multiple repeater antenna. The proposed repeater antenna is designed to operate at 13.56 MHz of ISO 15693, I-code standard. The proposed repeater antenna is located above the conventional HF RFID reader antenna without direct connection. The proposed repeater antenna configuration and its proper parameters are investigated. It is found that the reading area of the conventional HF RFID reader antenna can be increased. Moreover, the reading performances in the term of arbitrary tag orientation are improved more than 161.28 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Experimental evaluation towards approximate DoA estimation using 2 by 2 MIMO sensor with time correlation of channel matrix
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The multiple input multiple output (MIMO) sensor utilized for human detection by channel state information in a MIMO propagation channel has been proposed. In this paper, we evaluate the estimation of the detection of the person and the approximate direction of arrival (DoA) of the person using a correlation function with only 2 by 2 MEMO configuration. We focus on the DoA estimation of the human in an indoor scenario by applying MEMO sensor with the time correlation for wide and narrow element spacings in the horizontal place at the transmit and receive array antennas. The measurement results show that the narrow element spacing was effective for the broadside direction estimation, whereas the wider element spacing was effective for the end-fire direction estimation considering the approximate DoA estimation using the time correlation even if high-resolution techniques, such as the MUSIC algorithm, is not used.

articleTitle: Analysis of cancerous tissue temperature in the breast during hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the computational modeling of the 2D human breast in hyperthermia treatment at 2.45 GHz is studied. The mathematical tool used in this study for investigating the distribution of generated heat is the COMSOL software where the breast is modeled by Pennes' bioheat equation. The model simulation is conducted to investigate the effects of exposure time and power inputs on the cancerous tissue temperature field. The results show that this method can cure the breast cancer patient without damaging the breast tissue.

articleTitle: The structure tuning of plugs-shaped monopole antenna for wireless communication applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper purposed the plugs-shaped monopole antenna by adding stub and slot etching tuning technique on patch for the impedance bandwidth enchantment and the capability to support the applications in DCS, PCS, WCDMA/UMTS, WLAN IEEE 802.11 b/g and Bluetooth system. The prototyped antenna structure has been fabricated on FR4 printed circuit board (FR4) with dimensions of 36×40 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The measured result has been found that the impedance bandwidth of 70.16% (1.24-2.58 GHz) The radiation pattern is omnidirectional and average again of 3.14 dBi.

articleTitle: Suppressing multi-component interference in chirp signal for spaceborne sar based on FRFT
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a kind of interference on chirp pluses in spaceborne SAR and the corresponding suppression method are introduced. This interference is a kind of multi-component linear frequency modulated (LFM) signal which is difficult to be suppression by classical elimination methods. According to the generation mechanism of interference, the mathematical model is established firstly. Moreover, the characteristics of the interference are analyzed in detail. And quantitative analyses of the interference on imaging quality are presented. Furthermore, the suppression method based on the fractional Fourier transform (FrFT) is proposed. Finally, simulation results validate the effectiveness and the correctness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Influence of leaves, branches and trunks on the propagation loss in 920-MHz on a mulberry farm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Radio wave propagation characteristics were measured in 920-MHz band on a mulberry farm, and influence of leaves, branches and trunks was investigated by analyzing the measured data in three different environments and in two polarizations. RSSIs (Received Signal Strength Indicators) were measured at two propagation distances and converted to path losses. And, then they were compared among maturity stage, deciduous stage, and the case without plants. As a result, it was found that horizontal polarization was mainly influenced by leaves and that vertical polarization was mainly influenced by branches and trunks. The obtained radio wave propagation characteristics are useful for building a farm sensor network.

articleTitle: Fast design of low scattering metasurface
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a fast design procedure for the low scattering metasurface in the microwave region. Since there are numerous units with various geometric dimensions inside the metasurface aiming to generate a diffusion-like scattering pattern, it presents a large computation burden for the evaluation and optimization of the scattering behaviors of the whole metasurface. To overcome this drawback, we will discuss the far field prediction method based on the fourier-transform method, and then introduce the fast global optimization method to get the desired array pattern. Such method is extremely beneficial for the synthesis of large metamaterial array and therefore promote the design efficiency significantly.

articleTitle: A high-gain double reflectors microstrip-fed slot antenna for WLAN and WiMAX applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents a high-gain double reflectors microstrip-fed slot antenna for WLAN and WiMAX applications as the IEEE 802.11b/g and IEEE 802.11a standards. The antenna is composed of a microstrip-fed slot with a complementary stub on a single substrate and a pair of reflectors. The reflectors are exploited to achieve bi-directional radiation patterns which is suitable for using in buildings or corridor. The antenna is optimized to obtain gains: 4.75 dbi, 5.1 dBi, and 9.9 dBi, at the frequency of 2.4 GHz, 3.5 GHz, and 5.2 GHz, respectively. To validate the designed antenna, a prototype antenna was fabricated and measured to carry out its S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, radiation patterns, and gain. The measured results are in good agreement with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Double band switchable metamaterial absorber using double square loop
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper a double square loop switchable metamaterial absorber based on active frequency selective surface (AFSS) is introduced. The design of AFSS structure is comprised of periodically arranged square loops with PIN diodes. There are four states simulation results can be presented by controlling the bias voltage of the PIN diodes, and the method for the design of feeder circuits is probe-fed. The AFSS structure exhibits the stable response for both TE and TM polarizations because of the symmetrical structure.

articleTitle: High-efficiency broadband cross-dipole antenna for wireless energy harvesting
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-polarized cross-dipole antenna with a radiating patch and a tapered balun is proposed for the harvesting of wireless energy over the frequency band from 1.92 GHz to 2.16 GHz. By optimizing the antenna dimensions, the performance of the proposed antenna is improved, such as a 1.01 of VSWR, a 96 % efficiency, and a nearly omnidirectional beam pattern. The proposed antenna could be used to supply power to many low-power electronic devices.

articleTitle: A dual-axis wide-angle rectenna using a triple-feed array antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a new planar rectenna which provides dual-axis wide-angle reception. An in-phase/anti-phase triple-feed array antenna is employed to obtain high gain but prevent gain degradation due to main-beam misalignment. The proposed rectenna separately rectifies the in-phase and anti-phase components of the received RF waves in a simple structure by effectively using two types of magic-Ts. The performance of the proposed rectenna is experimentally evaluated. Better than 100-mV open-circuit DC voltages are obtained at 0.05-W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> RF power density over the wide reception angle from −30° to 30° in both E- and H-plane when rectifying diodes are connected in parallel.

articleTitle: Rotational circularly polarized array antenna for mutual coupling reduction
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents rotational circularly polarized array antenna at 12 GHz. Array antenna degraded radiation performance because of mutual coupling between adjacent elements. General array antenna has same direction port each single elements. However, proposed rotational array antenna has different direction port to reduce the mutual coupling. As a results, mutual coupling of 2 by 2 rotational array reduce the about 10 dB compare with conventional array antenna. So proposed array antenna is better radiation performance than conventional; improve the realized gain, axial ratio, sidelobe level and efficiency.

articleTitle: Investigation of the electrical property of multi-layer soil using short-time matrix pencil method
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an investigation of the electrical property of the multi-layer soil using a short-time matrix pencil method (STMPM). The simulations are conducted in order to investigate the poles on the different electrical property of soil. In simulations, a Gaussian pulse is transmitted to the multi-layer soil with various electrical properties. Poles including the damping factor and natural frequency are extracted from the electromagnetic (EM) wave scattered from the soil. Five successive poles obtained from the late-time portion were chosen to investigate their effects on the electrical property of the multi-layer soil. Simulation results show that the different electrical properties of multi-layer soil have different pole groups.

articleTitle: Optical fiber connected passive primary surveillance radar using two receiver units
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes a concept of multi-static primary surveillance radar (MSPSR) developed by ENRI. We have so far proposed an optical fiber connected passive primary surveillance radar (OFC-PPSR) which is based on the principle of passive bistatic radar. A separated receiver unit uses scattered waves from aircraft and radar reference data transmitted by the radio over fiber (RoF). Radio frequency signals of transmitter unit and processing data such as rotating angle, transmitted timing and so on, are included as reference data. In this paper, we introduce the proposed system which consists of two receiver units. Then, we show a preliminary experimental result. It will be shown that the proposed system detects the moving object.

articleTitle: Study on propagation channel characteristics at 20-GHz band for outdoor small cell
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the 5G system, high frequency bands over 6 GHz (6-100 GHz) will be a key factor in providing a very wide bandwidth. Because of high path losses, these bands are considered to use for small cells. To design radio links with high accuracy and evaluate 5G system performances for various scenarios, channel characteristics must be clarified. In this paper, we clarify channel characteristics in an outdoor small cell environment at the 20 GHz band based on the measurement using a channel sounder.

articleTitle: A tunable inverted-L antenna (TILA) for LTE mobile terminals
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A Tunable Inverted L Antenna (TILA) for Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) mobile terminals is presented. Two ILAs with different lengths and varactor diodes are combined to enable bandwidth and resonance tunability at lower and upper bands respectively. The antenna 10dB bandwidth is tunable from 2250 MHz to 2700 MHz in the lower band and from 5000 MHz to 5800 MHz in the upper band. The realized gain in the lower and upper bands is 3.87 dB and 2.73 dB, respectively, with good isolation and Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) of less than 0.05.

articleTitle: Simple squint angle compensation for SAR with millimeter wave automotive radar
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Application of squint-mode SAR for millimeter wave automotive radar has been studied for high-resolution imaging technique to realize safety driving of automobile. In observation with automobile, real-time image generation is necessary while running. In this paper, we propose a simple squint angle compensation for the squint-mode SAR imaging. Computer simulation and experimental results are provided to show the validity of this compensation.

articleTitle: Electrically small, low profile, broadside radiating LP and CP Huygens dipole antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Electrically small Huygens dipole antennas are reported that are low profile, broadside radiating, have high radiation efficiencies, and are either linear (LP) or circularly (CP) polarized. The Huygens behavior, i.e., a high front-to-back ratio with a cardioid-like pattern, is realized by exciting two (LP) or two pairs (CP) of complementary electric and magnetic dipole radiators, simultaneously having the same amplitude and proper phase. These designs are achieved with near-field resonant parasitic (NFRP) Egyptian axe dipole (EAD) elements that act as the electric radiators and capacitively loaded loop (CLL) NFRP elements that act as the magnetic radiators.
