By efficiently combining the crossed EAD and CLL NFRP elements together with proper excitations by a single (LP) or a pair (CP) of driven dipole elements, the resulting electrically small antennas generate broadside Huygens radiation patterns. They have ka <; 1.0, are low-profile, ≤ 0.04 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>; exhibit good radiation performance with better than 4.5 dBi LP and 4.5 dBic CP peak realized gains; have > 20 dB front-to-back ratios; and have > 90% radiation efficiencies at their resonant frequencies. These antenna systems are quite suitable for a variety of compact narrow bandwidth applications including wireless power transfer (WPT), unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and on- and off-body sensor networks.

articleTitle: Design of a wide band Butler matrix in groove gap waveguide technology
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The steps to design a 4 by 4 Butler matrix in groove gap waveguide technology are presented. The operation frequency has been selected as one of the bands candidates for future 5G systems (26 GHz). The different components of the matrix are designed and optimized to be wideband and low loss.

articleTitle: Simulation and analysis of an ultra-wideband TEM horn antenna with ridge
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An ultra-wideband TEM horn antenna with ridge is simulated and designed. The feed mode of the antenna adopts the form that the coaxial line is parallel to the radiation direction. By modeling and simulating in CST Microwave Studio<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> software, it can realize that the impedance bandwidth of |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|<; -10dB is 1-30 GHz or more. Within this operating bandwidth, the antenna has directional radiation pattern with the gain 6.70-19.40dBi. The simulation results of the antenna are analyzed, and it shows the principle of ultra-wideband operation and directional radiation. The antenna's bandwidth covers L/S/C/X/Ku/K band and it can be widely used in communication and radar system of the band mentioned above.

articleTitle: Far-field estimation of antennas above the earth using hemispherical source reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Far-field pattern of an antenna above the earth is different from the characteristics in free space. We propose an estimation method of antenna far-field above the earth from near-field data in free space. The method reconstructs current distribution on a surface of an antenna from near-field data in free space and estimates the far-field pattern above the earth using the reconstructed current distribution. It is shown that the use of the proposed method achieves the far-field estimation of an antenna above the earth from near-field data in free space by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Broadband design using matrix analysis of frequency selective surface inserted at the center of dielectric plate in millimeter-wave band
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Thicknesses of window glasses, radomes, plastic cases of wireless systems are comparable with the wavelength in the millimeter-wave band. The reflections from the dielectric plate surfaces are canceled out of phase when the thickness is identical to a half of the wavelength. The reflection loss is minimum at the resonant frequency. However, they are not canceled at any other frequencies except integer multiple of a half wavelength. Therefore, the return loss is a serious problem in the millimeter-wave band. We propose to insert a frequency selective surface (FSS) at the center of the dielectric plate, which satisfies the phase condition to cancel three reflections from two dielectric surfaces and the FSS. A wide bandwidth for low return loss was obtained by generating three resonances, which satisfy the amplitude condition to cancel the three reflections. The matrix analysis is applied in the calculation of the scattering matrices (S-matrix) of the three reflections in this paper.

articleTitle: Leaf-shaped log-periodic slot antenna for broadband applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes simulation study on a single-sided planar log-periodic slot antenna providing wide bandwidth. The proposed antenna is very compact having overall physical size of 50.9×50.9 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (equivalent to electrical size of 0.27λ×0.27λ at lowest operating frequency) and is easy to integrate with other circuit components of communication devices. It provides wide bandwidth of 11.6 GHz (from 1.6 to 13.2 GHz), nearly stable bidirectional radiation pattern and gain variation of 2-6 dBi with more than 60% radiation efficiency over its operating frequency band. It can be a suitable element for portable wireless systems operating over wide range of frequencies including IMT 1800, UMTS 2100, WLAN 2450, and UWB.

articleTitle: Implantable intracranial pressure monitoring sensing antenna with magnetic resonance compatibility
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A planar implantable sensing antenna is designed for intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring by utilizing the capacitive coupling principle with the use of two parallel rings. The overall dimensions of the sensor is 1×1×0.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The sensor operates over the medical implant communication service (MICS) band and found to be effective in monitoring variations of pressure differences within the brain. Magnetic compatibility of the implantable ICP sensor is also investigated and found to meet the radiation and thermal safety levels of MRI system standards.

articleTitle: Experimental study of double-balanced-multiplier integrated circularly polarized microstrip antenna with nonlinear characteristics
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a double balanced multiplier (DBM) integrated circularly polarized microstrip antenna is investigated experimentally. The DBM is one of functional microwave circuits. The DBM is loaded in order to achieve a circularly polarized antenna with wideband and its sense switching function. Performances of the antenna due to the nonlinear characteristics of the DBM depend on the input power. The antenna performances for the input power are experimentally discussed.

articleTitle: A compact monopole antenna for bluetooth and UWB applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a compact monopole antenna is proposed for Bluetooth (2.4–2.484 GHz) and ultra-wideband (UWB; 3.1–10.6 GHz) applications. The size of the proposed antenna is 19× 28× 0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. It consists of a double ring-type monopole and branched monopole. The double ring-type monopole operates above 5 GHz, and the branched monopole produces additional resonance in the Bluetooth band and the UWB low-frequency band.

articleTitle: High gain spherical dielectric resonator antenna using higher-order resonant mode
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper propose a high gain spherical Dielectric Resonator Antenna(DRA) operating in higher-order modes. A simple amputated spherical DRA model was designed to implement the characteristics of the resonant modes generated in the dielectric. The prototype antenna was fabricated by spherical ceramic having a dielectric constant of ∊r = 21 and operates in TE401 mode at 5.85GHz. The 10dB bandwidth and peak gain of prototype antenna are 5.81–5.93GHz(120MHz, 2.04%) and 10.1dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Near-field measurement of transmit antenna factor of small dipole antenna in saline solution
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To determine E-field at a tip of probe for evaluating SAR (specific absorption rate) values of DUTs in saline solution, use of near-field transmit antenna factor (NF-TAF) of small dipole antenna is proposed. NF-TAF can be expressed in closed form by assuming hyperbolic sinusoidal current distribution. Also, it can be evaluated by measuring S parameters between two identical dipole antennas and dielectric property of the saline solution. Calculated and measured NF-TAF are compared with each other, and limited range of antenna distance should be used for accurate calibration of E-field probe in the saline solution at 6.78MHz.

articleTitle: Active element pattern and array pattern of patch array antenna including ground edge effect
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The active element pattern (AEP) and beam pattern of a patch array antenna are analytically calculated with a finite ground plane. The patch antenna is modeled by two equivalent magnetic current sources. Edge diffraction by surface wave is also added. To obtain AEP, the phase and magnitude of scattering parameters from full-wave simulation are utilized. To validate our calculation, the calculated results are compared with HFSS full-wave simulation. The results show that the effects of edge diffraction are significant as the number of array is smaller.

articleTitle: Design of a multi-band orthomode transducer for radiometers
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A multi-band orthomode transducer design, which covers 89, 36.5, 22.3 and 18.6 GHz, the general operating frequencies of microwave radiometers, is presented in this paper. Excellent impedance matching and polarization purity are achieved across all the frequency bands. The coaxial-type orthomode transducer-junction can provide adequate isolation between ports of different frequencies, and avoid serious higher-order mode excitations within cascaded constructions.

articleTitle: A broadband circularly-polarized antenna with wide axial-ratio beamwidth
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A broadband circularly polarized antenna with wide axial-ratio beamwidth utilizing a wideband power divider network is presented. The vertical and horizontal paired-dipoles are used as the antenna elements, which are excited by a 1-to-4 sequential broadband feeding network. Through a rational design of the spacing between two parallel dipoles and the feeding network, an antenna with broad impedance and axial-ratio bandwidth and wide 3-dB axial ratio beamwidth is achieved. A prototype of the proposed antenna is designed, fabricated, and tested. It can achieve a measured impedance bandwidth for VSWR≤1.5 of 67.9% and a 3-dB axial-ratio bandwidth of 42.5%. Moreover, the antenna has wide 3-dB axial ratio beamwidth of more than 120° ranging from 1.16 to 1.46 GHz. The proposed antenna is low profile, and can be built using low-cost printed circuit fabrication methods.

articleTitle: Microwave electromagnetic field characteristic evaluations in aircrafts containing lossy materials based on quality factor of a reverberation chamber
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The effects of electromagnetic lossy materials such as humans, on the electromagnetic field (EMF) characteristics of an aircraft are evaluated using finite-difference time-domain analyses and experiments conducted in a reverberation chamber. This study aims to confirm the EMF reduction effect, through measurements. The results of a large-scale finite-difference time-domain analysis conducted on a model of the B777-200 aircraft with occupants show a reduction in the electric field strength inside the cabin. The EMF loss due to a human phantom is measured quantitatively using a reverberation chamber, between 500 MHz and 6 GHz. The measured quality factor is found to be reduced by 55% when using a full-sized human phantom, which is lower than of the value measured at 2.1 GHz, without using a phantom.

articleTitle: Acceleration for RPM-based three-dimensional imaging for 140 GHz-band millimeter wave radar
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: 140 GHz-band millimeter wave radars significantly expands the appilication range of three-dimensional (3-D) imaging sensors, making them suitable for short-range surveillance or watching sensors. The range points migration(RPM) is recently established as promising imaging approach for achieving an accurate and real-time 3-D imaging. However, in dealing with objects with many scattering points like human body, the RPM suffers from an expensive computational cost. This paper proposes an acceleration of the RPM method, based on the newly designed cost function for multiple small array conflagrations. The results from 140 GHz based numerical data demonstrate that our proposed algorithm remarkably reduces the computational cost without sacrificing its reconstruction accuracy.

articleTitle: Simulation and analysis of an X-band low sidelobe and high gain microstrip antenna array
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A kind of low sidelobe and high gain microstrip antenna array with 32×8 units operating in the X-band is designed, which achieves the gain of 28 dBi and the sidelobe level of −25 dB at 9.37 GHz. The Chebeshev distribution is used in designing the current distribution on the surface of this antenna, which achieves a width of main lobe of 5° in E-plane and a main lobe width of 10° in H-plane. The amplitude and phase of the feed current are extracted by using CST Microwave Studio®, the commercial simulation software, which indicate that the antenna achieves the Chebeshev current distribution. The sidelobe level calculated from this kind of current distribution is in good agreement with the simulation results, which proved the self-consistency of the simulation data.

articleTitle: Acceleration of RPM-based microwave imaging for non-destructive testing
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A microwave ultra-wideband (UWB) radar has an advantage for high range resolution and deep penetration depth in a concrete object, and is promising for non-destructive testing for aging transportation infrastructure. The traditional delay-and-sum (DAS) based imaging algorithm inherently suffers from an insufficient resolution to identify a detailed structure of buried targets. As promising alternative, the range points migration (RPM)-based imaging method has been developed. However, this method faces a serious problem in terms of an expensive computational cost, particular in three-dimensional case. This paper, then, introduces an acceleration of the RPM-based imaging method by exploiting the feature of Envelope outer boundary extraction. The results from experimental data demonstrate that this method accurately reconstructs the shape of air cavity buried in concrete object with considerably reduced computational cost.

articleTitle: Reflectarray antenna constructed by arranging double omega-shaped resonant elements with mirror image for circular-polarization conversion
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes novel reflectarray elements by arranging double omega-shaped resonant strips with mirror image for converting a linearly polarized incident wave into a circularly polarized radiated wave. As a design example, a linear-to-circular polarizer reflectarray is presented and also its polarization property of far-field patterns over 12-17 GHz is discussed numerically and experimentally.

articleTitle: Ultra-high resolution (0.05m) SAR image formation processing
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: With the continuous improvement of the SAR resolution, image formation signal processing becomes a challenging problem. In this paper, image formation signal processing including image formation algorithm, motion compensation and autofocus are discussed. Processing results of real data collected by an ultra-high resolution SAR are presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Improvement of HF RFID reader performance under metallic environment using ferrite sheet
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Conventional loop antennas for RFID reader usually perform worse with metallic environment. To improve reading range under this condition, a ferrite sheet is incorporated in the conventional loop antenna. The proposed antenna yields similar reading range with or without metallic environment.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of TDD-SVD-MIMO system with feedback delays
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The authors have been researching a 4×4 SVD-MIMO-OFDM system that adaptively changes transmitter weights and modulation schemes in accordance with feedback information received by a TDD. This report presents our evaluation of the effects of feedback delays due to the TDD on the BER performance of the proposed system. The computer simulation results revealed that the required normalized SNR of a system with the shortest feedback delay of 2 ms degraded about 1 dB from that of an ideal system without feedback delays. In this case, the results showed that the system improved the required normalized SNR by about 4 dB in comparison with that of a fixed modulation MIMO-OFDM system.

articleTitle: High isolation two-element MIMO antenna array based on embedded meta-material cells
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A high isolation two-element MIMO antenna array is proposed by using embedded meta-material structure. The proposed meta-material is comprised of two layers at different level and the two layers are connected together by shorted pins. Five proposed meta-material cells are embedded in the FR-4 substrate, which is installed between the two antenna elements, to improve the isolation of the two-element MIMO antenna array. The proposed MIMO antenna array with meta-material isolation elements are created by the HFSS and its performance is also investigated in detail. The experimental results show that the proposed meta-material cells can provide a mutual coupling reduction of 18 dB in terms of the transmission coefficients.

articleTitle: A small UHF RFID passive tag antenna using modified split ring resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a UHF RFID tag antenna designed for using in Thailand (920-925 MHz). The modified split ring resonator (SRR) is used to reduce an antenna size. The antenna contains 3-ring resonator: 2-circular ring and 1-square ring. The outer ring is a square SRR which is connected to circular SRR on the radiating part. This structure can be matched the IC chip impedance by adjusting the space of the square SRR. The proposed tag antenna can operate to cover the frequency range of 920-925 MHz with the |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| of less than -10 dB. The antenna size is 38 mm × 38 mm. The proposed tag has maximum read range of 3.20 meters.

articleTitle: E-band one-step 45° double-wing gap waveguide twist for waveguide WR12
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel double-wing one-step 45° Gap waveguide twist at E-band. By employing an optimal double-wing structure for Gap waveguide flange, only one gap waveguide section is needed for the polarization transform between diagonal polarization and horizontal/vertical polarization, which does not require good conductive contacts between the connected flanges. This new waveguide twist is in particular useful and of low cost at millimeter wave frequency and up to THz.

articleTitle: Monopole decagon fractal patch resonator with defected ground plane for WLAN MIMO antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a monopole decagon fractal patch resonator with the defected ground plane for WLAN MIMO antenna. The fractal technique on the edge of the decagon patch is used for reducing the operating frequency of the antenna. Concurrently, the defected ground plane (DGP) with a rectangular shape can reduce the mutual coupling between the radiating patches due to the suppression of coupling current. The reflection coefficient and isolation of the proposed antenna are achieving higher than -10 dB and -15 dB, respectively, which are covering the entire WLAN frequency band of 2.40-2.485 GHz. Then, the radiation results clearly perform the behavior of spatial diversity with the contrary beams from two excitation ports of the MIMO antenna.

articleTitle: An autofocus algorithm for multi-rotor UAV SAR
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Multi-rotor UAV is a popular platform for low-cost SAR system because it has small volume, lightweight and flexible motion. However, due to complicated flight trajectory and low-accuracy motion sensor, autofocus in SAR processing becomes a challenging problem. In consideration of the characteristics of multi-rotor UAV SAR, this paper proposes an autofocus algorithm based on improved Mapdrift technology. The proposed algorithm can estimate the real-time velocity of multi-rotor UAV SAR and compensate the motion error, and then process the signals with range-Doppler algorithm.

articleTitle: Digital beamforming technique with high resolution digital phase shifter and digital phase calibration using SDR
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes high resolution digital beamforming technique using software defined radio (SDR). Digital phase shifter was designed with digital mixer and digital source and digital phase calibration technique was designed using digital processing block with correlation coefficient.

articleTitle: A low-profile spiral termination helical antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The spiral termination helical antenna is proposed in this paper. To reduce axial length, the number of helical turns is selected to be two turns and the pitch angle is selected to be 2.5°. The axial length of the proposed antenna is 0.15 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (46 mm). It is reduced to 80% of conventional low-profile helical antenna. The gain of proposed antenna is 9.6 dB and 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth is 10%.

articleTitle: A ground-based synthetic aperture radar system using portable VNA for landslide monitoring
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Landslide monitoring is crucial for early detection of landslide hazard and reduce the risk of a landslide. In this work, a Ground-Based Synthetic Aperture Radar (GB-SAR) system intended for landslide monitoring has been developed. The system is used to cognize a point target located at a certain distance. This GB-SAR system consists of portable VNA module, SAR processor, stepper controller, linear guide, and horn antenna. A portable VNA module is employed as transmitter and receiver of the signal based on the reflection coefficient (S11) principle. The laboratory experiment is done to verify the system performance to detect the point target. Result of laboratory experiments is highlighted and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Localization method using received signal strength for wireless power transmission of capsule endoscope
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, capsule endoscopy has attracted attention as a medical device that examines the internal digestive tract without burdening the patient. Wireless power transmission of the capsule endoscope is researching now, and the power transmission efficiency can be improved by knowing the capsule location. In this report, we try to use the three-dimensional localization method with five antennas.

articleTitle: Ku-band Car-borne FMCW stripmap synthetic aperture radar
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a Ku-band car-borne frequency modulated continuous wave synthetic aperture radar (FMCW SAR) system in order to acquire clear images in stripmap mode. The specification and the architecture of the system are provided to demonstrate the outstanding performance. The conventional range doppler algorithm(RDA) is modified to be suitable for the radar system equipped in an automobile. After gathering raw data on the highway and signal processing, the effectiveness of the radar to get SAR images is verified in the practical results.

articleTitle: Axial mode helical antenna with circular prasitic rings for gain enhancement
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposed a helical antenna in which circular parasitic rings are arranged inside a helical antenna. Compared to the gain boosting technique the traditional helical antenna, the height of the additional antenna does not increase. The gain of the proposed antenna is enhanced by a maximum of 2.5 dB in the working bandwidth by adding circular parasitic rings, while maintaining the Axial Ratio(AR) below the 3 dB. The simulation results and experimental results are used to confirm the gain and AR of the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Improvement of the accuracy of the microstrip-to-waveguide transition model using measured loss tangent at 76.5 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The accuracy of the microstrip-to-waveguide transition (MWT) simulation model near 76.5 GHz is shown to increase by using the estimated loss tangent of the dielectric substrate. The loss tangent is estimated by measuring the attenuation through two microstrip lines with different lengths connected between a pair of MWT's in a back-to-back configuration. The approach is validated by comparing the simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Sleeve antenna composed of two coaxial composite right/left-handed transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A sleeve antenna composed of two kinds of composite right/left-handed (CRLH) transmission lines (TL) is proposed. The proposed sleeve antenna is designed good matching to 50 ohms at 710 MHz. The radiation pattern is similar to that of conventional sleeve antenna. The length of the antenna is 0.14 wavelength at resonant frequency.

articleTitle: A wideband antenna using modified magneto-electric curved strip dipole
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The important factors increased the efficiency of the antenna to support users in the current technology are necessary wide impedance bandwidth, high gain, and low back radiation. In this paper, the antenna composed of the curved strip electric dipole and the vertically-oriented short patch is presented. The measured impedance bandwidth of 60.9% (SWR<;2) from the frequency range of 1.62-2.9 GHz is obtained and the maximum gain of 8.7 dBi is found over the operating frequencies.

articleTitle: MACKEY type O with dual-band characteristics when changing position of a dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Meta-surface inspired antenna (called MACKEY) which works not only in free space but also on metal plates, was proposed. In this paper, a dual-band MACKEY device, in which the position of the dipole antenna is changed from the center of the substrate, is proposed. Additionally, the conditions for controlling the resonance frequencies are clarified.

articleTitle: A novel ultra-wideband quasi-yagi antenna for millimeterwave applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For the first time, we propose a novel quasi-yagi end-fire antenna for wideband applications such as high resolution biomedical imaging, wireless backhaul communication and chip to chip communication in millimeter wave frequency band (67.5-107 GHz). The designed antenna covers a wideband of 39.5 GHz by achieving a fractional bandwidth of more than 45%. The gain of the antenna ranges from 4-6.58 dBi. An excellent radiation efficiency of more than 98% is also reported.

articleTitle: Metasurface beam splitter based on all-dielectric elliptic resonators
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We describe an all-dielectric metasurface, based on elliptic dielectric resonators (EDRs), which is designed to work as a beam splitter at 16.98 GHz. The proposed metasurface refracts electromagnetic incident waves with orthogonal polarizations along two specific directions without reflection.

articleTitle: Polynomial chaos expansion as a tool to quantify the performance of the GeReLEO-SMART satellite antenna under uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: At Ka-band frequencies, small deviations in the antenna production process result in sub-optimal performance. Classically, Monte-Carlo methods are used to quantify the influence of those tolerances. In this application, Monte-Carlo simulations are not feasible due to the high computational effort and the high number of parameters to be considered. As an alternative, we use polynomial chaos expansion to create a surrogate model using very few full-wave simulations. This model predicts the influence of the production tolerances on the performance of the antenna. Measurements confirm the results of the polynomial chaos expansion method.

articleTitle: Low-profile Fabry-Perot cavity (FPC) antenna using meta-surface for dual-band
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A subwavelength superstrate antenna operated at dual-band is proposed using a metasurface (MTS). To design the proposed antenna, the MTS as a partially reflective surface (PRS) has a zero-degree reflection phase at dual-band and is composed of a substrate, periodic metallic square patches and rings on one side, and periodic metallic meshes on the other side. To satisfy the resonance condition of Fabry-Perot cavity (FPC) at a certain frequency and height of PRS from the ground plane, a reflection phase of the MTS should be controlled by the dimension of the substrate, square patch, square ring, and mesh. In this letter, the planar radiator having a ring patch and a rectangular patch is employed and designed to operate at 2.1GHz and 5.8GHz. Also, the height of MTS from the ground plane is 12mm, which corresponds with about 0.08 wavelength and 0.23 wavelength at operation frequencies of radiator, respectively. As a result, the gain improvement at 2.1GHz and 5.8GHz are measured to be 4.1dB and 3.2dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Raytracing analysis of DME ranging error variation due to atmospheric change
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: GNSS (global navigation satellite systems) are widely used in aircraft navigation. However, a GNSS backup system is required due to GNSS vulnerability. Enhancement of DME (distance measuring equipment) is one of candidates for the GNSS backup system. Optimization of tropospheric propagation delay is suggested as one of technologies for the enhancement. In developing an optimization technology, first, the amount of variation in tropospheric propagation delay at very low elevation angles for aircraft application should be clarified quantitatively. Moreover, the cause of the variation should be detailed. This study analyzes these issues by using the raytracing method and upper-air observation data. The result provides data that can be utilized for the future development of the DME enhancement.

articleTitle: Evaluation of filtering technique for human activity identification using MIMO radar
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we evaluate the correction filter for human activity identification using Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar. The human activity is estimated by the trajectory of the estimated height and Radar Cross Section (RCS). We confirm that the filtering technique is effective in increasing the identification rate of the human activity, and the highest recognition rate is over 90%.

articleTitle: A printed array antenna for multi-layer PCB design
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a design of 1×4 printed array antenna excited by proximity coupling. The gain of patch antenna built on thin substrate is usually inferior to the one with thicker substrate of the same material. The goal of this work is to design an antenna with realized gain less responsive to substrate thickness. Patch antenna fed by two-layer proximity coupled feeding line is introduced to alleviate gain degradation caused by thin substrate. Proposed antenna is compared with conventional patch antenna in simulation. 1×4 array antenna is fabricated on multi-layer PCB to validate our design. Array antenna fabricated on FR-4 substrate exhibits good radiation characteristics and a flat gain response from 7.7 to 8.3 GHz is measured. Measured radiation patterns of array antenna are similar to simulations.

articleTitle: Design of dual-band metallic reflectarray antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band design of reflectarray antenna by using metallic elements for high energy efficiency at 28 and 60GHz bands. The dual-band operation is created by considering the frequency bands below and above the cutoff frequency of metallic waveguides. This frequency band separation differentiates the waveguide's characteristics as a resonant and non-resonant reflecting elements, respectively at the two bands, respectively. In our examples, the array consists of 20×32 waveguide elements at various locations of open-aperture and with various depths to create the desired phases of elements for equal-phase focusing beam radiation. Our numerical results have shown that high gain and low side lobe levels can be achieved with this design, which are of importance in the potential 5G applications.

articleTitle: Dual-band horizontally polarized sector antenna using frequency selective reflector and bent dipole element
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-band integrated horizontally polarized antenna composed of an alternately arranged frequency selective reflector (FSR) and a bent dipole element. The antenna is composed of a FSR backed dipole antenna designed in 3.5GHz band and it is placed in front of 2GHz band reflector backed dipole antenna. It is found that the alternate FSR configuration is suitable and there is an appropriate distance between the 3.5 and 2 GHz band antennas to obtain stable sector pattern in both the frequency bands. Moreover, by using bent dipole element, the HPBW of the both frequency bands can be almost identical.

articleTitle: A circular polarization antenna with square ring slot loaded on ground plane
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A new circular polarization microstrip antenna having a defected ground plane is presented in this paper. A defect on the ground plane is introduced by inserting a square ring slot just below one of the top corners of the patch. The inserted slot on the ground creates a perturbation in the patch as like as conventional perturbed circular polarization antennas. The measured 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth was 1.26% with a gain of around 6.1 dBic.

articleTitle: Paper moisture content determination from microwave reflection measurement
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a microwave reflection method for monitoring paper moisture content by using reflection coefficient. The different reflection coefficient and various moisture contents were measured and determined for monitoring paper humidity. The experiment shows good separation of dry and wet paper in reflection coefficient which the probability to design a simple paper moisture content monitoring system.

articleTitle: Experimental study of bell-shaped monopole antenna with short stub for UWB applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An experimental study for miniaturization of a broadband printed bell-shaped monopole antenna is described in this paper. This antenna improves the matched impedance in the lower frequency band by using the short stub structure. The fabricated antenna operates impedance bandwidth of 3.1~10.6 GHz and has a compact size of 20 × 28 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> using a FR-4 dielectric substrate. The proposed antenna acquired broadband characteristic covering the frequency band of UWB system by measurement.

articleTitle: Resoltuion improvement of GPR image using antenna calibration for object detection
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an improvement of the vertical resolution of a ground penetrating radar (GPR) image. The near-field calibration is employed to reduce the antenna effects including variation in the antenna response and coupling between transmitting and receiving antennas. The simulations with a scenario of the detection of an object buried under the ground are conducted. The ground surface affects the resolution of the GPR image. The effect of the ground surface was mitigated by using background subtraction. The effect of the antenna on the performance of the GPR image is investigated and then mitigated by using the antenna calibration technique. Simulation results are shown that the antenna calibration can significantly improve the resolution of GPR image.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of power dividers using quarter-wave-like transformers (QWLTs)
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the miniaturization of a three-port power divider for microwave frequency. The size reduction is achieved by the use of a quarter-wave-like transformer (QWLT) implemented by a properly designed conjugately characteristic-impedance transmission line (CCITL). The QWLT has a significantly shorter physical length than the conventional quarter-wave transformer (QWT). A novel condition for the isolation impedance has been derived and presented in this paper. The size reduction of the power divider can consequently reduce the whole dimension of the circuit composing the divider with insignificant performance degradation, and thus decreasing the manufacturing cost.

articleTitle: Wideband circularly polarized antenna and low-cost phase-shifters using partially transmitting surface
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a design for a circularly polarized (CP) antenna and a low-cost phase shifting mechanism using a partially transmitting surface (PTS). Both the return loss (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>) and the axial ratio (AR) bandwidth enhancement is achieved by using a partially transmitting surface (PTS) type of superstrate, placed above a crossed-Bowtie shaped antenna with cloverleaf arms. Designs for achieving a continuous phase variation, ranging from either (i) 10° to 70° (ii) or 10° to 43° are presented, the former with a wider phase range of 60° but a relatively narrow impedance matching bandwidth, as compared with the latter design whose phase range is 33°, but the impedance bandwidth is wider. The realized return loss (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>) bandwidth of the antenna is 38.5%, and its 3dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth is 41.5 %. Furthermore, the gain of the antenna is enhanced in the band of 4.2 to 6.2 GHz via the use of the PTS superstrate.

articleTitle: Wide-angle isolation characteristics of full-duplex image-sensor visible light communication
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Full-duplex visible light communication over a wide angle range is experimentally investigated using wide-angle LED and image sensor under fluorescent light condition. Isolation characteristics of more than 147 dB between received signal and other transmitted, reflected, and background lights are quantitatively estimated in the field of view of 70 degrees. Error free operation of full-duplex OOK visible light communication is also achieved in the field of view of 70 degrees.

articleTitle: Invited talk 2: Various kinds of antenna and their applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Antennas are important for digital data communication and radar applications. For various applications, special performances of antennas are required. In this paper various kinds of antenna, reflector antenna, phased array antenna, low profile antennas, and reconfigurable antennas, will be discussed for various applications.

articleTitle: Blind beamforming method by terminal station for downlink multi-beam massive MIMO
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Multi-beam massive MIMO configuration has been proposed that utilizes the beam selection with high power in an analog part and blind algorithm such as constant modulus algorithm (CMA) which does not need channel state information (CSI) in a digital part. In this paper, we evaluate the transmission performance in the downlink with a simple control at the user terminal by the massive MIMO transmission. By the computer simulation, it is shown that the multi-beam selection at the base station and CMA at the user terminal with two antennas can effectively realize the transmission with high order modulation scheme.

articleTitle: Gain measurement of 60 GHz CMOS on-chip dipole antenna by proton irradiation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a 60 GHz CMOS on-chip dipole antenna with loss-reduced silicon substrate, which had been proposed and simulated by the authors, was measured and gain improvement of approximately 9 dB was obtained. In the antenna, rectangular region with 500 μm × 1000 μm around the dipole is irradiated by proton and conductivity is reduced from 10 S/m (10 Ω cm) to 0.1 S/m (1 kΩ cm). Antenna gain of -4 dBi could be achieved.

articleTitle: Compact antenna for digital beamforming with software defined radios
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An adaptive radio system combining compact switchless reconfigurable antenna with Software Defined Radio is proposed. The system allows control of the direction of the transmitted signal solely by adjusting the baseband I and Q components of the modulated signal, while maintaining small antenna size through the use of compact multiport antenna. The system is demonstrated in a line-of-sight configuration with QPSK modulation. Experimental results demonstrate good received power and low error vector magnitude of the demodulated signals.

articleTitle: Performance improvement of MIMO radar using transmission beam and code diversity
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: By introducing diversity techniques to the transmitting array of MIMO radar, the performance of MIMO radar in target estimation can be enhanced. This paper utilizes compositely the transmission beam diversity and spreading code diversity, and also propose the algorithm for the diversity technique. The computer simulation shows the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Point-to-point 3 × 3 MIMO performance gains with aperiodic sparse arrays in pure LOS channels
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Analyzed is the topology of a 3-element linear array antenna with vertically polarized isotropic antenna elements. The focus has been on point-to-point (PtP) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communication over pure line-of-sight (LOS) channels. An empirical equation is presented for the mid-element's relative position achieving near-optimal 3 × 3 MIMO capacity. The position is a function of the transmit and the receive antennas separation distance and the wavelength of the transmit signal. The capacity gains of aperiodic over uniform array antenna configurations are presented, which at some distances can be a factor 2.5.

articleTitle: Compact directive array antenna design for UAV application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a compact two-patch array design is proposed for unmanned aerial vehicle applications. High gain directive antennas are employed to extend the wireless transmission range of either control signals or data streams. Considering that the handheld remote controller is likely to be aligned toward the airplane during operation, a compact patch array, which can be attached to the top of a remote controller, is designed. The antenna is operated in the 2.4 GHz band. To maximize the radiation efficiency, patches with air cavities are employed. Vertical polarization is chosen to match the antenna on the airplane. Measured results of the prototype antenna exhibit desired performance features for the operation scenario.

articleTitle: O-Shape monopole antenna structure with etching and impedance matching for digital TV system application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of O-shape monopole antenna with rectangular tuning stub to support the digital TV system which is simulated by using CST program. This antenna is designed coverage the digital TV system. The dimension of prototype antenna was 60 mm. × 100 mm. with etching technique and tuning impedance matching on antenna patch structure for bandwidth expansion. The measurement results of the antenna are the bandwidth of 76.24% (422-942 MHz) and the average gain of 3.35 dBi. The radiation pattern of the proposed antenna is omni-directional pattern.

articleTitle: Free-space material measurement of dielectric plate in millimeter frequency range
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: These days it has been rapidly increasing the use of millimeter and submillimeter EM (electromagnetic) devices and systems in very broad industry and science fields. Free-space method using antennas is one of the popular methods suitable for measuring material parameters which are a prerequisite to design and to fabricate EM devices and systems used in millimeter and submillimeter frequency ranges. This paper describes a quasi-optical free-space material measurement system and shows material measurement results of Glass, Bakelite, and PVC plates in 110–325 GHz frequency range (i.e. D-band (110–170 GHz), G-band (140–220 GHz) and J-band (220–325 GHz)).

articleTitle: Distributed source DOA estimation for more sources than sensors using sparse circular arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In wireless communications, the signal that a base station receive cannot be regarded as a point source because of the multipath propagation. A distributed source model is more suitable for the realistic scenario due to some environmental phenomenon. This paper presents subspace based method for distributed source direction of arrival estimation. Using nested sparse circular arrays, we are capable of estimating more distributed sources than the number of sensors. Simulation results confirms the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Graphene-based tag antenna for universal UHF-RFID system using modified single loop-matching techniques
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes a design of a UHF-RFID tag built by a graphene, designing with NXP G2XL IC chip. The tag can operate covering the UHF-RFID universal standard in accordance with the EPC global Class 1 Gen. 2 standard. The presented antenna is compact, easy to read and responsive. These articles focus on a design and developing of a compact universal passive tag antenna in order to operate entire UHF-RFID band of 860-960 MHz. The proposed tag antenna has the total dimension of 14 mm × 84 mm designed on PET (Polyethylene terephthalate) substrate with a thickness of 1 mm. The radiation pattern of tag antenna is omni-directional with linear polarization. The simulation of the maximum read range is 5.2 m considering at 900 MHz.

articleTitle: Switching beam antenna for LTE small cell application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)

articleTitle: Measurements of the 664 GHz feed horn for the ICI instrument of the MetOp-SG satellite
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the results of the antenna pattern measurements conducted on the Ice Cloud Imager 664 GHz feed horn at the ESTEC Sub-mmwave Scanner (SmS) in support to the ICI instrument of the MetOp-SG program. Very good agreement between simulations and measurements was obtained, both in the co- and cross-polar component. The measured peak directivity was 26.28 dBi ± 0.13 dB while the simulated one was 26.35 dB.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of LTE-Hi channel emulator
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design and test of 2×2 channel emulator, which is especially optimized for LTE-Hi testing. It adopts traditional convention method of the channel impulse response in time domain. The design features lower memory resource with sharing delay data buffering, which could reduce the cost of efficient VLSI Implement. In addition, Bidirectional design offers flexible and reliable duplex separation. Finally, the initial test is performed in both time and frequency domain for performance validations.

articleTitle: Dual-band patch antenna incorporated with SRR for GPS and WLAN application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the development of dual-band patch antenna incorporated with split ring resonator (SRR) for Global Positioning System (GPS) and Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) application. The antenna is composed of 3 layers of copper conductor flanking 2 layers of FR4 Epoxy dielectric substrate with the total thickness of 1.6mm and the dimension of 78.6mm × 48.4mm. The characterization shows that the resonant frequency of first frequency band is 1.47GHz with reflection coefficient of −16.4dB and −10dB working bandwidth of 335MHz. Whilst the resonant frequency of second frequency band is 2.43GHz with reflection coefficient of −22.6dB and −10dB working bandwidth of 60MHz.

articleTitle: A study on reactance time sequence for 2-element antenna with periodically variable antenna pattern
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, we derive a periodic time reactance sequence of a parasitic element for 2-element dipole antenna. We have designed the reactance sequence to make the antenna pattern vary in sinusoidal manner. With the antenna pattern, the receiver can obtain three received signal components for diversity reception or Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) reception in the frequency domain. Through analysis of the spectrum components of antenna pattern for azimuth, we confirm three received signal components or diversity branches in the frequency domain. Besides, by coherently adding the two frequency-shifted components we can obtain two equivalently strong diversity branches, that is, the coherently added component and dc component of the antenna pattern.

articleTitle: Resolution enhancement for MIMO radar by using Khatri-Rao product virtual array processing
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: High-resolution property is important for indoor location estimation radars. In order to realize the high-resolution property with a small number of elements, it is effective to utilize a virtual array technique in addition to the MIMO radar. In this report, we employ the Khatri-Rao product virtual array processing to the MIMO radar. The angular resolution improvement by this technique has already reported. We show in this report that we can apply the Khatri-Rao product virtual array processing to improve not only angular resolution but also range resolution for the FM-CW based MIMO radars. We also provide some experimental results to show validity of this processing.

articleTitle: L-band propagation measurement at tropical environment
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Communication and data transfer demands are growing fast in last few decades. In order to obtain higher data transfer, it is necessary to determine proper antenna placement in a wireless system. In this paper, we research propagation in tropical environment and L-Band frequency by conducting distance and high variation measurement at frequency 1.8 GHz and 2.4 GHz. The received power level decreases as the distance increases. Some discrepancies come from obstacles around the measurement set up. These results can contribute to find out the maximum channel capacity by considering an optimum antenna configuration based on received power levels.

articleTitle: A novel design of non-foster circuit using dispersive transmission line resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In brief, some properties of non-Foster circuits (NFC) are linked to the negative group delay (NGD) network. These properties are negative group delay and phase. It means that the NGD in conjunction with the effect of negative impedance is used to improve bandwidth of radio frequency (RF) modules. In this paper, we propose a design of passive non-Foster circuit by using NGD network that designed by two ways: RLC resonator and short-circuit half-wavelength in a specified dispersive medium. Finally, in a limitation of paper, the simulation results and some measurement results of our design will be shown in the last of our description.

articleTitle: Propagation characteristics of Laguerre-Gaussian beams through atmospheric turbulence in optical wireless communication
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The scintillation and bit error rate performance of optical wireless communication systems employing Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) beams were evaluated considering the size of the transmitted beam and receiving aperture. As a result, it was found that the system employing LG beams with a high radial number can reduce the effect of scintillation and improve communication quality.

articleTitle: A decoupling method for closely MIMO antennas by using a short stub
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, the MIMO (Multiple-Input Multiple-Output) technology, using multiple antennas, has been introduced in wireless terminals. If terminals are miniaturization, a strong mutual coupling caused by installing plural MIMO antenna closely is occurred. The coupling decreases radiation efficiency and channel capacity. Hence, the mutual coupling must be reduced. In previous studies, a decoupling method of inserting the inductor L or the capacitor C between antennas and using branch elements instead of L or C is confirmed. This paper proposes a decoupling technique by using a short stub.

articleTitle: Instantaneous freuqnecy measurement for broadband radio signals using optical single sideband modulation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: By using optical single sideband modulation, we demonstrated instantaneous frequency measurement, which would be useful to monitor wideband radio signals with agile frequency change.

articleTitle: Development of compact SLR BPF with cross-shaped I/O coupling
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper deals with the development of compact square-loop-resonator (SLR) bandpass filter (BPF) with cross-shaped input/output (I/O) coupling. The proposed filter is designed for X-band frequency application with the center frequency of 9GHz and the -3dB fractional bandwidth larger than 4%. It is deployed on a 1.9mm thick high permittivity RT/duroid® 6010.2LM dielectric substrate with the dimension of 15mm × 15mm. From the characterization, it shows that the realized BPF has the -3dB working bandwidth of 427MHz ranges from the frequency of 8.82GHz to 9.247GHz comparable with the simulated one which has the -3dB working bandwidth of 571MHz ranges from the frequency of 8.729GHz to 9.3GHz.

articleTitle: Workshop 4: Satellite communication antennas: Challenges for the next generation payloads
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Satellite communications has recently introduced several new services in the recent past. These include local-channel broadcast for direct broadcast satellite service (DBS), high capacity K/Ka-band personal communication satellite (PCS) service, hosted payloads, mobile satellite services using very large deployable reflectors, high power hybrid satellites etc. All these satellite services are driven by the operators need to reduce the cost of satellite and pack more capability into a single satellite launch. Antenna sub-system design, mechanical packaging on the spacecraft and RF performance are very critical for these satellites. This talk will cover recent developments in the areas of antenna systems for FSS, BSS, PCS, & MSS satellite communications. Advanced antenna system designs for contoured beams, multiple beams, and reconfigurable beams will be presented. Multiple beam antenna (MBA) concepts and their advantages compared to conventional contoured beam payloads will be introduced. Next generation satellite systems for navigational and high frequency payloads require advanced antenna systems to meet the demanding requirements in terms of generating plurality of beams from a single antenna, on-orbit beam re-configurability, multiple band operation, and low-loss antennas. The talk will focus on existing technologies, limitations, advantages of the next generation payloads, RF performance and hardware implementation challenges. A dual-band antenna working at very high frequencies for future payloads capable of a ten-fold increase in satellite capacity will be discussed. Recent advances in feed technology and reflector technology will be addressed with few examples. Topics such as antenna designs for high capacity satellites, large deployable mesh reflector designs, low PIM designs, and power handling issues will be included. Advanced test methods for high power TVAC test of satellite payloads using “pick-up horn absorber loads” will be presented. Future trends in the satellite communications including use of higher frequency bands and navigational payloads will be discussed. At the end of this talk, engineers will be exposed to typical requirements, designs, hardware, software, and test methods for various satellite antennas.

articleTitle: Assessment of FETI DDM methodologies for the simulation of high gain Ka-band transmit arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper is presenting Finite Element Tearing and Interconnecting (FETI) simulation results of large scale Ka-band lens transmit-arrays obtained on massively parallel clusters. The computation times observed with the FETI method allow us to consider using it in the optimization phase of such transmit-arrays.

articleTitle: Multi-beam design method for reflectarray antenna using aberration theory
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Aberration theory has been proposed to estimate the frequency characteristics of a reflectarray antenna. In this paper, a multi-beam design of a reflectarray antenna by using first-order aberration is proposed. The validity of the design method is then quantitatively verified through simulations.

articleTitle: Design of implantable on-chip antenna for bio-telemetry applications at ISM 2.45 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Implantable medical device (IMD) with on-chip antenna (OCA) has got an increasing attention for the biotelemetry applications to monitors the patient's health condition by transmitting the sensed bio-signal to the monitoring device outside the body. This paper presents a novel OCA designed by using standard 0.18um CMOS technology to operate at ISM 2.45 GHz. Using two oxide layers namely, Silicon dye oxide (SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) above the Si substrate and Hafnium oxide (HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) on the SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layer, a meander line Microstrip patch antenna with Al is embedded on the top of the HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layer. Above the patch, Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> layer is embedded to make it biocompatible. The proposed compact OCA of dimensions 3 × 3.45 × 0.3922 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> is useful for such applications as it provides a good return loss of 47.62 dB with an acceptable gain of -14dB as simulated under the human body environment using Ansys HFSS EM simulation tools. The effectiveness of the proposed OCA is presented by comparing the results of reported articles.

articleTitle: Design of RFID tag with electromagnetic band gap applying for metalic objects
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of radio-frequency identification tags to reduce the effect of material. The proposed tag consists of planar inverted-F type antenna with electromagnetic band gap (EBG) and the micro-chip UCODE I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>C at frequency of 923 MHz. The antenna is designed to be small by using technical bending and controlling the EBG reflection phase that placed on material objects. From the results of the testing tag, the tag can be placed close to EBG reflection plane, tag is also located on EBG applying to insulation of the antenna, and the distance between antenna and EBG is 2.7 mm. The tag can be used on material objects and have higher gain of 4.77 dBi with the read range of 2.55 m.

articleTitle: Slot antenna array unit cell directly fed by inverted microstrip gap waveguide
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Inverted microstrip gap waveguide is mechanically flexible millimeter wave transmission line. This paper describes a single-layer slot antenna array unit cell at 60-GHz designed by using this inverted microstrip gap waveguide technology. This antenna unit mainly consists of a 2×2 slot layer and corporate-feed networks. The unit-cell shows more than 14.6% bandwidth over 57-66 GHz band with 10-dB return loss. Infinite array environment has been utilized later to determine overall efficiency for bigger 16×16 antenna array which is around 70% with a directivity value of 33.5 dBi between 57-66 GHz.

articleTitle: Multi-frequency printed microwave absorber with adjacent absorption peaks by dual-layer technique
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A multi-frequency printed microwave absorber with very close absorption peaks is designed using a dual-layer technique. The absorption ranges are applicable in the lower WiMAX bands with the adjacent bands (i.e. 2.3/2.7GHz), and also covering almost all U-NII-1/2/3 bands. The absorber consists of two layers with simple rectangular copper patterns, which can improve the modeling and manufacturing accuracy. The design processes are based on numerical simulations. The results show three absorption bands with bandwidths (at 50%) of 140MHz (2.27-2.41GHz), 130MHz (2.68-2.81GHz) and 740MHz (5.025.76GHz). The absorption peaks in each band (i.e. at 2.35, 2.75 and 5.45GHz) are at 98.7%, 85.0% and 99.5%, respectively. The presented absorber exhibits fairly wide-angle characteristics of wave incidence. The advantages of the proposed absorber are thin, simple and low-cost with adjacent absorption peaks, which is suitable for various applications in the lower-band WiMAX and the U-NII frequency ranges, simultaneously.

articleTitle: Ultra-compact Microstrip UWB bandpass filter with improved performance
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-compact Ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter (BPF) based on modified multimode resonator (MMR) is proposed. The compactness of the proposed UWB BPF with good impedance matching in passband is achieved using modified MMR, which consists of meandered coupled lines, stepped-impedance stubs, open-circuited stubs and coupled-line sections. Stepped-impedance stubs which are used to nullify the effect of mutual coupling due to the presence of meandered coupled lines are analyzed in detail. The proposed filter is fabricated using Roger RT/duroid 5880 substrate (ϵ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 2.2, thickness = 0.787 mm) having size of 14 mm × 5.9 mm. The experimental results show that the proposed filter has passband frequency range 3.05-10.9 GHz with upper wide stopband attenuation better than 38 dB up to 15.5 GHz. The simulation results are nearly in agreement with corresponding experimental results.

articleTitle: A high gain Fabry-Perot cavity antenna with a double-layered partially reflecting frequency selective surface structure
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presented the design of a Fabry-Perot cavity antenna with a double-layered partially reflecting frequency selective surface (FSS) to enhance the gain and reduce the antenna height. The FSS structure placed on both sides of substrates is used to simplify the feeding structure and reduce the antenna dimensions. The performance of the proposed antenna was verified by CST microwave studio and the simulation results showed that the maximum gain of the antenna reaches 12.5dB at 5GHz and that the gain was 6dB compared with the patch antenna without superstrate. The total height of the antenna is less than λ/9. The proposed antenna was proved to have the high gain with miniature structures.

articleTitle: Graphene reflectarray that steers vortex THz waves
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A graphene reflectarray is designed to realize two functions simultaneously at terahertz frequency: generating vortex waves, and steering the waves. Four parts of graphene patches with different values of reflection phase are used to generate vortex waves. On the other hand, generalized Snell's Law is applied to introduce additional reflection phase. Anomalous reflection is realized to steer the Vortex wave by 30 degrees.

articleTitle: Heuristic UTD corner and slope diffractions for antenna problem
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a heuristic UTD corner diffraction for an antenna problem. The proposed heuristic UTD corner diffraction coefficient and slope diffraction are developed from the original UTD solution. This proposed solution can deal with a finite size perfect electric conductor (PEC) configuration including edges and corners for any antenna problem. A half wavelength dipole above a square PEC patch is used to be a case study in the paper. It is found that the numerical result from the proposed UTD agrees well with the simulation result from CST computer software. However, there are some discrepancies discontinuity at 90 degrees. It is in progress work to fix this problem.

articleTitle: An improved current reconstruction technique for internal field assessment of dielectric phantoms
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this research, an inverse source reconstruction method is proposed for internal field evaluation of dielectric phantoms. We aims at the cost reduction and accuracy improvement of dosimetric measurement including specific absorption rate (SAR) assessment. The current reconstruction employs the continuity condition at the boundary of dielectric surface to improve the reconstruction accuracy. It is shown that this method works for internal field evaluation of a lossy dielectric sphere by numerical test.

articleTitle: Broadband linear to circular polarization reflector using modified metasurface
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A broadband linear to circular polarization reflector is proposed. To suppress the radiation from surface wave (SW), four corners of the square metasurface (MS) reflector is removed. By this modification, the 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 27% can be obtained at the center frequency of 8.8 GHz. In this paper, the detail discussion about the principle of SW resonance suppression and the guideline to design finite metasurface are presented.

articleTitle: A closely located dual-band FSS with frequency stability for multi-frequency communication
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel angular independent dual-band FSS for multi-frequency communication is discussed in this letter. The proposed FSS with closely spaced response is consist of improved cross-shaped metal strips and a dielectric substrate. The unit cell size of the proposed FSS is 0.13λ×0.13λ where λ corresponds to the wavelength of the first resonant frequency. The proposed FSS exhibits dual stop band characteristics at 2.5 GHz and 3.5 GHz providing -15 dB bandwidth of 298 MHz and 290 MHz. Both bands are closely spaced providing the frequency ratio of f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sub>(upper resonant frequency value) to f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub>(lower resonant frequency value) of 1.40. It also exhibits angular stability up to 60° for both TE mode and TM mode because of its symmetry.

articleTitle: Communication system development of the pioneer Thai CubeSat project: KNACKSAT
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Development of a 1-U CubeSat communication system is presented in this paper. GMSK modulated data from the satellite is transmitted to the ground station via a UHF channel. The uplink of the FSK modulated command from ground to the satellite is carried out via a VHF channel. As Tx and Rx antennas aboard KNACKSAT-the CubeSat to be created in this project, half wavelength dipoles were chosen. The developed communication system have successfully been tested with data communication between the satellite and the ground station.

articleTitle: Feasible calibration of DOD-based BLE beacon for indoor localization application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the authors proposes a easy calibration of DOD-based BLE beacon system for an indoor localization application. By the proposed calibration method, we can easily recognize the orientation and location of the beacon even though the beacons are roughly installed. The method uses DOD calculated from RSSI of received beacon signals and sensor information of the mobile handset for calibration. The experimental results showed the median angular error of the estimated beacon orientation was 2.8~3.9°. Also, the median distance error of the estimated beacon location was 0.69~0.72 m.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling reduction for 5 GHz PIFAs in MIMO terminal
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, two planar inverted-F antennas on a slitted ground plane is proposed for MIMO mobile terminal. This antenna is designed to operate at 5 GHz with 1 GHz bandwidth. In simulation stage, the length and width of slitted are varied. The optimum slit's dimension is shown to be λ/4 length and 0.0333λ width, which produced reflection coefficient of -16.38 dB and isolation of -23.52 dB at 5 GHz, while maintaining 1 GHz bandwidth. It is found that the slitted ground plane has resulted a better isolation of 7.2 dB compared to the full ground plane. Simulated and measured results indicate a satisfactory agreement.

articleTitle: Feasibility on multiplexing antenna system based on rectangular-coordinate orthogonality by using two-dimensional 180-degree hybrid
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For mode multiplexing transmission using two-dimensional orthogonal field distribution, a beam switching circuit is designed and transmission between Tx and Rx antenna systems are calculated. Generation of orthogonal four modes by the beam switching circuit is presented in this paper. The simulated isolations between the orthogonal modes are over 20 dB at the center frequency.
